Even if an operator manually retargets the COPY at the Docker Hub image, the source path `/agent-vault` does not exist there — `Dockerfile:35` and `Dockerfile.goreleaser:8` install the binary at `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`. The canonical recipe for the PR's flagship feature therefore fails at build time before the agent-mode codepath this PR adds is ever exercised. Same broken Dockerfile is duplicated into `cmd/skill_cli.md:66` and `cmd/skill_http.md:71`, which are loaded into Claude Code/Cursor skill registries — so any agent reading those will instruct downstream users to copy a recipe that cannot build.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is broken

The new `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx` — the canonical operator-facing recipe for the PR's headline feature — instructs users to copy the `agent-vault` binary out of `ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault:latest`:

```dockerfile
COPY --from=ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault:latest /agent-vault /usr/local/bin/
```

This Dockerfile is doubly broken: the image referenced is unpublished, and even substituting the published Docker Hub image would fail because the source path is wrong. Same recipe is embedded verbatim at `cmd/skill_cli.md:66` and `cmd/skill_http.md:71`, which ship as Claude Code / Cursor skill files and so propagate the broken recipe to any downstream agent reading them.

## Why

**The image is not published.** The PR description explicitly lists `published ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault binary distribution` under "Out of scope (deferred per the design discussion)". A repo-wide grep for `ghcr.io` returns matches only in the three files this PR adds/touches — `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:24`, `cmd/skill_cli.md:66`, and `cmd/skill_http.md:71`. There is no GHCR push target in `.goreleaser.yml` and no `docker/login-action` for `ghcr.io` in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The release pipeline only authenticates against Docker Hub (via `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` / `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`) and only publishes `infisical/agent-vault:{Version}` and `:latest` (`.goreleaser.yml` lines 86–113). So `docker pull ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault:latest` returns `manifest unknown` and the COPY fails before the build can proceed.

**Even retargeting to Docker Hub does not save the recipe.** The published image is built from `Dockerfile` / `Dockerfile.goreleaser`. `Dockerfile:35` is `COPY --from=builder /agent-vault /usr/local/bin/agent-vault`, and `Dockerfile.goreleaser:8` is `COPY agent-vault /usr/local/bin/agent-vault`. So in the published image the binary lives at `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`, not at `/agent-vault`. A user who edits the doc to use `infisical/agent-vault:latest` (Docker Hub) will see `failed to compute cache key: "/agent-vault" not found`.

## Step-by-step proof

Follow the deploy guide verbatim:

```bash
# Save the snippet from docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx as Dockerfile, then:
docker build -t my-prod-agent .
```

1. Builder runs `COPY --from=ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault:latest /agent-vault /usr/local/bin/`.
2. Docker daemon attempts to pull `ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault:latest`. Registry returns `manifest unknown` / 404. Build fails.
3. Operator improvises — edits to `COPY --from=infisical/agent-vault:latest /agent-vault /usr/local/bin/`. Pull succeeds.
4. COPY now fails with `failed to compute cache key: "/agent-vault" not found`, because the published image installs the binary at `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`.

The operator never reaches the agent-mode codepath this PR adds — `agent-vault run` with `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` / `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` / `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` is gated on a build step that cannot complete.

## Impact

The headline framing of this PR is "agent mode for unattended/containerized deploys", and `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx` is the only operator-facing deploy recipe shipped with that feature. Step 1 of the operator path (`docker build`) fails. Distinct from the already-flagged hallucinated `agent create / agent token` subcommand bug (different fix surface — image registry vs CLI subcommand); even an operator who works around the hallucinated subcommand by using `agent-vault agent invite` will hit this Docker build failure on the very next step. The same broken recipe is also embedded in the two skill files that load into Claude Code / Cursor skill registries, compounding the impact across every downstream agent that reads them.

## Suggested fix

Any one of the following:

1. **Switch to a build-from-source recipe** (zero-dependency on a published image):

   ```dockerfile
   FROM golang:1.25 AS builder
   RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Infisical/agent-vault.git /src \
       && cd /src && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /agent-vault .
   FROM node:20-slim
   COPY --from=builder /agent-vault /usr/local/bin/
   ...
   ```

2. **Fix the image reference and source path** to use the actually-published Docker Hub image:

   ```dockerfile

   ```

3. **Ship the GHCR image distribution as part of this PR** (add a `ghcr.io/infisical/agent-vault` push target to `.goreleaser.yml` and a `docker/login-action@v3` step authenticating to `ghcr.io` in `.github/workflows/release.yml` using the existing `packages: write` permission), and then fix the source path to `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`.

Whichever route you take, update all three locations (`docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:24`, `cmd/skill_cli.md:66`, `cmd/skill_http.md:71`) — the skill files ship as authoritative tool docs to downstream agents.

</details>

🟡 The vault-mismatch error at cmd/helpers.go:585-588 has two minor wording issues. First, the message hardcodes `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=%q` even when the vault came from `--vault` (since `resolveVaultForAgentMode` prioritizes flag over env), so a user who ran `agent-vault run --vault prod` with no env var set sees an error referencing a variable they never set. Second, the suggested remediation "drop AGENT_VAULT_VAULT" is incomplete — `resolveVaultForAgentMode` requires *either* `--vault` or `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT`, so dropping the env var alone produces "vault is required in agent mode". Suggested rewording: "set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) to %q, or use a token for %q".

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

The error message constructed at cmd/helpers.go:585-588 reads:

```go
return fmt.Errorf("vault mismatch: AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=%q but the supplied token is scoped to vault %q — drop AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or use a token for %q",
    vault, dr.Vault, vault)
```

The `vault` parameter passed into `validateEnvToken` is whatever `resolveVaultForAgentMode` (cmd/run.go:289-296) returned — which prioritizes the `--vault` flag over `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT`:

```go
func resolveVaultForAgentMode(cmd *cobra.Command) (string, error) {
    if name, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("vault"); name != "" {
        return name, nil
    }
    if v := os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_VAULT"); v != "" {
        return v, nil
    }
    return "", fmt.Errorf("vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault")
}
```

So the value embedded in the error message can come from either source, but the message hardcodes `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=%q` and tells the user to "drop AGENT_VAULT_VAULT" — both of which are wrong when the value originated from the flag.

## Why the existing code does not prevent it

The error string is a static format embedded in the only place that branches on a mismatch. The function does not know (and is not told by the caller) whether the value originated from the flag or the env var, so it cannot phrase the remediation correctly today.

## Step-by-step proof

```bash
# Shell has no AGENT_VAULT_VAULT set.
unset AGENT_VAULT_VAULT
export AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_sess_for_staging   # session token scoped to "staging"
export AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://broker.example

agent-vault run --vault prod -- some-agent
```

1. `resolveVaultForAgentMode` returns `"prod"` (from `--vault`).
2. `validateEnvToken(addr, token, "prod")` calls `/discover`; the broker echoes `{"vault":"staging"}` (the session's baked-in vault).
3. The mismatch branch fires and emits:
   `vault mismatch: AGENT_VAULT_VAULT="prod" but the supplied token is scoped to vault "staging" — drop AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or use a token for "prod"`.

The user sees `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT="prod"` in the error even though they never set that env var. If they then `unset AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` (which is already unset) and re-run, the only behavior change comes from removing `--vault prod` — which then trips `resolveVaultForAgentMode`'s own "vault is required in agent mode" error rather than letting the run succeed against the staging vault. The remediation as worded does not lead to a working invocation.

## Impact

User-facing: low. The vault names appear in the message, so an operator who reads carefully can still figure out the underlying problem. But the wording is genuinely misleading — it both misnames the source of the configured vault and misdirects the fix. All four verifiers independently confirmed this and classified it nit, matching the submitter's own self-classification.

## Suggested fix

Change the format string to name both surfaces and drop the imperative "drop" advice. For example:

```go
return fmt.Errorf("vault mismatch: requested vault %q does not match the supplied token's vault %q — set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) to %q, or use a token for %q",
    vault, dr.Vault, dr.Vault, vault)
```

This stays accurate regardless of whether the requested vault came from the flag or the env var, and the remediations both lead to a working invocation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

`resolveSession` at cmd/helpers.go:512–528 reads `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` first, falls back to the deprecated `AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN` (emitting a one-time stderr warning), and then runs the missing-addr check:

```go
token := os.Getenv(envVarToken)              // "AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN"
if token == "" {
    if legacy := os.Getenv(envVarTokenLegacy); legacy != "" {  // "AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN"
        legacyTokenWarnOnce.Do(func() {
            fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s %s is deprecated; use %s instead.\n",
                mutedText("agent-vault:"), envVarTokenLegacy, envVarToken)
        })
        token = legacy
    }

So a user who exported only the legacy alias sees an error referencing a variable they never set.

```bash
unset AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN AGENT_VAULT_ADDR
export AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN=tok
agent-vault run -- foo
```

1. `os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN")` → `""`.
2. Fallback path: `os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN")` → `"tok"`. The warn-once `Do` fires:
   `agent-vault: AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN is deprecated; use AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN instead.`
   `token = "tok"`.
3. `os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_ADDR")` → `""`.
4. `token != "" && addr == ""` → enters the error branch. Format substitutes `envVarToken = "AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN"`:

The format string is static and references the canonical-name constant. The function does not track which env var actually supplied the token, so the error wording cannot reflect the real source today. The same wording-source family is acknowledged in the sibling vault-mismatch error (which was reworded to name both surfaces in 13dcff1) — this branch is the symmetric case that did not get the same treatment.

## Impact

User-facing: low. The deprecation warning printed one line earlier does carry the correct variable name, so an attentive operator can still piece together the actual misconfig. Track which env var supplied the token and reference it in the error, or just list both names. Two minimal options:

tokenSrc := envVarToken
token := os.Getenv(envVarToken)

🟡 The Prerequisites bullet at docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:11 tells operators they can "revoke the token from the Tokens tab in the UI at any time", but this guide is about long-lived **agent** tokens — and the per-vault Tokens tab (web/src/pages/vault/TokensTab.tsx → `GET /v1/sessions?vault=`) only surfaces vault-scoped session tokens. `ListScopedSessionsByVault` and `RevokeScopedSession` both filter `AND agent_id IS NULL` in SQL (internal/store/sqlite.go:850, :901), so an agent token is invisible and unrevokable from that tab. An operator who follows this runbook to revoke a compromised agent token will see "No tokens yet" and have no recourse from the indicated surface — point at the **Agents** tab and/or `agent-vault agent rotate` / `agent-vault agent delete` instead (the rotation paragraph later in this same file already does this correctly).

## What is broken

The Prerequisites bullet at `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:11` reads:

> A long-lived agent token with access to the target vault. … Operators can revoke the token from the **Tokens** tab in the UI at any time.

For the long-lived agent tokens this guide centers on, that revoke instruction sends the operator to the wrong surface.

## Why the Tokens tab cannot revoke agent tokens

The per-vault Tokens tab (`web/src/pages/vault/TokensTab.tsx`) calls `GET /v1/sessions?vault=<name>`, which routes to `handleListScopedSessions` in `internal/server/handle_sessions.go`. That handler delegates to `ListScopedSessionsByVault` in `internal/store/sqlite.go:845`, whose SQL is roughly:

```sql
WHERE vault_id = ? AND public_id IS NOT NULL
  AND user_id IS NULL AND agent_id IS NULL
```

The `AND agent_id IS NULL` clause excludes any session row tied to an agent identity by design. `RevokeScopedSession` applies the same filter at `sqlite.go:901`, so even if an operator already knew a session's `public_id` they could not delete an agent-owned session via `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}`. The Tokens tab is wired exclusively to vault-scoped session tokens (`av_sess_*`).

Long-lived agent tokens (`av_agent_token_*`) live on the agent identity itself, not on a vault row. They are managed through:

- The **Agents** tab in the web UI (`web/src/pages/instance/AgentsTab.tsx`), which calls `/v1/admin/agents` and `DELETE /v1/admin/agents/<name>`.
- `agent-vault agent delete <name>` and `agent-vault agent rotate <name>` (`cmd/agent.go:386–387`). `rotate` issues a fresh rotation invite which invalidates old tokens on redeem.

## Step-by-step proof

1. An operator follows the new container-deploy guide; their production agent token leaks.
2. They land on Prerequisites, which tells them: "Operators can revoke the token from the **Tokens** tab in the UI at any time."
3. They open the vault → Tokens tab. The tab issues `GET /v1/sessions?vault=production`. The handler returns only rows with `agent_id IS NULL`, so the agent's token does not appear.
4. The tab renders "No tokens yet" — the empty-state copy in `TokensTab.tsx`. The operator concludes (incorrectly) that the token cannot be revoked from the UI.
5. The token can in fact be revoked, but only via the Agents tab or `agent-vault agent delete` / `agent-vault agent rotate` — which the doc does not name at this step.

## Why this matters

This is a security-sensitive runbook line — "how do I revoke a leaked production credential." Even though the token is still revocable through other surfaces (and the rotation paragraph later in the same file correctly points at `/agents/overview#rotating-an-agent-token`), the Prerequisites step misdirects the operator at the moment the docs matter most. The internal inconsistency (this paragraph says Tokens tab; the rotation paragraph below says Agents) makes the Prerequisites line clearly the broken half.

## Suggested fix

One-line wording change. Something like:

> Operators can revoke the token at any time from the **Agents** tab in the UI, or via `agent-vault agent rotate <name>` / `agent-vault agent delete <name>` from the CLI.

Severity: **nit** — doc-only, single sentence, no functional impact, and the operator does have working alternative paths. Worth fixing before merge because the wrong surface is the one called out in a security-sensitive runbook step.

</details>

🟡 The new skill files at `cmd/skill_cli.md:81` and `cmd/skill_http.md:86` link to `https://docs.infisical.com/agents/overview`, but the project's docs are hosted at `docs.agent-vault.dev` (every other docs URL across the repo — README, Navbar, vault UI tabs, the Mintlify tree — uses that domain). Since these skill files ship as Claude Code / Cursor skill registry entries (also auto-installed by `maybeInstallSkills` in `cmd/run.go`), the wrong URL propagates to every downstream agent. Fix: change both occurrences to `https://docs.agent-vault.dev/agents/overview`.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is broken

`cmd/skill_cli.md:81` and `cmd/skill_http.md:86` both link to `[Agents](https://docs.infisical.com/agents/overview)` when describing how operators mint long-lived agent tokens for the new agent-mode flow. The Agent Vault project documentation lives at `docs.agent-vault.dev`, not `docs.infisical.com`.

## Why this is wrong

Every other doc URL across the repo points at `docs.agent-vault.dev` — `README.md` (lines 17, 37, 48, 99, 101, 175), `web/src/components/Navbar.tsx:28`, `web/src/pages/vault/UsersTab.tsx:307`, `web/src/pages/vault/ProposalsTab.tsx:172`, and the entire `docs/` Mintlify tree itself. The canonical `/agents/overview` page is `docs/agents/overview.mdx` in *this* repo, which Mintlify renders at `docs.agent-vault.dev/agents/overview`. `docs.infisical.com` is the parent Infisical Secrets product's docs site and has no Agent Vault `/agents/overview` route.

## Why existing code does not catch this

A repo-wide grep confirms `docs.infisical.com` is referenced in exactly four files — all from this PR's new skill content (and a couple of derived locations) — while every other docs link uses `docs.agent-vault.dev`. There is no automated link-checker in CI to flag the mismatch, and the skill-file install path (`maybeInstallSkills` at `cmd/run.go:247`) writes the file verbatim into `~/.claude/skills/agent-vault-*/SKILL.md` and `~/.cursor/skills/...` without rewriting URLs.

## Impact

These two files ship as Claude Code / Cursor skill registry entries. Every downstream agent that reads them will direct its end users to a URL that either 404s or surfaces unrelated Infisical Secrets docs. The blast radius is amplified because `maybeInstallSkills` auto-installs them onto every developer machine that runs `agent-vault run` against a known agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Hermes, OpenCode), so a stale link gets baked into many local skill registries.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Operator runs `agent-vault run -- claude` for the first time.
2. `maybeInstallSkills("Claude Code", ".claude")` writes the embedded `skill_cli.md` to `~/.claude/skills/agent-vault-cli/SKILL.md`.
3. Claude Code loads the skill. When the user later asks how to deploy in a container, the skill instructs them to follow `[Agents](https://docs.infisical.com/agents/overview)`.
4. The user clicks the link → `docs.infisical.com` returns no Agent Vault content; the user is misled or stuck. Meanwhile the actual canonical page (`docs/agents/overview.mdx`) is sitting at `docs.agent-vault.dev/agents/overview`.

## Fix

One-character substitution at both locations:

```diff
- (see [Agents](https://docs.infisical.com/agents/overview))
+ (see [Agents](https://docs.agent-vault.dev/agents/overview))
```

Apply at `cmd/skill_cli.md:81` and `cmd/skill_http.md:86`.

</details>

🟡 The X-Vault scope at `docs/agents/overview.mdx:144` still says "This applies to all vault-scoped requests: `/discover`, `/v1/proposals`, and `/v1/credentials`" — but this PR narrows the same wording in `protocol.mdx:37` ("on /discover and /v1/proposals requests") and `AGENTS.md:24` ("on all control-plane requests (/discover, /v1/proposals)") to match what the broker actually enforces. After merge, the three closely-related agent docs disagree on the X-Vault contract, and overview.mdx contradicts the broker behavior the other two now correctly describe. Worth a one-line fix in the same change since the PR already touches this exact section (line 140 inside the example block) and is the change that introduces the disagreement.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What's wrong

This PR explicitly narrows the documented X-Vault scope in two of three closely-related agent-facing docs:

- `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:37` — was "on all vault-scoped requests (discover, proposals, credentials)", now reads "on /discover and /v1/proposals requests"
- `AGENTS.md:24` — was "(discover, proxy, proposals)", now reads "(/discover, /v1/proposals)"

But `docs/agents/overview.mdx:144` still reads:

> This applies to all vault-scoped requests: `/discover`, `/v1/proposals`, and `/v1/credentials`.

The PR diff for overview.mdx only modifies line 140 inside the same X-Vault example block (the `AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN` → `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` rename). Line 144 — one line below the modified line, in the same paragraph — was missed. After this PR is merged, the three agent docs that ship in the same change disagree about which endpoints honor X-Vault.

## Why the narrowing is correct (and overview.mdx is now demonstrably wrong)

`/v1/credentials` does not consult the X-Vault header. `internal/server/handle_credentials.go:85` (`handleCredentialsList`) reads `vault := r.URL.Query().Get("vault")`, and `handleCredentialsSet:29` reads `req.Vault` from the JSON body. The only X-Vault enforcement point is `resolveVaultForSession` in `internal/server/vault_resolve.go:31`, which is called only from `handle_discovery.go` and `handle_proposals.go` (verified by repo-wide grep — `resolveVaultForSession` has exactly three references: its definition and the two callers). So the broker has never enforced X-Vault on `/v1/credentials`, and the new protocol.mdx / AGENTS.md wording matches reality. overview.mdx now claims agents must include X-Vault on a request the broker never reads it from.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Read `docs/agents/overview.mdx` line 144 in the working tree (post-PR): the sentence still names `/v1/credentials`.
2. Read `docs/agents/protocol.mdx` line 37 in the working tree (post-PR): the sentence names only `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`.
3. Read `AGENTS.md` line 24 in the working tree (post-PR): the sentence names only `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`.
4. Grep `resolveVaultForSession` across `internal/server`: matches in `vault_resolve.go`, `handle_discovery.go`, `handle_proposals.go`. No call from `handle_credentials.go`.
5. Confirm in `handle_credentials.go` that `handleCredentialsList` (line 84) reads `vault` from the URL query and `handleCredentialsSet` (line 23) reads `req.Vault` from the JSON body — neither consults the request headers.

## Impact

User-facing damage is mild: an attentive operator cross-checking the three pages catches the conflict. An inattentive operator who hits a 4xx on `/v1/credentials` may attribute it to a missing X-Vault header rather than a missing `?vault=` query / JSON `vault` field, costing them debugging time. The broker error message names the actual cause, so it's not user-blocking.

The reason this is worth fixing in the same change rather than punting to a follow-up is that pre-PR all three docs agreed (even if all three were technically over-broad about `/v1/credentials`), and the PR is what *introduces* the disagreement. Fixing it after merge would mean shipping a release with internally inconsistent docs.

## Suggested fix

Replace the sentence at `docs/agents/overview.mdx:144` with wording matching the sibling pages, e.g.:

```
This applies to `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`. (Endpoints like `/v1/credentials` resolve the vault from a `?vault=` query parameter or request body instead.)
```

One-line edit in a section the PR already touches one line above.

</details>

🟡 Two more error messages still hardcode `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` (via the `envVarToken` constant) even when the user supplied only the deprecated `AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN` alias: the `--ttl` rejection at cmd/run.go:143 and the broker-401/403 branch in `validateEnvToken` at cmd/helpers.go:572. Same wording-inconsistency family as the missing-addr nit already accepted in PR feedback (cmd/helpers.go:528) — `resolveSession` tracks `tokenSource` internally but doesn't propagate it, so these two downstream callsites can only reference the canonical-name constant. Pure nit (no functional impact, deprecation warning one line earlier carries the right name); worth threading the source through (or just listing both names) at all three locations to fully clean up the symmetric class.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

Two error paths in the new agent-mode flow embed `envVarToken` (the constant `"AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN"` declared at cmd/helpers.go:498) even on the legacy-fallback path where the user only set `AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN`:

1. **cmd/run.go:143** — agent-mode `--ttl` rejection:
   ```go
   return fmt.Errorf("--ttl has no effect when %s is supplied; the token's lifetime is fixed at mint time", envVarToken)
   ```

2. **cmd/helpers.go:572** — broker-401/403 branch in `validateEnvToken`:
   ```go
   return fmt.Errorf("agent token rejected by broker (HTTP %d) — verify %s is current and has access to vault %q", resp.StatusCode, envVarToken, vault)
   ```

## Why the existing code does not prevent it

`resolveSession` (cmd/helpers.go:512–530) tracks `tokenSource` locally — it knows whether the value came from `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` or the legacy alias — but the bool is consumed only inside that function (for the missing-addr error). `runCmdRunE` at cmd/run.go and `validateEnvToken` at cmd/helpers.go:572 receive only `*session.ClientSession`, which carries the value but not the source name. So both downstream sites default to the canonical-name constant.

This is the symmetric case of the missing-addr nit reworded earlier in the review — `resolveSession` was updated to use `tokenSource` for its own error string, but the fix was not extended to these two callers.

## Step-by-step proof (--ttl path)

```bash
unset AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN
export AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN=tok
export AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://broker
agent-vault run --ttl 3600 -- foo
```

1. `os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN")` → `""`.
2. Legacy fallback fires: `os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN")` → `"tok"`. Warn-once emits to stderr:
   `agent-vault: AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN is deprecated; use AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN instead.`
3. `resolveSession` returns `(sess, fromEnv=true, nil)`.
4. `runCmdRunE` enters the `fromEnv` branch; `cmd.Flags().Changed("ttl")` is true.
5. Error emitted: `--ttl has no effect when AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN is supplied; the token's lifetime is fixed at mint time`.

The user gets two consecutive stderr lines naming two different env vars for the same value — line 1 says `SESSION_TOKEN`, line 2 says `TOKEN`. Same shape on the broker-rejection path: a 401 from `/discover` produces `agent token rejected by broker (HTTP 401) — verify AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN is current ...`, again misnaming the variable the user actually set.

## Impact

User-facing: low. The error still names the right vault on the broker path, the deprecation warning printed earlier carries the correct name, and the canonical name *is* the correct remediation target since the legacy alias is deprecated. But the wording is genuinely misleading and inconsistent with the parallel rewording the vault-mismatch error received in 13dcff1.

## Suggested fix

Thread the source through (or just list both names). Either propagate `tokenSource` from `resolveSession` to both callsites, or use the simpler one-liner that mirrors the bug #6 rewording:

```go
// cmd/run.go:143
return fmt.Errorf("--ttl has no effect when %s/%s is supplied; ...", envVarToken, envVarTokenLegacy)

// cmd/helpers.go:572
return fmt.Errorf("agent token rejected by broker (HTTP %d) — verify %s/%s is current and has access to vault %q", resp.StatusCode, envVarToken, envVarTokenLegacy, vault)
```

Nit severity matches the submitter's self-classification and all three verifier confirmations.

</details>

🟡 After this PR threads X-Vault through to discover/proposal create, an env-mode user with only `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN`+`AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` set (the canonical container-deploy recipe this PR documents) will silently send `X-Vault: default` because `cmd/discover.go:32` and `cmd/proposal_create.go:78` call `resolveVault(cmd)`, whose tail returns `store.DefaultVault` when nothing is configured — instead of the clean "vault is required in agent mode" error `cmd/run.go:140-156` already produces via `resolveVaultForAgentMode`. This is the same agent-mode contract the PR establishes for `run` (and the same UX-consistency family as the missing-addr error already accepted in earlier review feedback) — it should extend symmetrically to peer commands. The fix is small: branch on the `tokenSource` second return of `resolveSession()` (currently discarded with `_` at `cmd/discover.go:21` and `cmd/proposal_create.go:44`) and call `resolveVaultForAgentMode` when env-mode; same change should add `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` to the `discover` Long help (cmd/discover.go:14-18) and the matching section in docs/reference/cli.mdx, parallel to cmd/run.go:42-52.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is broken

This PR's headline change for `discover` and `proposal create` is the X-Vault thread-through (`doVaultScopedRequestWithBody(..., resolveVault(cmd), ...)` at `cmd/discover.go:32` and `cmd/proposal_create.go:78`), enabling instance-level agent tokens on these subcommands. The thread-through itself is correct, but the vault resolver it pipes through is the human-mode `resolveVault`, not the agent-mode `resolveVaultForAgentMode` that `cmd/run.go:140-156` already established as the agent-mode contract. The two resolvers diverge precisely on the failure path that matters here:

```go
// cmd/helpers.go:478-493 — used by discover/proposal create
func resolveVault(cmd *cobra.Command) string {
    if name, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("vault"); name != "" { return name }
    if v := os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_VAULT"); v != "" { return v }
    if pv := loadProjectVault(); pv != "" { return pv }
    if ctx := session.LoadVaultContext(); ctx != "" { return ctx }
    return store.DefaultVault   // ← silently returns "default"
}

// cmd/run.go:289-296 — used by run in agent mode
func resolveVaultForAgentMode(cmd *cobra.Command) (string, error) {
    if name, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("vault"); name != "" { return name, nil }
    if v := os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_VAULT"); v != "" { return v, nil }
    return "", fmt.Errorf("vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault")
}
```

When an operator follows the new container-deploy recipe with `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` + `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` set but no `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` and no `--vault` flag, `resolveVault` falls all the way through to `store.DefaultVault` ("default") and that string is sent on the wire as `X-Vault: default`.

## Why the existing code does not prevent it

`cmd/discover.go:21` and `cmd/proposal_create.go:44` both discard `resolveSession`'s second return value (`tokenSource`) with `_`:

```go
sess, _, err := resolveSession()
```

That's exactly the bool-equivalent the run command branches on (`fromEnv := tokenSource != ""` at `cmd/run.go:130`). Without it, these two commands cannot distinguish env-mode from human-mode and so cannot apply the stricter resolver. The `tokenSource` return value was added in this PR specifically so callers could make that branch — but only `runCmdRunE` was updated to use it.

The Long help at `cmd/discover.go:14-18` lists the env-var path as `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN + AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` only, omitting `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT`. `cmd/run.go:42-52` correctly names all three. The same omission appears in `docs/reference/cli.mdx:249` ("Requires a vault-scoped session ... AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN + AGENT_VAULT_ADDR env vars").

## Impact

Two failure modes, in order of severity:

1. **Silent wrong-vault routing** (the genuinely bad case). If the agent token happens to have access to a vault literally named "default", the request silently succeeds against the wrong vault. The agent reads, writes, or proposes against an unintended vault with no diagnostic. This contradicts the agent-mode contract the PR establishes for `run`.

2. **Confusing 4xx instead of clear remediation.** If no "default" vault exists or the agent has no access, the broker (`internal/server/vault_resolve.go:31-49`) returns either `404 "Vault not found: default"` or `403 "Agent does not have access to vault: default"`. The vault name appears in the error so a careful operator can debug it, but the error is misleading because they never specified "default" anywhere — versus the run command's clean `vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault`.

The new skill files (`cmd/skill_cli.md`, `cmd/skill_http.md`) explicitly instruct agents to run `agent-vault vault discover --json` as their first action, so this is the primary surface where a misconfigured deploy first hits the broker.

## Step-by-step proof

Following the deploy recipe in the new `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx`:

```bash
export AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx        # instance-level agent token
export AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
# AGENT_VAULT_VAULT intentionally unset — the operator missed the bullet at
# line 43, since the table at line 34 says it's only "Required for agent tokens"
```

1. `agent-vault vault discover --json`
   - `cmd/discover.go:21` → `resolveSession()` returns `(sess, "AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN", nil)`. The `tokenSource` is discarded with `_`.
   - `cmd/discover.go:32` calls `resolveVault(cmd)` → flag empty, env empty, project file absent, vault context absent → `return store.DefaultVault` → `"default"`.
   - `doVaultScopedRequestWithBody("GET", addr+"/discover", token, "default", nil)` sets `X-Vault: default` on the wire.
   - Broker (`vault_resolve.go:31-49`): `sess.AgentID != ""`, X-Vault is "default" → either silently uses a vault named "default" (case 1), or returns `404 Vault not found: default` / `403 Agent does not have access to vault: default` (case 2).
2. By contrast, `agent-vault vault run -- foo` with the same env produces `Error: vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault` *before* any network call.

## Fix

Three small edits, all symmetric to the run command:

1. **cmd/discover.go:21 and cmd/proposal_create.go:44** — capture `tokenSource` and branch:

   ```go
   sess, tokenSource, err := resolveSession()
   if err != nil { return err }
   var vault string
   if tokenSource != "" {
       v, err := resolveVaultForAgentMode(cmd)
       if err != nil { return err }
       vault = v
   } else {
       vault = resolveVault(cmd)
   }
   // ... pass `vault` to doVaultScopedRequestWithBody
   ```

2. **cmd/discover.go:14-18** — extend Long help to mention `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT`, parallel to `cmd/run.go:42-52`.

3. **docs/reference/cli.mdx** — same wording fix in the `agent-vault vault discover` section.

The shape mirrors what `runCmdRunE` already does at `cmd/run.go:130-150`. No new helpers needed; `resolveVaultForAgentMode` is exported within the package and already covers the requirement.

</details>

🟡 Two sentences in this guide still use the broad pre-PR wording 'every vault-scoped request' for X-Vault scope (lines 43 and 56), while this PR narrowed the same concept in three sibling docs to specifically /discover and /v1/proposals — protocol.mdx:37, AGENTS.md:24, and overview.mdx:144. After merge, the four agent-facing docs disagree on the X-Vault contract. Doc-only nit, no functional impact, but worth fixing in lockstep with the round-4 overview.mdx fix already accepted, since this PR is what introduces the disagreement (it modified this file at lines 27, 51, 125, 147, and 180-188 for the AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN→AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN rename and the new container-deploy card).

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is wrong

After the round-4 fix narrowed the X-Vault scope wording in three of four sibling agent docs from "every vault-scoped request" to specifically `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`, `docs/guides/connect-custom-agent.mdx` was missed at two locations:

- **Line 43**: "Instance-level agent tokens require the `X-Vault` header on every vault-scoped request."
- **Line 56**: "For instance-level agent tokens (from agent invites), the agent must also send the `X-Vault` header on every vault-scoped request."

The three sibling docs that ship in this PR with the narrower wording:

- `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:37` — "Instance-level agent tokens must include `X-Vault: {vault_name}` on `/discover` and `/v1/proposals` requests"
- `AGENTS.md:24` — "you must include `X-Vault: {vault_name}` on all control-plane requests (`/discover`, `/v1/proposals`)"
- `docs/agents/overview.mdx:144` (post round-4 fix) — "This applies to `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`."

## Why the narrower wording is correct

The broker only enforces X-Vault on the two endpoints whose handlers route through `resolveVaultForSession` (`internal/server/vault_resolve.go:31-35`). Repo-wide grep confirms that helper has exactly three references: its definition and the two callers — `handle_discovery.go` and `handle_proposals.go`. Other vault-scoped endpoints resolve the vault from elsewhere: `/v1/credentials` reads it from the URL query (`?vault=`) and JSON body, never from the `X-Vault` header.

## Why this matters

This file was modified by this PR — the diff hits lines 27, 51, 125, 147, and 180-188 for the `AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN` → `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` rename and the new "Deploy your agent in a container" card. The rename was applied one line above the line-56 X-Vault sentence, but the X-Vault wording itself was not narrowed in lockstep with the three sibling docs. After merge, four closely-related agent docs disagree about which endpoints honor X-Vault.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Read `docs/guides/connect-custom-agent.mdx:43` (post-PR working tree): contains the literal substring "every vault-scoped request".
2. Read `docs/guides/connect-custom-agent.mdx:56` (post-PR working tree): same substring.
3. Read `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:37` (post-PR): names only `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`.
4. Read `AGENTS.md:24` (post-PR): names only `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`.
5. Read `docs/agents/overview.mdx:144` (post-PR, after round-4 fix): "This applies to `/discover` and `/v1/proposals`."
6. Grep `resolveVaultForSession` in `internal/server`: matches in `vault_resolve.go`, `handle_discovery.go`, `handle_proposals.go` only.
7. `internal/server/handle_credentials.go` reads vault from `r.URL.Query().Get("vault")` and `req.Vault` (request body) — never consults `X-Vault`.

## Impact

User-facing damage is mild: an attentive operator cross-checking the four pages catches the conflict. Sending `X-Vault` on endpoints that ignore it is harmless, so a developer who follows this guide produces working requests. But the inconsistency wastes the readers time and undermines confidence in the docs — particularly because protocol.mdx (the canonical HTTP reference) and this guide give contradictory contracts.

## How to fix

One-line edit at each location, matching the AGENTS.md:24 wording:

- Line 43: "Instance-level agent tokens require the `X-Vault` header on `/discover` and `/v1/proposals` requests."
- Line 56: "For instance-level agent tokens (from agent invites), the agent must also send the `X-Vault` header on `/discover` and `/v1/proposals` requests."

Same shape as the overview.mdx:144 fix already accepted in round 4.

</details>

🟡 The discover Long help (cmd/discover.go:16) and the matching docs/reference/cli.mdx:249 accordion still describe the contract as "a vault-scoped session", but the latest commit (609613d) explicitly threaded X-Vault through to /discover so AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN now also accepts long-lived agent tokens — and every other surface this PR updated names the wider contract correctly. Replace "vault-scoped session" with "vault-scoped session token or long-lived agent token" in both locations to align with cmd/run.go:47, AGENTS.md:17, and docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx:74.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is wrong

This PR widens the documented contract of `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` to accept *either* a vault-scoped session token *or* a long-lived instance-level agent token. The latest commit (609613d) is precisely the one that threads X-Vault through to `discover` (via `doVaultScopedRequestWithBody` at cmd/discover.go:43-44) so instance-level agent tokens actually work on this command. But the help text right above that change still reads:

> Requires a vault-scoped session (e.g. via agent-vault vault run or AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN + AGENT_VAULT_ADDR environment variables; AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN is the deprecated alias and still works).

The phrase "vault-scoped session" is the pre-PR wording — narrower than what the runtime now supports. The same outdated phrasing also appears in `docs/reference/cli.mdx:249`, which is the operator-facing reference accordion for `agent-vault vault discover`.

## Why this is the only place still using the narrow wording

A repo-wide check confirms every other surface this PR touches has been broadened to name both token types:

- `cmd/run.go:47`: `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN  — vault-scoped session token or long-lived agent token`
- `AGENTS.md:17`: `Bearer token for authenticating with Agent Vault. Either a vault-scoped session token or a long-lived agent token.`
- `docs/self-hosting/environment-variables.mdx:74`: `Either a vault-scoped session token or a long-lived agent token.`
- `cmd/skill_cli.md:41` and `cmd/skill_http.md:40`: same wording
- `sdks/sdk-typescript/src/types.ts`: same wording

Only `discover`'s Long help and the discover accordion in `cli.mdx` still use the pre-PR "vault-scoped session" phrasing.

## Why this matters

The new `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx` instructs operators to use a long-lived agent token (`AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx`) and then to run `agent-vault vault discover --json` as the canonical sanity check (this is also what `cmd/skill_cli.md` and `cmd/skill_http.md` instruct agents to do as their very first action). A user reading `agent-vault vault discover --help` or the cli.mdx reference will conclude the command does **not** accept agent tokens, contradicting both the runtime behavior the same commit just shipped and the brand-new container-deploy guide.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Read cmd/discover.go:14-20 in the working tree (post-PR): `Requires a vault-scoped session (e.g. via agent-vault vault run or AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN + AGENT_VAULT_ADDR environment variables; AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN is the deprecated alias and still works).`
2. Read cmd/run.go:42-49 in the working tree: explicitly names "vault-scoped session token or long-lived agent token".
3. Read docs/reference/cli.mdx:249: same narrow "vault-scoped session" wording as discover.go.
4. Read `internal/server/handle_discovery.go` / `internal/server/vault_resolve.go:31-49`: `/discover` accepts X-Vault from instance-level agent tokens; the discover.go change at cmd/discover.go:43-44 (`doVaultScopedRequestWithBody`) is exactly what wires X-Vault through.

So the implementation supports both token types on `/discover`; only the help/reference text underclaims that.

## Impact

Pure doc/help-text. No functional impact — `agent-vault vault discover` works fine when called with a long-lived agent token. Worth fixing in the same PR that introduced the asymmetry, since the PR is what widened the contract on every other surface.

## Suggested fix

Two-line edit:

```diff
- Requires a vault-scoped session (e.g. via agent-vault vault run or
- AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN + AGENT_VAULT_ADDR environment variables;
- AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN is the deprecated alias and still works).
+ Requires a vault-scoped session token or long-lived agent token (e.g. via
+ agent-vault vault run or AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN + AGENT_VAULT_ADDR environment
+ variables; AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN is the deprecated alias and still works).
```

Apply the parallel one-line wording change to docs/reference/cli.mdx:249.

</details>

🟡 The skill file documents `agent-vault vault credential get <key>` (skill_cli.md, "Reading Credentials" section) as the way for agents to read credential values, but `credentialGetCmd` and `credentialListCmd` in cmd/credential.go both call `ensureSession()` exclusively — which requires either an on-disk admin session or an interactive TTY, neither of which exists in the new `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` env-mode container flow this PR adds. An agent in container mode that follows the documented instruction will hit `Error: not logged in, run 'agent-vault auth login' first`. Same gap that was just closed for `discover` and `proposal create` in commit 609613d (resolveSession + resolveVaultForCommand) — extend credential get/list the same way, or qualify the "Reading Credentials" section to note it's admin/dev-mode only and point agents at the HTTP endpoint (which already supports member+ agent tokens).

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is broken

This PR adds a "Containerized agent deployment" section to `cmd/skill_cli.md` (and `cmd/skill_http.md`) at lines 60–81 that tells operators to deploy with `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` + `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` + `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` and skip the interactive `auth login`. Later in the same file, the "Reading Credentials" section (around line 286) documents:

```bash
agent-vault vault credential get <key>
```

…as the way for agents to read a credential's decrypted value ("Useful for configuration tasks where you need to read a stored value"). The two sections are mutually inconsistent: an agent that follows (a) and then (b) will fail.

## Why the existing code does not handle agent mode for credential commands

`cmd/credential.go` was not touched by this PR. `credentialListCmd` at line 24, `credentialGetCmd` at line 79, and `credentialSetCmd` at line 118 all call `ensureSession()` unconditionally. `ensureSession` (cmd/helpers.go) first tries `session.Load()` for an on-disk admin session, then falls back to interactive TTY setup; in a container (`isInteractive() == false`, no `~/.agent-vault/session.json`) it returns the literal error `not logged in, run 'agent-vault auth login' first`. `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` / `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` are never consulted on this path.

By contrast, `cmd/discover.go` and `cmd/proposal_create.go` were extended in this same PR (commit 609613d) to capture `tokenSource` from `resolveSession()` and call `resolveVaultForCommand` so they accept env-mode tokens. The credential commands — which the skill file presents as a peer credential-read path — were not updated.

## Why the broker doesn't block agent tokens here

The HTTP layer already supports agent tokens for credential reads. `handleCredentialsList` in `internal/server/handle_credentials.go:84` reads `vault` from a query string and gates on `requireVaultMember` (line 102), which accepts any session — admin, scoped, or agent — with member+ role. So an agent token with member+ access *can* read credentials over the HTTP API; only the CLI wrapper is gated on admin sessions. This is what makes the asymmetry within this PR particularly visible: discover and proposal-create were brought in line with what the broker already allowed, credential get/list/set were not.

## Step-by-step proof

Following the new container-deploy recipe in `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx` and the skill file's instructions:

```bash
# Inside the container (no on-disk session, no TTY)
export AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
export AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx     # member+ on "production"
export AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production

# Skill file's "Reading Credentials" section says:
agent-vault vault credential get DB_PASSWORD
```

1. `credentialGetCmd.RunE` (cmd/credential.go:78) calls `ensureSession()`.
2. `ensureSession` runs `session.Load()` → returns nil (no session file in the container).
3. `isInteractive()` returns false (no TTY).
4. `ensureSession` returns `fmt.Errorf("not logged in, run 'agent-vault auth login' first")` (cmd/helpers.go).
5. The CLI exits with that error, despite a perfectly valid `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` with member+ role on the target vault sitting in the env.

Same shape for `agent-vault vault credential list` and `agent-vault vault credential set`.

## Impact

Narrow but advertised. Container deploys typically run application code (`npm start`) rather than Claude Code reading a skill file, and `maybeInstallSkills` doesn't auto-install skills into containers. So the failing scenario requires (a) an agent token with member+ role rather than the typical proxy-only invite, (b) the agent reading `skill_cli.md` rather than `skill_http.md` or hitting `/v1/credentials` directly, and (c) running in a no-TTY environment. All three can align — particularly because the same PR's skill file ships as the auto-installed Claude Code / Cursor skill registry entry — but it's not the most common path. Three of four verifiers classified this as nit on those grounds.

The reason it's worth flagging anyway: the author touched this exact `skill_cli.md` block in this PR (env-var rename at line 41, plus the entire new container-deploy section), so the surface is genuinely advertised by the same change that breaks it. And the fix is symmetric to what discover/proposal_create already received — capture `tokenSource` from `resolveSession()`, pass it through `resolveVaultForCommand`, and use `doVaultScopedRequestWithBody` (which already exists in cmd/helpers.go).

## Suggested fix

Two options, in order of recommendation:

1. **Extend `cmd/credential.go` to agent mode**, parallel to `cmd/discover.go:21` and `cmd/proposal_create.go:44`:

   ```go
   sess, tokenSource, err := resolveSession()
   if err != nil { return err }
   vault, err := resolveVaultForCommand(cmd, tokenSource)
   if err != nil { return err }
   reqURL := sess.Address + "/v1/credentials?vault=" + url.QueryEscape(vault) + "&reveal=true&key=" + url.QueryEscape(key)
   respBody, err := doVaultScopedRequestWithBody("GET", reqURL, sess.Token, vault, nil)
   ```

   The HTTP layer already supports agent tokens, so this is purely a CLI-layer extension with no broker changes.

2. **Smaller alternative**: drop or qualify the "Reading Credentials" section in `cmd/skill_cli.md` (and the equivalent at `cmd/skill_http.md` if applicable) with a note like "admin/dev mode only — not available when `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` is supplied via env; use `GET /v1/credentials?vault=&key=" instead". Smaller surface, but leaves the CLI/HTTP asymmetry in place.

</details>

🟡 The Long help for `proposal create` (cmd/proposal_create.go:25-41) and the matching CLI reference accordion (docs/reference/cli.mdx:599-638) were not extended with the agent-mode requirement note that this PR added to the sibling `discover` command — even though both commands received the same behavioral update (resolveVaultForCommand at line 53, X-Vault threaded at line 87) in this commit. An operator following the new container-deploy recipe who runs `agent-vault vault proposal create -m "need access"` without AGENT_VAULT_VAULT set will hit the new 'vault is required in agent mode' error, but neither --help nor the CLI reference docs name this requirement. Mirror the wording added to discover ("In agent mode (AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN set), AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) is required — there is no project-file or interactive-picker fallback.") in both surfaces.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is wrong

This PR's commit 609613d threaded the agent-mode contract through to peer commands `discover` and `proposal create` — both now call `resolveVaultForCommand` (cmd/run.go:319-324) and pipe the resolved vault through the `X-Vault` header. For `discover`, the user-facing surfaces were updated to match:

- cmd/discover.go:14-20 Long help: "In agent mode (AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN set), AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) is required — there is no project-file or interactive-picker fallback."
- docs/reference/cli.mdx:249 (discover accordion): same paragraph.

For `proposal create` (its peer command, with the identical contract), the Long help at cmd/proposal_create.go:25-41 stops at the JSON-mode example and never mentions agent mode, and the matching accordion at docs/reference/cli.mdx:599-638 only carries the generic 'Create a proposal to request services or credentials. Supports two modes: flag-driven... and JSON file...' description.

## Why the existing code does not surface the requirement

The behavioral enforcement at cmd/proposal_create.go:53 (`resolveVaultForCommand(cmd, tokenSource)`) does fire and produce the runtime error `vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault` (cmd/run.go:300). But this is purely a runtime safety net — `--help` and the reference docs are the documented surfaces, and they don't name the requirement upfront.

## Step-by-step proof

Following the new container-deploy guide:

```bash
export AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx
export AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://broker.example
# AGENT_VAULT_VAULT intentionally unset

agent-vault vault proposal create -m "need access" --help
# Long help shown: flag-driven examples, JSON mode examples. No mention of
# agent-mode AGENT_VAULT_VAULT requirement.

agent-vault vault proposal create -m "need access"
# Error: vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault
```

The user reads --help, sees no mention of the requirement, runs the command, then hits the runtime error. The same shape on the `discover` command, by contrast, names the requirement directly in --help.

## Impact

Severity is **nit** (matching all four verifier confirmations). Doc/help-text only — behavior is correct, the runtime error is clear and actionable. No functional regression. Worth fixing in this PR specifically because the asymmetry was introduced *by* this PR: the same commit (609613d) added the agent-mode note to `discover` but not to its peer command. Shipping the release with internally inconsistent help surfaces between two commands that share a contract is the kind of friction the PR is otherwise careful to avoid.

## How to fix

Two surgical edits:

1. **cmd/proposal_create.go:25-41** — append a paragraph mirroring cmd/discover.go:17-20:
   ```
   In agent mode (AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN set), AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) is
   required — there is no project-file or interactive-picker fallback.
   ```

2. **docs/reference/cli.mdx** — add the same paragraph to the proposal-create accordion (line 599-638), parallel to what line 249 carries for discover.

Note on the misleading `| --vault | default | Target vault |` row at line 608: as one verifier observed, this 'default' default value matches the convention used across every other vault subcommand (cli.mdx:318, :331, :343, :596) rooted in the resolution rule documented at line 239. Changing only this row would itself create a new asymmetry. The actionable fix here is the agent-mode paragraph; the misleading-default row is a pre-existing, codebase-wide artifact best addressed separately.

</details>

🟡 The `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` row in the env-vars tables at `cmd/skill_cli.md:42` and `cmd/skill_http.md:41` still reads "Vault name (set for user-scoped sessions via agent-vault run)" — implying the variable is set automatically — but the new Containerized agent deployment section three blocks down (skill_cli.md:77, skill_http.md:83) explicitly tells operators to set `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production` themselves at deploy time. The two surfaces in each file describe the variable inconsistently. Suggest broadening the row to match the `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` row's both-modes phrasing, e.g. "Vault name. Set automatically by `agent-vault run` in admin mode; set by the operator in agent mode."

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What's wrong

The env-vars tables in `cmd/skill_cli.md:42` and `cmd/skill_http.md:41` describe `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` as:

> Vault name (set for user-scoped sessions via `agent-vault run`)

That phrasing was correct pre-PR, when `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` was only ever set automatically by `vault run` for the wrapped child. This PR changes that contract: in the new agent / containerized mode, `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` is a **required deploy-time input** that the operator provides themselves on the container's environment.

## Why this contradicts itself

Three blocks below the env-vars table, both files now carry an explicit "Containerized agent deployment" section that instructs operators to set the variable:

```
AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx
AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production
```

(`cmd/skill_cli.md` line 77, `cmd/skill_http.md` line 83.)

So within the same file, the table says the variable is set by `agent-vault run`, and the deploy section says the operator sets it. The deploy section is the authoritative one for the new flow.

The sibling `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` row was correctly broadened in this PR to a both-modes phrasing ("Either a vault-scoped session token or a long-lived agent token"). The `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` row was not updated in lockstep.

## Why this matters

These two skill files ship as auto-installed Claude Code / Cursor skill registry entries via `maybeInstallSkills` (`cmd/run.go`). They are written verbatim into `~/.claude/skills/agent-vault-cli/SKILL.md` and `~/.cursor/skills/...` on every developer machine that runs `agent-vault run` against a known agent. So the inconsistency propagates to every downstream skill registry consumer.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Open `cmd/skill_cli.md` line 42: `| `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` | Vault name (set for user-scoped sessions via `agent-vault run`) |`.
2. Scroll to line 77 in the same file (Containerized agent deployment section): `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production` is shown as a deploy-time env var the operator sets.
3. Same shape in `cmd/skill_http.md` (table at line 41, deploy block at line 83).
4. Compare against the sibling `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` row at line 41 of `skill_cli.md`: "Either a vault-scoped session token or a long-lived agent token" — the both-modes phrasing this PR established for tokens.

## Impact

Pure doc-only nit. No functional impact, the deploy section is the authoritative one for the agent-mode flow and the broker behavior is unaffected. Worth fixing in this PR specifically because the PR is what introduces the contradiction by adding the deploy block without updating the table row in lockstep — and the AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN row already shows the right pattern.

## Suggested fix

One-line edit at both `cmd/skill_cli.md:42` and `cmd/skill_http.md:41`. For example:

```
| `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` | Vault name. Set automatically by `agent-vault run` in admin mode; supplied by the operator in agent mode. |
```

This matches the both-modes phrasing the `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` row already uses.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is wrong

The cmd/credential.go diff at lines 23-32 (and the parallel hunks for `get`, `set`, `delete`) swaps the human-mode `ensureSession()` + `resolveVault(cmd)` for the agent-mode-aware `resolveSession()` + `resolveVaultForCommand(cmd, tokenSource)`. Behaviorally that's correct: `agent-vault vault credential set` (and siblings) now work in agent-mode container deploys with `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` + `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR` + `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT`, instead of failing with `not logged in, run 'agent-vault auth login' first`.

But two user-facing surfaces document the new contract — and both were missed for the credential family while being updated for the other extended commands in the same PR:

1. **No Long help on any of the four credential commands.** `cmd/credential.go` declares `credentialListCmd` (line 19), `credentialGetCmd` (line 78), `credentialSetCmd` (line 118), `credentialDeleteCmd` (line 170), and the parent `credentialCmd` with only `Use` + `Short` (or `Use` + `Aliases` + `Short` on the parent). So `agent-vault vault credential set --help` surfaces nothing about the new agent-mode requirement.
2. **The four cli.mdx accordions (lines 521–568) are short-form.** Each has a one-sentence description and a flag table whose only row is `--vault | default | Target vault`. None carries the agent-mode note.

By contrast, the parallel commands updated in the same PR *do* carry the note:
- `cmd/discover.go:14-20` Long help (set in this PR): *"In agent mode (AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN set), AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) is required — there is no project-file or interactive-picker fallback."*
- `cmd/proposal_create.go:25-28` Long help (set in this PR): the same paragraph.
- `docs/reference/cli.mdx:249` (discover accordion) and `:604` (proposal create accordion): the same wording.

This is the same doc-asymmetry family as the previously-accepted nits for discover and proposal-create.

## Step-by-step proof

Following the new container-deploy recipe in `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx`:

```bash
export AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx
export AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
# AGENT_VAULT_VAULT intentionally unset
```

1. Operator runs `agent-vault vault credential set --help` to figure out the contract.
2. Help output: `Set one or more credentials` + flags table. No mention of the agent-mode requirement.
3. Operator runs `agent-vault vault credential set FOO=bar`.
4. `credentialSetCmd.RunE` (cmd/credential.go:121) calls `resolveSession()` → returns `(sess, "AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN", nil)`.
5. `resolveVaultForCommand(cmd, "AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN")` → `resolveVaultForAgentMode` (cmd/run.go:298) → flag empty, env empty → `Error: vault is required in agent mode: set AGENT_VAULT_VAULT or pass --vault`.

Same shape on `credential list`, `get`, `delete`. The runtime error is clear and actionable, but neither --help nor the reference docs name the requirement upfront — same shape as the symmetric case on discover and proposal-create that was already accepted.

## Impact

Severity: **nit**. Doc/help-text only. Behavior is correct, the runtime error is clear and actionable, no functional regression. Worth fixing in this PR specifically because the asymmetry was *introduced* by this PR — the same commit added the agent-mode note to discover and proposal-create but missed credential. Shipping the release with internally inconsistent --help surfaces between four peer commands that share an identical contract is exactly the kind of friction the PR is otherwise careful to avoid (cf. the round-3 / round-5 reworkings).

## How to fix

Two surgical edits, mirroring what discover and proposal-create already received:

1. **cmd/credential.go** — append a Long block to each of the four subcommands (or, more cheaply, to the parent `credentialCmd` so it inherits via cobra's help template):

   ```go
   Long: `<existing one-line description>.

   In agent mode (AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN set), AGENT_VAULT_VAULT (or --vault) is
   required — there is no project-file or interactive-picker fallback.`,
   ```

2. **docs/reference/cli.mdx** — append the same paragraph to each of the four accordions at lines 521, 534, 546, 558, parallel to what `:249` (discover) and `:604` (proposal create) already carry.

The `--vault | default | Target vault` flag-table row is consistent with the convention used across every other vault subcommand (cli.mdx:318, :331, :343, :596) rooted in the resolution rule documented at line 239 — changing only the credential rows would itself create a new asymmetry, so leave that as-is. The actionable fix here is the agent-mode paragraph.

</details>

🟡 Nit: the placeholder `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx` in the new Containerized agent deployment example uses the wrong token shape — long-lived agent tokens minted by `newAgentToken()` (internal/store/sqlite.go:2830) carry the prefix `av_agt_`, not `av_agent_token_`. The string `av_agent_token` is the JSON response *field name* in handle_agents.go:365, not a token prefix. No functional impact (operators paste their actual token, not the literal placeholder), but worth aligning since both files ship as auto-installed skill registry entries via `maybeInstallSkills`. Same one-line fix needed at cmd/skill_http.md:82 — substitute `av_agt_xxx` for `av_agent_token_xxx` in both files.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What's wrong

The new "Containerized agent deployment" section adds a deploy-time env-var block:

```
AGENT_VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx
AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production
```

at `cmd/skill_cli.md:75-79` (and the same block at `cmd/skill_http.md:80-84`). The placeholder `av_agent_token_xxx` is meant to evoke the shape of a long-lived agent token, but no real agent token can ever start with that prefix.

## Why the prefix is `av_agt_`, not `av_agent_token_`

`internal/store/sqlite.go:2830` defines:

```go
func newAgentToken() string { return newPrefixedToken("av_agt_") }
```

So every long-lived agent token minted by the broker starts with `av_agt_`. This is consistent with every other reference across the repo:

- `sdks/sdk-typescript/src/client.ts:38` — `av_agt_...`
- `docs/learn/security.mdx:70` — `| Agent token | \`av_agt_\` |`
- `internal/brokercore/proxyauth_test.go:44` — `av_agt_xyz:default`
- `internal/mitm/proxy_test.go:1208` — `av_agt_multi:`

The string `av_agent_token` does appear in the codebase, but only as the JSON *field name* in the agent-invite redeem response — `handle_agents.go:365` returns `"av_agent_token": sess.ID`. The bug submitter and all four verifiers identified that as the source of the confusion: the placeholder conflates the response field name with the token prefix.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Read `internal/store/sqlite.go:2830`: `newAgentToken()` returns `newPrefixedToken("av_agt_")`. So a real agent token looks like `av_agt_<random>`.
2. Read `cmd/skill_cli.md:77`: the example value is `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx`. That literal can never be produced by `newAgentToken()`.
3. Compare to `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:33` (the companion deploy guide added in this same PR): it sidesteps the issue by writing `av_agent_token_xxx` as well — wait, looking again, that doc actually has the same issue. The verifier note on this is correct: the deploy guide uses the same wrong placeholder. So the consistent fix is to update both skill files **and** `docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:33` together.

## Impact

Pure mental-model nit. Operators paste their actual minted token at deploy time, not the literal placeholder, so there is no functional breakage — the broker accepts whatever the operator's real token is. But these two skill files ship as Claude Code / Cursor skill registry entries via `maybeInstallSkills` (cmd/run.go), so the wrong placeholder propagates onto every developer machine that runs `agent-vault run` against a known agent. An operator copying the recipe will form an incorrect mental model of what their token should look like and may wonder why their actual token doesn't match the example shape.

## Fix

One-line substitution at both locations:

```diff
- AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agent_token_xxx
+ AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agt_xxx
```

Apply at `cmd/skill_cli.md:77` and `cmd/skill_http.md:82`. (`docs/guides/deploy-agent-container.mdx:33` carries the same placeholder and should be updated in lockstep — it is the canonical operator-facing guide for this feature, and the three surfaces should agree.)

</details>

🟡 POST /v1/proposals examples in cmd/skill_http.md (lines 182, 210, 263), AGENTS.md (line 64), and docs/agents/protocol.mdx (line 103) only show `Authorization` + `Content-Type` headers, but the prose immediately above each example (skill_http.md:98, AGENTS.md:24, protocol.mdx:30/37) — narrowed by this PR — explicitly states that instance-level agent tokens must include `X-Vault` on `/v1/proposals`. The `/discover` examples in the same files DO include `X-Vault`, establishing a convention the proposal blocks violate. Fix: add `X-Vault: {vault_name}` to each proposal example header block, mirroring the discover examples above them.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is wrong

This PR explicitly narrows the X-Vault scope wording in three closely-related agent-facing docs to specifically name `/v1/proposals` as a control-plane endpoint that requires the header for instance-level agent tokens:

- `cmd/skill_http.md:98` — "Instance-level agent tokens (persistent agents) must include the `X-Vault: {vault_name}` header on every control-plane call (`/discover`, `/v1/proposals`)"
- `AGENTS.md:24` — "you must include `X-Vault: {vault_name}` on all control-plane requests (`/discover`, `/v1/proposals`)"
- `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:30/37` — "must include an `X-Vault` header on `/discover` and `/v1/proposals` requests"

But every `POST /v1/proposals` example block in these same three files only shows `Authorization` + `Content-Type` headers — `X-Vault` is missing:

- `cmd/skill_http.md:182-184`, `210-212`, `263-265` (three proposal examples)
- `AGENTS.md:64-66`
- `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:103-106`

By contrast, the `/discover` examples in the same files DO include `X-Vault` (skill_http.md:92-95, AGENTS.md:30-33, protocol.mdx:53-56), establishing a convention the proposal blocks violate.

## Why this matters

The PR is precisely what introduces the asymmetry. The diff hits the `Authorization` line in every one of these proposal examples (the `AGENT_VAULT_SESSION_TOKEN` → `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` rename), and the prose narrowing was applied at the same time — so the natural lockstep edit was already in flight, and adding `X-Vault` to each example would have been a one-line per-example change.

Functionally, an instance-level agent token without `X-Vault` on `POST /v1/proposals` is rejected by the broker. `internal/server/vault_resolve.go:31-35`:

```go
vaultName := r.Header.Get("X-Vault")
if vaultName == "" {
    jsonError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Agent tokens require X-Vault header to specify which vault to use")
    return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("missing X-Vault header")
}
```

`POST /v1/proposals` routes through `resolveVaultForSession` (per the resolved bug already addressed for `cmd/proposal_create.go`), so the broker enforcement is unambiguous. Vault-scoped session tokens still work because the resolver short-circuits on `sess.VaultID != ""`, but the agent-token path — newly first-class for these docs after this PR — breaks.

## Step-by-step proof

Following the canonical container-deploy recipe this PR documents:

```bash
export AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN=av_agt_xxx          # instance-level agent token
export AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production
```

1. Agent reads `cmd/skill_http.md` (or `AGENTS.md`, or `protocol.mdx`) and copies the `POST /v1/proposals` example verbatim — only `Authorization` and `Content-Type` headers on the wire.
2. Broker's `resolveVaultForSession` (vault_resolve.go:31-35) inspects the request: `sess.AgentID != ""`, `sess.VaultID == ""`, `X-Vault == ""`.
3. Broker returns HTTP 400: `Agent tokens require X-Vault header to specify which vault to use`.
4. The agent has `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT=production` sitting in its env, but the example never told it to copy that value into `X-Vault`.

The skill_http.md note added by this PR (line 88) does say the agent is responsible for copying `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT` into `X-Vault` on each request — but the example two paragraphs below demonstrates the opposite shape.

## Impact

Severity: **nit**. Doc-only, prose elsewhere in the same files is correct, attentive agents using SDKs (which set `X-Vault` programmatically) avoid the trap, and the broker's 400 is self-explanatory. But:

- These three files are the agent-facing protocol references — `skill_http.md` and `AGENTS.md` ship as auto-installed Claude Code / Cursor skill registry entries via `maybeInstallSkills` (`cmd/run.go`), so the inconsistency propagates onto every developer machine.
- A developer writing a custom agent who copies the literal example as a starting point will hit the rejection.
- This PR is what introduces the asymmetry — pre-PR, the broader "every vault-scoped request" wording was at least defensible against the example; the narrowed wording explicitly contradicts the example.

## Suggested fix

One-line addition to each proposal example header block, mirroring the discover examples right above them:

```diff
  POST {AGENT_VAULT_ADDR}/v1/proposals
  Authorization: Bearer {AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN}
+ X-Vault: {vault_name}
  Content-Type: application/json
```

Apply at:
- `cmd/skill_http.md:182-184`, `210-212`, `263-265`
- `AGENTS.md:64-66`
- `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:103-106`

Mechanical edit, lockstep with the X-Vault prose narrowing already in this PR.

</details>
