body:
🟡 The path-scoped example in `serviceAddCmd.Long` shows `--host slack.com/api/*` without quotes (cmd/service.go:158), while the two sibling examples added in this same PR — cmd/skill_cli.md:102 and cmd/proposal_create.go:39 — wrap the inline-form host in single quotes. A user copy-pasting this line into zsh (default `nomatch`) gets `zsh: no matches found: slack.com/api/*` before the binary runs; under `shopt -s failglob` in bash it fails similarly. Fix is one character: wrap the value in single quotes to match the convention used in the two adjacent examples.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

In the help text for `agent-vault vault service add` (`cmd/service.go:158`), the path-scoped example reads:

```
agent-vault vault service add --name slack-bot --host slack.com/api/* --auth-type bearer --token-key SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
```

The `slack.com/api/*` value is unquoted. The two parallel examples added in this same PR both wrap the inline-form host in single quotes:

- `cmd/skill_cli.md:102` — `--host 'slack.com/api/*'`
- `cmd/proposal_create.go:39` — `--host 'slack.com/api/*'`

So `serviceAddCmd.Long` is the lone outlier in a PR that otherwise consistently quotes the inline form.

### Why it matters

The `*` is a shell glob, so its fate depends on the user’s shell config:

- **zsh, default `nomatch`**: aborts with `zsh: no matches found: slack.com/api/*` before `agent-vault` is even invoked.
- **bash, `shopt -s failglob`**: same outcome — failed glob, non-zero exit, command never runs.
- **bash, default** (literal-on-no-match): the glob is left literal and the command happens to work, which is why this slips through manual smoke-testing.
- **Either shell, if a directory tree literally matching `slack.com/api/` happens to exist** (e.g. an operator who cloned the repo and inspected the example): glob expansion replaces the argument with one or more file paths.

The help text is a copy-paste invitation; on any of the shell configs above the documented example simply does not run as printed.

### Why the inconsistency is the strongest evidence

The same author quoted `slack.com/api/*` in both sibling examples added in this PR (one in another `cmd/` Go file, one in a markdown skill doc). The asymmetry isn’t a deliberate choice — it’s a one-line oversight in a hunk that already established the right pattern in two other files.

### Step-by-step proof

1. Operator opens `agent-vault vault service add --help`, scans the examples section.
2. Copies line 158 verbatim: `agent-vault vault service add --name slack-bot --host slack.com/api/* --auth-type bearer --token-key SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`.
3. Pastes into a zsh prompt (default settings).
4. zsh attempts to expand `slack.com/api/*` against the cwd, finds no match, aborts with `zsh: no matches found: slack.com/api/*`. The binary never runs; no auth-type prompt, no service add.

### Fix

Wrap the value in single quotes to match `cmd/skill_cli.md:102` and `cmd/proposal_create.go:39`:

```diff
-  agent-vault vault service add --name slack-bot --host slack.com/api/* --auth-type bearer --token-key SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
+  agent-vault vault service add --name slack-bot --host 'slack.com/api/*' --auth-type bearer --token-key SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
```

This is documentation-only (no runtime code path is affected) and one character of churn — nit severity, but worth aligning with the convention already established elsewhere in the same PR.

</details>

🟡 The JSDoc on `services.set()` (sdks/sdk-typescript/src/resources/services.ts:230-234) still describes pre-PR semantics: "Upsert one or more services by host. If a service with the same host already exists, it is replaced." Post-PR, identity is canonical Name (slug), not Host — two services can coexist at the same host with different names/paths (the headline Slack two-credential case this PR motivates). The sibling `ServiceInput` JSDoc (lines 80-108) and `remove()` JSDoc (lines 252-267) were updated for the new semantics; `set()` was missed. Fix: rewrite the JSDoc to say upsert-by-name and mention the server's auto-slug + collision-bump behavior.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

The JSDoc block above `ServicesResource.set()` at `sdks/sdk-typescript/src/resources/services.ts:230-237` reads:

```
/**
 * Upsert one or more services by host.
 *
 * If a service with the same host already exists, it is replaced.
 * Requires vault admin role.
 * ...
 */
async set(services: ServiceInput[]): Promise<SetServicesResult> { ... }
```

This documents the pre-PR host-keyed identity model. Post-PR, the server identifies services by canonical **Name** (slug), and two services with the same host can coexist as long as their names differ — the motivating Slack split (`slack-bot` at `slack.com/api/*` and `slack-conn` at `slack.com/api/apps.connections.*`) is exactly this case.

### Why this is a real inconsistency, not a phrasing quibble

The rest of the SDK was migrated to the new model in the same PR:

- The `ServiceInput` JSDoc (lines 80-108) correctly describes Name as the identity field and host as the matcher pattern (with inline-form examples).
- The `remove()` JSDoc (lines 252-267) explicitly calls out the name-vs-host disambiguation and the 409-candidate-list behavior.
- The server handler `handleServicesUpsert` (internal/server/handle_services.go:457-461) builds `byName := …` from existing services and upserts via `existing[idx] = svc` keyed on `svc.Name` — never on `Host`.
- The bumped-collision pass in `normalizeIncomingAgainstExisting` (handle_services.go:69-101) auto-slugs blank Names from `Slugify(Host, Path)` and bumps to `-2`, `-3`, etc. on collision — so the literal claim that "a service with the same host already exists, it is replaced" is now strictly false in two distinct ways.

### Step-by-step proof that the JSDoc is wrong

1. Vault holds `{name:"slack-bot", host:"slack.com", path:"/api/*", auth:{...}}`.
2. Caller invokes `vault.services!.set([{name:"slack-conn", host:"slack.com", path:"/api/apps.connections.*", auth:{...}}])`.
3. Per the existing JSDoc, "a service with the same host already exists, it is replaced" — so `slack-bot` should be replaced.
4. Per the actual behavior (verified in handle_services.go: `byName` index), both services coexist because their Names differ.

The documented behavior and runtime behavior diverge on the exact use case this PR exists to enable.

### Impact

Documentation-only — the type system (`ServiceInput`) and the runtime path both work correctly. But the JSDoc on `set()` is what TypeScript users see as IDE hover-text and in generated API references (typedoc, ts-docs). For a v0.2.0 release whose headline feature is precisely the host-shared, name-disambiguated service model, leaving the canonical write method's docstring contradicting that model is a real onboarding hazard.

### How to fix

Replace lines 230-234 with text that mirrors what `ServiceInput` and `remove()` already say. Suggested wording:

+
+### Matching priority
+
+When two service `host` patterns could match a request, the winner is chosen deterministically:
+
+1. **Host tier first.** A service whose host portion is an **exact match** of the request host always beats one with a **wildcard** host (`*.example.com`) — even when the wildcard rule has a more specific path portion.
+2. **Path specificity within a host tier.** Among services in the same host tier, the rule with the **longest literal path prefix** wins (characters in the path portion of `host` before the first `*`). A bare-host pattern (no path) scores 0 (catch-all).
+3. **Declaration order on tie.** If two rules tie on host tier and literal path-prefix length, the rule appearing first in the configured service list wins.
+
+Example — Slack with two credentials at the same host:
+
+| Request | `host=slack.com/api/apps.connections.*` | `host=slack.com/api/*` | Winner |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `slack.com/api/apps.connections.open` | matches, prefix length 22 | matches, prefix length 5 | `slack-conn` (longer prefix) |
+| `slack.com/api/chat.postMessage` | doesn't match | matches | `slack-bot` |
+
+The matcher does not run regex, does not match on method/headers/query/body, and does not bound `*` at path segments. Patterns that tie under rule 2 fall to declaration order.

🟡 The new `### Matching priority` H3 (cmd/skill_http.md:230) is inserted in the middle of the `Key fields:` bullet list — services[].* bullets at 222-228, the H3 + paragraphs + table at 230-245, then the list resumes at 246-249 with `credentials[].action`, `credentials`, `message`, `credentials[].obtain`. Per CommonMark, the H3 terminates the prior list, so those four trailing bullets render under "Matching priority" rather than "Key fields" — making credentials/message look like sub-fields of match priority. The sibling `cmd/skill_cli.md` avoids this by inlining the matching-priority summary into the `services[].host` bullet's description; doing the same here (or moving the entire H3 block to after the Key fields list) keeps the list contiguous.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

`cmd/skill_http.md` has a `Key fields:` heading at line 222 that opens a bullet list describing the JSON shape of a proposal. The list begins with six `services[].*` bullets (action, name, host, auth, substitutions, enabled) at lines 223-228, then this PR inserts a `### Matching priority` H3 heading at line 230 followed by a multi-paragraph body (intro paragraph, numbered list, comparison table, closing paragraph at lines 232-245). Lines 246-249 then continue the original list with `- credentials[].action`, `- credentials`, `- message`, `- credentials[].obtain` — but there is no resumed `Key fields:` preamble before them.

### How it manifests

Under any standard CommonMark renderer (GitHub web, Mintlify previewing this PR, mdBook, the docs site), an H3 heading terminates the preceding list. The four trailing bullets at 246-249 therefore start a **new** list nested visually under the `### Matching priority` section. A reader scanning the document sees:

- Matching priority
  - (paragraphs, table)
  - credentials[].action — ...
  - credentials — ...
  - message — ...
  - credentials[].obtain — ...

…which strongly implies those four keys are sub-fields of match priority, when in fact they describe the proposal payload's credentials/message keys and have nothing to do with matching.

### Step-by-step proof

1. Open the Mintlify preview at https://agent-vault-services-path-based-matching.mintlify.app (or render the file on github.com).
2. Navigate to the proposal-creation section of `cmd/skill_http.md`.
3. Observe that the `Key fields:` list visually ends after the `services[].enabled` bullet because the `### Matching priority` H3 closes the list per CommonMark.
4. The `credentials[].action`, `credentials`, `message`, `credentials[].obtain` bullets render under the `Matching priority` section, mislabeling them as sub-fields of matching priority semantics.

### Why existing code does not prevent it

The sibling file `cmd/skill_cli.md` handled the same content correctly: it folded the matching-priority summary directly into the `services[].host` bullet (`resolves overlapping rules deterministically (exact-host beats wildcard, then longer literal path prefix wins, then declaration order)`), keeping the `Key fields:` list contiguous. The PR author followed two different patterns for the same information across the two skill files; only `skill_http.md` has the structural break.

### Impact

Documentation-only — the underlying content is all present, and an LLM agent reading the raw bullets correctly will still parse them (which is why severity is **nit**). The failure mode is comprehension/rendering: humans previewing on GitHub or Mintlify, and any agent consuming an HTML-rendered version, see the four trailing bullets as sub-fields of `Matching priority` rather than as continuation of `Key fields:`. No runtime impact, no functional regression, but it undermines the migration guidance the PR exists to provide and is a one-paragraph fix.

### How to fix

Two equivalent options:

1. **Move `### Matching priority` after the entire `Key fields:` list** — keeps the existing detailed treatment intact but at the right scope level.
2. **Inline the matching-priority summary into the `services[].host` bullet** as `cmd/skill_cli.md` already does. Smallest diff, perfect symmetry between the two skill files, but loses the comparison table — keep option 1 if the table is worth preserving.

</details>

🟡 DELETE /v1/vaults/{name}/services (handleServicesClear, handle_services.go:724-745) writes `SetBrokerConfig(ns.ID, "[]")` without acquiring `s.lockVaultServices(ns.ID)`, while every other write-side handler in this PR does (handleServicesUpsert:454, handleServiceRemove:533, handleServicePatch:622, handleServicesSet:714, handleAdminProposalApprove:491). The new `vaultServiceMu` docstring at server.go:77-83 explicitly enumerates "DELETE on /services" as covered, so this is a one-line oversight: insert `defer s.lockVaultServices(ns.ID)()` between the role check and the SetBrokerConfig call. Nit severity — the trigger requires concurrent admin operations on the same vault, which is rare in practice, but the contradiction between the documented invariant and the implementation is concrete and fixable in one line.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

The PR adds an in-process `vaultServiceMu` lock to serialize the load → modify → save cycle that every service-mutating handler follows, with a docstring at `internal/server/server.go:77-83` that explicitly enumerates the covered surface:

> serializes the read-modify-write cycle that all service-mutating handlers (POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE on /services and proposal apply) follow. SQLite's MaxOpenConns(1) only serializes individual SQL statements, not the load → mutate → save sequence

The lock is acquired in every other write-side handler in this PR:

- `handleServicesUpsert` — POST /services (handle_services.go:454)
- `handleServiceRemove` — DELETE /services/{name-or-host} (line 533)
- `handleServicePatch` — PATCH /services/{name-or-host} (line 622)
- `handleServicesSet` — PUT /services (line 714)
- `handleAdminProposalApprove` — proposal apply (handle_proposals.go:491)

But `handleServicesClear` — DELETE /v1/vaults/{name}/services (clear-all, registered at server.go:754) — is missing the acquisition. Between `requireVaultAdmin` at line 735 and `SetBrokerConfig` at line 739 there is no `lockVaultServices` call.

## Step-by-step proof of the race

The lock's docstring describes exactly the failure mode this gap enables. Concretely:

1. **Admin A** issues `POST /v1/vaults/foo/services` with an upsert. `handleServicesUpsert` acquires the lock, calls `loadServices` and reads existing = `[S1, S2]`. It has computed its updated slice but has not yet written.
2. **Admin B** issues `DELETE /v1/vaults/foo/services` (clear-all). `handleServicesClear` does not acquire the lock — its `SetBrokerConfig(ns.ID, "[]")` runs immediately, returns 200 with `{"cleared": true}`.
3. **Admin A** finishes its computation and writes `SetBrokerConfig(ns.ID, "[S1, S2, S3]")`.

Admin B saw a 200 OK and reasonably believed the vault was empty, but the services are back. SQLite's statement-level serialization (`MaxOpenConns(1)`) does not help: each `SetBrokerConfig` SQL write is atomic on its own, but the cycle (A's load → A's mutate → A's save) interleaves with B's save in the bad order. This is the exact mechanism the PR added the lock to prevent for upserts; the gap on clear leaves the same hazard in place for the documented invariant.

## Why existing code does not prevent it

- The handler body of `handleServicesClear` is unchanged by this PR, but the *invariant* the docstring enumerates is new. Pre-PR there was no lock at all, so "no lock on clear" was not a contradiction. Post-PR, the docstring and the implementation disagree.
- There is no other in-process serializer for `/services` mutations — the PR's lock is the singular mechanism.

## Impact

Severity is nit. The trigger requires concurrent admin operations on the same vault where one is a clear-all and the other is a write; this is rare in practice. There is no data exfiltration or security implication. But the failure mode is silent (the clear returns 200 OK while the services come back) and the gap is a one-line oversight that contradicts the new docstring contract.

## Fix

One-line addition mirroring every other write-side handler, inserted between the role check and `SetBrokerConfig`:

```go
func (s *Server) handleServicesClear(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    name := r.PathValue("name")

    ns, err := s.store.GetVault(ctx, name)
    if err != nil || ns == nil {
        jsonError(w, http.StatusNotFound, fmt.Sprintf("Vault %q not found", name))
        return
    }

    if _, err := s.requireVaultAdmin(w, r, ns.ID); err != nil {
        return
    }

    defer s.lockVaultServices(ns.ID)()  // <-- add this line

    if _, err := s.store.SetBrokerConfig(ctx, ns.ID, "[]"); err != nil {
        jsonError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to clear services")
        return
    }

    jsonOK(w, map[string]interface{}{"vault": name, "cleared": true})
}
```

</details>

🔴 Stored auto-slug Names from create-time normalization are persisted into the proposal JSON without their `autoSlugged` flag, so at apply time `normalizeProposalServices` (handle_services.go:190 — gated on `svc.Name == ""`) and the bump pass (line 217 — gated on `autoSlugged[i]`) both skip them. `MergeServices` then upserts purely by Name (merge.go:50-62, no (Host, Path) consistency check), silently overwriting an unrelated existing service that happens to share that slug — within the 7-day proposal TTL, a co-admin adding a service with an explicit slug-shaped name (very common: `stripe`, `api-mycompany-com`, etc.) is enough to trigger silent data loss. Smallest fix: add a Host/Path consistency check in MergeServices's `case exists` branch and surface a 409 ("proposal targets name X but the current service with that name has changed Host/Path — reject manually"), matching the create-path safety the PR already shipped.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What goes wrong

The proposal flow normalizes Names twice — at create time and at apply time — using the same `normalizeProposalServices` helper. At **create time** (handle_proposals.go:156, ActionSet branch in handle_services.go:189-197), entries with no Name get `Slugify(Host, Path)` and `autoSlugged[i] = true`; the bump pass at handle_services.go:216-226 then suffixes `-2`, `-3`, … if the slug collides with any existing or explicit name. The resolved Name is written back into the proposal services JSON via the marshal at handle_proposals.go:206. **The `autoSlugged` flag is intra-call only — it does not cross the storage boundary.**

At **apply time** (handle_proposals.go:485), the same helper runs against the *current* existing state, but the ActionSet branch is gated on `if svc.Name == ""` (line 190). Every post-create-time proposal already has Name filled, so:
- Lookup branch (190-197) — skipped, `autoSlugged[i]` stays `false`.
- Bump pass first loop (210-215) — `!autoSlugged[i]` true → `used[out[i].Name] = true` (treats it as an explicit name to defend).
- Bump pass second loop (216-226) — `!autoSlugged[i]` true → `continue`, no bumping.

The Name is frozen. `MergeServices` (merge.go:50-62) then runs:

```go
default: // ActionSet: upsert
    idx, exists := nameIndex[p.Name]
    switch {
    case exists && p.Auth == nil && p.Enabled != nil:
        merged[idx].Enabled = p.Enabled
    case exists:
        next := toBrokerService(p)
        if len(p.Substitutions) == 0 {
            next.Substitutions = merged[idx].Substitutions
        }
        merged[idx] = next   // ← unconditional replace, no Host/Path check
    default:
        ...
    }
```

There is no comparison between `existing[idx].Host/Path` and `p.Host/Path` — a Name match is treated as upsert intent regardless.

## Step-by-step proof (concrete data-loss scenario)

1. **t0:** vault holds `[{Name:"X", Host:"a.com"}]`.
2. **t0:** Operator A submits a proposal with no Name: `{action:"set", host:"b.com", path:"/api/*", auth:{type:"bearer", token:"StripeKey"}}`. `normalizeProposalServices` runs against t0 existing state. `findByHostPath` returns nil → `Slugify("b.com", "/api/*")` → `"b-com-api"`, `autoSlugged[0]=true`. Bump pass: `used = {"X"}`, `"b-com-api"` not in used → accepted. Stored proposal services_json: `[{"action":"set","name":"b-com-api","host":"b.com/api/*","auth":{...}}]`.
3. **t1 (3 days later, well within 7-day TTL):** Operator B independently adds a service via direct `POST /v1/vaults/foo/services`: `{name:"b-com-api", host:"unrelated.internal", auth:{type:"bearer", token:"OctopusToken"}}`. This is fully legitimate per the new model — slug-shaped names are how the docs and `/discover` advertise services. The POST goes through `normalizeIncomingAgainstExisting` (handle_services.go:69-101), which leaves explicit names alone (per its own comment line 62-65: 'Explicit-name collisions are left alone'). Vault state at t1: `[{Name:"X",...}, {Name:"b-com-api", Host:"unrelated.internal", Auth:OctopusToken}]`.
4. **t2:** Operator A approves their proposal. Apply path:
   - `loadServices` returns t1 state.
   - `normalizeProposalServices`: proposed[0].Name = "b-com-api" (non-empty) → ActionSet lookup branch SKIPPED. `autoSlugged[0]` stays `false`. Bump pass: first loop seeds `used["b-com-api"]=true`; second loop sees `!autoSlugged[0]` → continue. Name unchanged.
   - `MergeServices`: `nameIndex["b-com-api"]` → idx=1 (the unrelated service). `merged[1] = toBrokerService(proposed[0])` → silently replaces Operator B's `unrelated.internal` + OctopusToken with `b.com/api/*` + StripeKey.
5. **Result:** `{"status":"applied"}`. No warning. Subsequent traffic to `unrelated.internal` that depended on Octopus injection breaks (502 / missing credential). The Stripe rule lands at `b.com/api/*` correctly, but the unrelated service is the casualty.

## Why this isn't "by-design upsert-by-name" (addressing the refutation)

The refutation argues this is the same intentional semantic as the direct POST path. Three reasons that argument doesn't hold:

1. **The system already distinguishes auto-slugged from explicit names** — at create time. `autoSlugged[i]` is tracked precisely so that auto-derived slugs bump rather than overwrite, while explicit names (where the operator typed a slug expressing upsert intent) are left alone. The bug is that this distinction is **lost at the storage boundary**, not that it doesn't exist.

2. **The POST symmetry argument cuts the other way.** When Operator B does `POST {name:"b-com-api", host:"x.com"}`, B is making a fresh request *now* and is responsible for what they typed. When Operator A's proposal applies *days later*, A never typed "b-com-api" — the system generated it on A's behalf at create time, when the world looked different. Treating these two paths identically conflates user-expressed intent with system-derived state.

3. **The "rotate to a different host" downside is overstated.** A pre-merge (Host, Path) consistency check rejects the apply (with operator-actionable framing: 'reject the proposal manually') only when the existing service with that Name has a *different* Host/Path. A legitimate `{name:"stripe", host:"api.stripe.com"} → {name:"stripe", host:"api-mirror.stripe.com"}` rotation goes through the **direct POST path** (handle_services.go), not the proposal flow, and would still work fine. Even within proposals, an operator who *intended* to rotate Host can do so by explicitly naming the service in their proposal — the auto-slug path that this bug affects is by definition not that case (the operator omitted Name).

## Realism

Slug-shaped names are very common operator choices. `Slugify` is many-to-one over hosts (`api.foo.com` and `api-foo.com` both → `api-foo-com`; `b.com /api/*` and `b.com /api` both → `b-com-api`). Combined with the 7-day TTL window — long enough for any active multi-admin team to add new services while a proposal sits pending — the trigger is narrow but not exotic. This is the apply-time twin of the create-time bug already fixed in abfd87c (per inline-comment #3214250475) and the apply-time delete bug fixed earlier in this PR cycle (per inline-comment #3214479128).

## Suggested fix

Smallest change: add a (Host, Path) consistency check in `MergeServices`'s `case exists` branch:

```go
case exists:
    if existing := merged[idx]; existing.Host != p.Host || existing.Path != p.Path {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("proposal targets name %q but the current service with that name is at %s — reject the proposal manually", p.Name, existing.MatcherPattern())
    }
    next := toBrokerService(p)
    if len(p.Substitutions) == 0 {
        next.Substitutions = merged[idx].Substitutions
    }
    merged[idx] = next
```

Surfaced upstream as 409 in handleAdminProposalApprove. This matches the safety pattern the PR already shipped at the create path.

</details>

🟡 AGENTS.md:36 says `/discover` services entries have `name`, `host`, and `path`, but the actual wire shape (internal/server/handle_discovery.go:10-13, 65-68) is just `{name, host}` — Path is joined into Host via `MatcherPattern()`. The other docs touched in this PR (cmd/skill_cli.md:91, cmd/skill_http.md:100, docs/agents/protocol.mdx, docs/quickstart/custom-agent.mdx) all correctly say "each entry has `name` and `host`"; AGENTS.md is the lone outlier. Fix: change "each entry has `name`, `host`, and `path`" to "each entry has `name` and `host`" to match the sibling docs.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

AGENTS.md is the canonical agent-facing doc — it tells AI agents how to talk to the broker. Line 36 reads:

> Response includes `vault`, `services` (each entry has `name`, `host`, and `path`), and `available_credentials`...

This describes a third `path` field on each `/discover` services entry that does not exist in the response.

### The actual wire shape

`internal/server/handle_discovery.go:10-13` defines the response entry as:

```go
type discoverService struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
    Host string `json:"host"`
}
```

Two fields, no `path`. At handle_discovery.go:63-68 the response is built with:

```go
services[i] = discoverService{
    Name: svc.Name,
    Host: svc.MatcherPattern(),
}
```

`MatcherPattern()` (broker.go) joins `Host + Path` into a single inline string — so a path-scoped service appears as `{"name":"slack-bot","host":"slack.com/api/*"}` on the wire, not as separate `host` + `path` fields. There is no separate `path` key in the JSON output.

### The asymmetry is the strongest evidence

The same author updated four other docs in this PR consistently — only AGENTS.md drifted:

- `cmd/skill_cli.md:91` — "each with `name` and `host`"
- `cmd/skill_http.md:100` — "each with `name` and `host`"
- `docs/agents/protocol.mdx:74` — JSON example shows only `name` + `host`
- `docs/quickstart/custom-agent.mdx:77` — JSON example shows only `name` + `host`

AGENTS.md is the lone outlier, and AGENTS.md is the doc agents are explicitly pointed at.

### Step-by-step proof

1. Operator configures a path-scoped Slack service: `{name: "slack-bot", host: "slack.com", path: "/api/*"}`.
2. Agent calls `GET /discover`.
3. `handleDiscover` runs through `MatcherPattern()`, producing the JSON entry `{"name":"slack-bot","host":"slack.com/api/*"}` — no `path` field.
4. Agent, following AGENTS.md, parses the entry expecting three fields. Reading `entry.path` returns `undefined`.
5. Any routing/parsing logic the agent built on the assumption that `path` is a separate field is broken from the start.

### Impact

Documentation-only — no runtime regression, no security risk. But AGENTS.md is the highest-leverage agent-facing doc in the repo ("This file describes the protocol agents follow…"). Agents calibrated to AGENTS.md may build broken parsing/routing logic on top of an imaginary field. One-line fix.

### How to fix

Change AGENTS.md:36 to mirror the sibling docs:

🟡 The interactive service builder fires a misleading 'Warning: multiple services for host "slack.com" — the last service wins' on legitimate path-scoped services. After this PR, two services may share a Host with different Paths (the headline Slack two-credential split), but `findDuplicateHosts` (cmd/service_interactive.go:699-711) still keys only on `s.Host` — and the warning text is wrong on two counts post-PR: the services are NOT duplicates (NormalizeServices gives them distinct Names and both coexist), and `MatchService.Better` resolves ties to the FIRST declared, not last. Fix is one line: key the dedup on `s.MatcherPattern()` (or `(Host, Path)`) and reword the message to match the new first-wins tiebreak.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What goes wrong

`buildService` at cmd/service_interactive.go:269-286 was updated by this PR to call `broker.SplitInlineHost(host, "")` and return `&broker.Service{Host: bareHost, Path: path, Auth: auth}`. So a user who types `slack.com/api/*` for the Bot rule and `slack.com/api/apps.connections.*` for the Socket Mode rule produces two services that both have Host="slack.com" with distinct Paths.

The duplicate-host check at cmd/service_interactive.go:243-244 wasn't updated:

```go
for _, dup := range findDuplicateHosts(services) {
    fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "%s multiple services for host %q — the last service wins\n", warningText("Warning:"), dup)
}
```

And `findDuplicateHosts` at cmd/service_interactive.go:699-711 keys purely on Host:

```go
seen := make(map[string]int)
for _, s := range services {
    seen[s.Host]++
}
```

So the second Slack entry trips `seen["slack.com"]==2` and the warning fires.

## Both claims in the warning are wrong post-PR

1. **The services are not duplicates.** `mergeServices` no longer dedups by host (the legacy 'host = identity' overwrite behavior is gone), and `finalServices = broker.NormalizeServices(finalServices)` runs at cmd/service_interactive.go:64 before `broker.Validate`, so each gets a distinct Slugify-derived Name (`slack-com-api` and `slack-com-api-apps-connections`) and `broker.Validate` only rejects on duplicate Names. Both services persist intact.

2. **'The last service wins' is the legacy upsert-by-host overwrite framing.** Post-PR, `MatchService` (broker.go:542-561) iterates services and replaces `best` only when `score.Better(bestScore)` returns true. `Better` (broker.go:513-518) does strict `>` comparison on both HostTier and PathLiteralLen — returning false on tie — so the FIRST declared service wins on tiebreak. A user who reads the warning literally believes the second credential overrides the first, when in fact paths route distinctly *and* ties go to the first declared.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Operator runs `agent-vault vault service set` (interactive mode).
2. Builds `slack-bot` with host `slack.com/api/*`. `buildService` returns `{Host:"slack.com", Path:"/api/*"}`. `findDuplicateHosts([{Host:"slack.com"}])` returns []. No warning.
3. Builds `slack-conn` with host `slack.com/api/apps.connections.*`. `buildService` returns `{Host:"slack.com", Path:"/api/apps.connections.*"}`.
4. `services` is now `[{Host:"slack.com", Path:"/api/*"}, {Host:"slack.com", Path:"/api/apps.connections.*"}]`.
5. `findDuplicateHosts(services)` iterates and counts only `s.Host` → `seen["slack.com"]==2` → returns `["slack.com"]`.
6. Stderr gets: `Warning: multiple services for host "slack.com" — the last service wins`.
7. The flagship feature this PR exists to enable is presented as broken via misleading instrumentation, on the exact workflow the docs and PR description hold up as the motivating case.

## Why it is nit, not normal

The persisted state is correct (both services survive with distinct slug Names, the merge proceeds, validate passes, the PUT succeeds), so this is UX-only. But the false-positive warning fires precisely on the headline Slack two-credential split and uses the wrong tiebreak framing. Fix is a one-liner: key dedup on `s.MatcherPattern()` (or `(Host, Path)`) and update the message to reflect the new first-wins semantics.

## On the refutation (duplicate of bug_003)

The duplicate claim concerns the same underlying defect surface. The synthesis agent already merged duplicate descriptions into this single bug, and three independent verifiers confirmed the same code path with the same line numbers and the same severity (nit) — the substantive analysis stands on its own at this code location regardless of how an earlier near-duplicate was triaged. Filing this once, with the merged framing the synthesis chose, is the right outcome.

</details>

🟡 The CLI proposal review (`vault proposal show/approve/review`) prints proposed services as just `actionMarker + r.MatcherPattern()` at cmd/proposal.go:52, dropping the canonical service `Name` (slug) entirely. The web UI sibling (web/src/components/ProposalPreview.tsx) was updated in this same PR to render a dedicated 'Name' line above 'Host' for set entries — and the delete list at line 257 already prefers `service.name || service.host` — so the CLI is the lone surface that hides the identifier the merge actually keys on. Fix is one line: prepend `r.Name` when present, e.g. `fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s %s %s", actionMarker(string(r.Action)), r.Name, mutedText(r.MatcherPattern()))`.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

`printServices` at cmd/proposal.go:47-70 renders proposed services for the CLI's proposal-review surfaces (`vault proposal show`, `vault proposal approve`, `vault proposal review`). Line 52 emits exactly:

```go
fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s %s", actionMarker(string(r.Action)), r.MatcherPattern())
```

`MatcherPattern()` returns the joined inline form (`Host` + `Path`, e.g. `slack.com/api/*`). The canonical `Name` field — the slug this PR establishes as the per-vault upsert/delete identity — is never printed.

### The specific code path that triggers it

This PR makes Name canonical on three load-bearing axes that are now all invisible to the CLI reviewer:

1. **Upserts key on Name.** `handleServicesUpsert` (handle_services.go:457-461) builds `byName` from existing services and runs `existing[idx] = svc` keyed on `svc.Name` — never on `Host`.
2. **MergeServices keys on Name.** internal/proposal/merge.go:43-54 indexes purely by Name and removes/replaces whichever entry hits `nameIndex[p.Name]`.
3. **Validate hard-requires Name.** `proposal.Validate` (proposal.go:175 area, broker.go:374-376) rejects empty Name, and `normalizeProposalServices` auto-fills Name on every stored proposal — so every post-PR proposal carries a populated Name field that the CLI silently drops.

### Why existing code does not prevent it

The web UI sibling was updated correctly in this same PR. `web/src/components/ProposalPreview.tsx` lines 207-225 render a dedicated "Name" line above "Host" for each set entry; the delete list at line 257 prefers `service.name || service.host`. The CLI's parallel surface in `printServices` was missed — the diff for cmd/proposal.go only changed line 52 from `r.Host` to `r.MatcherPattern()` and removed the description block, but did not add the Name. There is no other code path that surfaces the Name on the CLI review output.

### Step-by-step proof

1. An admin runs `agent-vault vault service add --host slack.com --path '/api/*' --auth-type bearer --token-key SLACK_TOKEN` (no `--name`). The server's `normalizeIncomingAgainstExisting` auto-slugs the new service to `slack-com-api`. Suppose another service already used that slug, so the server bumps to `slack-com-api-2`.
2. Later, an agent raises a proposal with `{action:"set", host:"slack.com", path:"/api/v2/*", auth:{...}}`. `normalizeProposalServices` slug-bumps to `slack-com-api-v2` (or `-3` on collision).
3. The admin reviews via `agent-vault vault proposal show <id>`. The output reads:
   ```
   Proposed services:
     ~ slack.com/api/v2/*
         auth: bearer
   ```
4. The admin has zero visibility into which canonical slug the merge will actually create or update — only the inline-form host pattern. They cannot tell from the CLI whether this proposal will create `slack-com-api-v2`, update an existing entry by that name, or whether (in the case of a delete proposal targeting a host shared by two path-scoped services) the right service is being targeted.

### Impact

Severity is **nit** because the proposal still applies correctly — `MergeServices` keys on Name internally and the apply path is unaffected. The failure mode is human-facing CLI review UX losing visibility into the canonical identifier the PR makes load-bearing, especially relevant when:

- `normalizeProposalServices` auto-bumps to `-2`/`-3` (the admin can't tell which slug from CLI review alone).
- A delete proposal targets a service whose Name differs from its Host (a legitimate case once operators start using explicit slug-style names).
- The web UI and CLI now diverge on data the PR makes canonical.

### How to fix

One-line change at cmd/proposal.go:52, mirroring the ProposalPreview.tsx pattern:

```go
if r.Name != "" {
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s %s %s", actionMarker(string(r.Action)), r.Name, mutedText(r.MatcherPattern()))
} else {
    fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %s %s", actionMarker(string(r.Action)), r.MatcherPattern())
}
```

This prepends Name when present (matching the web UI's "Name above Host" structure) and falls back gracefully for legacy pre-PR proposals where Name was optional. The `mutedText` wrapping the host pattern echoes the existing convention used elsewhere in this file for secondary metadata (e.g. credential descriptions at line 84).

</details>

🔴 Approving any proposal on a pre-PR vault panics the request goroutine. Legacy services persisted before this PR have `Name=""` (the field is new in this diff), and `MergeServices`'s new guards (merge.go:15-25) fire on the first existing entry. The PR description claims "Legacy services are normalized lazily on read," but `broker.NormalizeServices` and `broker.Slugify` don't exist anywhere in this codebase — `loadServices` (handle_services.go:134-150) only applies `SplitInlineHost`, never backfilling Name. Fix: implement the missing normalizer and call it in `loadServices` so existing entries are backfilled before reaching `MergeServices`, or replace the panic with a returned error surfaced as a 500 with a migration message. The Web UI's PUT-services edit path is also broken for the same root cause (`broker.Validate` hard-rejects empty Name at broker.go:374-376), so operators have no in-product remediation.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

Legacy services persisted before this PR have no `Name` field on the struct (the diff shows `Description *string` being removed and `Name string` being added on `broker.Service`). When `json.Unmarshal` runs against a pre-PR `services_json` row, every legacy entry materialises with `Name=""`. This PR adds new panic guards at the top of `proposal.MergeServices` (merge.go:15-25):

```go
for i, s := range existing {
    if s.Name == "" {
        panic(fmt.Sprintf("proposal.MergeServices: existing[%d] has empty Name (host=%q)", i, s.Host))
    }
}
for i, p := range proposed {
    if p.Name == "" {
        panic(fmt.Sprintf("proposal.MergeServices: proposed[%d] has empty Name (host=%q, action=%q)", i, p.Host, p.Action))
    }
}
```

The PR description and the docstring on `MergeServices` both say "callers must normalize before MergeServices" / "Legacy services are normalized lazily on read." That contract is unimplemented.

### The missing helpers

`grep -rn 'NormalizeServices\|Slugify'` across the entire repository (Go, MDX, MD, TS, TSX) returns zero matches. The PR description, several review comments, and the docstring on `MergeServices` reference these helpers as if they exist, but only the call sites that depend on them landed — not the helpers themselves. Functions actually present in `internal/broker/broker.go` are `Validate`, `MatchService`, `ValidateSlug`, `ValidatePath`, `ValidateHost`, `SplitInlineHost`. None of them backfill `Name`.

### The specific code path that triggers it

`handleAdminProposalApprove` (handle_proposals.go:478-493) runs:

1. `existingServices, err := s.loadServices(ctx, ns.ID)` — returns legacy entries with `Name=""`.
2. `proposedServices, err = normalizeProposalServices(proposedServices, existingServices)` — only fills `Name` for `ActionDelete` (handle_services.go:71-83); `ActionSet` entries with empty `Name` pass through unchanged. Even on `ActionDelete`, when the matched existing service is legacy, the adopted `Name` is still `""`.
3. `merged, _ := proposal.MergeServices(existingServices, proposedServices)` — panics on the first iteration of the first guard loop at merge.go:17, before any merge work happens.

I verified `loadServices` end-to-end: it calls `GetBrokerConfig`, unmarshals into `[]broker.Service`, applies `SplitInlineHost` per entry, returns. No name normalization step exists. I verified no migration was added — `internal/store/migrations/` ends at `045_no_access_role.sql`; nothing touches `broker_configs.services_json`. I verified there is no `recover()` anywhere in `internal/server/`, so Go's net/http default panic handler closes the connection and the operator sees a 500 / dropped connection with the stack trace in logs.

### Step-by-step proof (legacy vault)

1. Operator upgrades to this PR. Vault holds `[{"host":"api.stripe.com","auth":{...}}, {"host":"*.github.com","auth":{...}}]` from before — JSON has no `"name"` key.
2. Agent submits a fresh proposal post-upgrade with a valid Name field: `{"services":[{"action":"set","name":"slack-bot","host":"slack.com","auth":{...}}], ...}`. Create succeeds.
3. Admin clicks Approve. `handleAdminProposalApprove` runs. `loadServices` returns the two legacy entries, both with `Name=""`. `normalizeProposalServices` returns the proposed slice unchanged (the new entry already has `Name="slack-bot"`).
4. `proposal.MergeServices(existingServices, proposedServices)` enters the first guard loop. At `i=0`, `existing[0].Name == ""` — panic fires with `proposal.MergeServices: existing[0] has empty Name (host="api.stripe.com")`.
5. The goroutine's stack trace gets dropped to logs; net/http's connection handler catches it and the operator sees a connection drop / 500. The proposal cannot be approved — there is no UI workaround.

### Web UI breakage (same root cause)

The Web UI's PUT-services edit flow is also fully broken for legacy vaults. `GET /v1/vaults/{name}/services` returns legacy entries with `name=""` because the read path doesn't backfill either. Saving any edit via the ServicesTab modal triggers `PUT /services` with the full list (ServicesTab.tsx:saveServices), which calls `broker.Validate` server-side — and broker.go:374-376 hard-rejects every empty-Name entry: `return fmt.Errorf("service %d: name is required", i)`. Operators cannot edit a single service without first manually filling Names for *every* legacy service. There is no UI path that backfills automatically.

### Why this is normal severity and how to fix

Severity is normal (not critical) because Go's `net/http` catches the panic at the connection level so the process keeps running, and brand-new installs with no legacy data are unaffected. But the trigger is a routine operator action (approve a proposal) on the headline data shape this PR claims to support, and there is no in-product remediation path. The fix the PR description implies is missing: implement `Slugify(host, path)` (a deterministic, idempotent slug builder) plus `NormalizeServices(svcs []Service) []Service` that backfills `Name = Slugify(Host, Path)` (with collision-bumping if needed) for any entry with empty Name, and call it in `loadServices` so every read path produces normalized entries. Alternatively/additionally: replace the `panic` in `MergeServices` with a returned error, and have the apply path surface it as a 500 with a clear migration message — at least no crash. The first option restores the documented "lazy normalization on read" contract; the second is a defense-in-depth backstop for the data-loss class concern the panic docstring cites.

</details>

🟡 The TypeScript SDK type `ServiceInput.name` at sdks/sdk-typescript/src/resources/services.ts:99 is declared `name?: string` (optional), but the JSDoc literally one line above says "Required on write" and the server hard-rejects missing Name with 400 (`broker.Validate` at internal/broker/broker.go:353-355: `service N: name is required`). A TypeScript user can write `vault.services!.set([{host:"api.stripe.com", auth:{...}}])` and `tsc --strict` compiles cleanly — the runtime failure is the first signal. The same mismatch exists on `WireService.name` at sdks/sdk-typescript/src/types.ts:108-109. Fix: drop the `?` on both interfaces so the type matches the contract.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

The SDK exports two write-side types whose `name` field is optional in the type system but mandatory at runtime:

- `ServiceInput.name?: string` at sdks/sdk-typescript/src/resources/services.ts:99 — the JSDoc directly above on line 98 says **"Required on write"**. This is the write shape consumed by `ServicesResource.set()` and `replaceAll()`.
- `WireService.name?: string` at sdks/sdk-typescript/src/types.ts:108-109 — the JSDoc says "Required on write — pick deliberately; the server does not derive it from `host`". This is the internal wire type.

The server enforces the contract hard at `broker.Validate` (internal/broker/broker.go:353-355):

```go
if s.Name == "" {
    return fmt.Errorf("service %d: name is required", i)
}
```

Surfaced by `handleServicesUpsert` as HTTP 400 with `Invalid services: service 0: name is required`.

### Why it matters

Every other write-required field on `ServiceInput` is non-optional in the type — `host: string`, `auth: ServiceAuth`. Optional fields are correctly typed optional — `enabled?`, `substitutions?`. The lone outlier is `name?`, where prose says required but the type system says optional. TypeScript strict mode protects against typos in object literals (e.g. the `description` excess-property error users hit), but it cannot protect against a field whose own type signature permits omission.

### Step-by-step proof

1. TypeScript user installs `@infisical/agent-vault-sdk@0.2.0`, opens `ServiceInput` in their IDE, sees `name?: string`.
2. Following the visible type, they write:
   ```ts
   await vault.services!.set([{
     host: "api.stripe.com",
     auth: { type: "bearer", token: "STRIPE_KEY" },
   }]);
   ```
3. `tsc --strict` compiles cleanly — `name?` permits omission.
4. SDK marshals `{services:[{host:"api.stripe.com",auth:{...}}]}` and POSTs to `/v1/vaults/{name}/services`.
5. Server `handleServicesUpsert` runs `broker.Validate(&incoming)`. At broker.go:353 the check fires.
6. Server returns HTTP 400 `{"error":"Invalid services: service 0: name is required"}`.
7. The user got no compile-time signal — only a runtime 400 on a field they were never told they had to fill in.

### Why the JSDoc is not enough

JSDoc renders in IDE hover tooltips but does not constrain the build. The strict-mode excess-property check that catches typos on the user-supplied side does NOT engage for missing optional fields. The type system is what users trust; the JSDoc is the second source of truth at best.

### Why this is nit, not normal

The runtime behavior is correct (server returns a clear 400 with an actionable message), no data loss, no security risk. But this is the v0.2.0 release whose headline feature is exactly "name is canonical" — the SDK's type system is the first line of error feedback for users adopting the new model, and a self-contradicting type signature on the canonical write method undermines the migration story this release exists to deliver. Fix is one character per location.

### How to fix

Drop the `?` in both files:

```diff
 // sdks/sdk-typescript/src/resources/services.ts:99
-  name?: string;
+  name: string;

 // sdks/sdk-typescript/src/types.ts:109
-  name?: string;
+  name: string;
```

Existing callers that supply name are unaffected. Callers omitting name now fail at compile time with `TS2741: Property 'name' is missing in type '{ host: string; auth: ...; }' but required in type 'ServiceInput'.` — immediate, actionable feedback matching the server contract.

</details>

🟡 The fallback error message printed when `vault proposal create` is invoked with no flags (cmd/proposal_create.go:86) shows an example that copies-and-pastes into an immediate failure: `--host api.example.com` is given without the now-required `--name` flag, so the user hits `--name is required when --host is specified` from buildFromFlags. The Long help block (lines 27-45) was correctly migrated to include `--name my-service` in every `--host` example; this parallel error-fallback string was missed. Fix is one token: insert `--name my-service ` before `--host` in the second example on line 86.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

### What the bug is

The error returned at `cmd/proposal_create.go:86` (when the user runs `agent-vault vault proposal create` with no `-f`, no `--host`, and no `--credential`) prints three examples to guide the user:

```
provide either --host/--credential flags or -f <file>

Examples:
  agent-vault vault proposal create --credential MY_KEY="description" --message "reason"
  agent-vault vault proposal create --host api.example.com --auth-type bearer --token-key MY_KEY --credential MY_KEY --message "reason"
  agent-vault vault proposal create -f proposal.json
```

The second example is broken on this PR: it sets `--host api.example.com` but omits `--name`. This PR introduced a hard requirement in `buildFromFlags` (cmd/proposal_create.go:194-197):

```go
name, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("name")
if name == "" {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("--name is required when --host is specified")
}
```

A user who copies the example verbatim hits this check immediately and gets an error referencing a flag that was not in the help they just read.

### Why existing code does not prevent it

The Long help block at cmd/proposal_create.go:27-45 was correctly updated in this PR to include `--name` in every `--host` example (e.g. `--name stripe --host api.stripe.com`, `--name slack-bot --host 'slack.com/api/*'`). The author was aware of the new requirement and migrated the canonical docs surface — but missed this second string constant at line 86, which is a separate piece of inline text only visible when the user provides no flags at all. The asymmetry between two places in the same file is concrete evidence this is an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

### Step-by-step proof

1. User runs `agent-vault vault proposal create` with no flags.
2. Lines 79-86 hit the `else` branch (no `filePath`, no `host`, no `credentials`), returning the error string at line 86.
3. User reads the output and copies the second example verbatim: `agent-vault vault proposal create --host api.example.com --auth-type bearer --token-key MY_KEY --credential MY_KEY --message "reason"`.
4. The new invocation reaches `buildFromFlags` (cmd/proposal_create.go:164), which builds the auth config and then runs the `--name` check at line 194-197.
5. `cmd.Flags().GetString("name")` returns `""` (the flag was never passed); buildFromFlags returns `--name is required when --host is specified`.
6. The proposal create aborts; the user sees an error about a flag that was not present in the example they just copied.

### Impact

Documentation-only — no runtime regression, no data loss, no security risk. Severity is **nit** because the user gets a clear error and can recover by adding `--name`.
