🟡 The new 400 `external_store_layout_conflict` code returned by `POST /v1/vaults` (handle_vaults.go:479-481, introduced in commit a3f9b35) is not mentioned in the operator-facing `POST /v1/vaults` bullets in `cmd/skill_http.md:156` or `cmd/skill_cli.md:191-200`, even though both files already enumerate the sibling `infisical_not_configured` (503), `infisical_fetch_failed` (502), `external_credential_store` (409), and the new 403 owner-only gate. Per CLAUDE.md:46, the skill-file pair must be updated together when response codes change; fix is one bullet per file (and ideally a matching note about the `--infisical-recursive` duplicate-key caveat in `docs/learn/credential-stores.mdx` and `docs/reference/cli.mdx`). Pure documentation completeness — the section is explicitly labeled informational, no functional impact.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is missing

Commit a3f9b35 ("infisical: cancellable FetchSecrets; distinguish layout conflict; trim config; skip sql.ErrNoRows warn") added a new agent-facing 400 response code to `POST /v1/vaults`. `internal/server/handle_vaults.go:478-481` returns:

```go
if errors.Is(err, infisical.ErrLayoutConflict) {
    jsonCodedError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "external_store_layout_conflict", err.Error())
    return
}
```

The same commit also persists the wrapped message into `vault_credential_stores.last_sync_error` via the carve-out in `internal/infisical/sync.go:206-209`.

The PR's new "Vaults backed by an external credential store" section in `cmd/skill_http.md:144-156` documents this endpoint with a bullet that enumerates every other failure code — `infisical_not_configured` (503), `infisical_fetch_failed` (502), the 403 owner-only gate, and `external_credential_store` (409) for mutations — but never mentions the new 400 layout-conflict code. The matching section in `cmd/skill_cli.md:191-200` has the same gap. Grepping the repo confirms `external_store_layout_conflict` appears only in `internal/server/handle_vaults.go`; no docs or skill file references it.

## Why the convention requires the update

CLAUDE.md:46 is explicit: *"When the agent-facing surface changes (endpoints, request/response fields, auth behavior), update both cmd/skill_cli.md and cmd/skill_http.md together — they are versioned as a pair."* The new 400 is a response-field change. The author already followed this convention for the analogous 403 owner-only gate (documented in both skill files in this same PR series), so the precedent for enumerating new error codes alongside their siblings in this bullet is locked in. The skill update for this commit stopped one bullet short.

## How an agent encounters the gap

An agent that has been told about an Infisical-backed project laid out per-service (e.g. `/stripe/API_KEY` + `/openai/API_KEY`, an idiomatic Infisical layout) may attempt vault creation with `recursive=true`. `flattenSecrets` at `internal/infisical/client.go:131-141` will reject the duplicate-key shape with `ErrLayoutConflict`, the handler returns 400 with `code=external_store_layout_conflict`, and the agent has no signal in its instruction set explaining the cause. The same gap exists in `docs/learn/credential-stores.mdx` (no caveat in the recursive section) and `docs/reference/cli.mdx:198` (`--infisical-recursive` flag documented without the flat-key-value constraint).

## Addressing the duplicate refutation

The refutation flagged this as a duplicate of bug_002 (refuted) and argued that since this endpoint is labeled "Operator-facing endpoints (informational, not used in the agent hot path)" in `skill_http.md:153`, the omission isn't blocking. That mitigation is real — a well-behaved agent following hot-path guidance won't typically call this endpoint, so the impact is small. But it doesn't refute the underlying CLAUDE.md:46 convention, and it doesn't address the asymmetry that the same PR enumerates 503/502/403 for the very same bullet while omitting the 400. The fix is one line per skill file and the asymmetry was introduced atomically by commit a3f9b35; closing it here costs less than carrying it as known debt.

## Step-by-step proof

1. `handle_vaults.go:479-481` returns `jsonCodedError(http.StatusBadRequest, "external_store_layout_conflict", err.Error())` when `FetchSecrets` returns `infisical.ErrLayoutConflict`. Verified directly.
2. `sync.go:206-209` persists the same wrapped message into `last_sync_error` (separate carve-out from the scrubbed generic).
3. `cmd/skill_http.md:156` enumerates `infisical_not_configured` (503), `infisical_fetch_failed` (502), and the 403 owner-only gate for this same `POST /v1/vaults` bullet — no mention of `external_store_layout_conflict`.
4. `cmd/skill_cli.md:191-200` documents the read-only consequences and the owner-only gate but does not mention `external_store_layout_conflict`.
5. Grep across the repo for `external_store_layout_conflict` returns one hit (the Go file). Zero hits in any `.md` or `.mdx` file.
6. CLAUDE.md:46 requires both skill files to be updated together on response-code changes; the convention is unmet for this code.

## Fix

Add one bullet to each of `skill_http.md` (under the existing `POST /v1/vaults` enumeration at line 156) and `skill_cli.md` (under the analogous section around line 191-200), e.g.:

> `{"code": "external_store_layout_conflict", ...}` (400, when `--infisical-recursive=true` pulls two secrets with the same key under different sub-paths). Agent Vault vaults are flat key-value and cannot disambiguate; resolve by narrowing `secret_path` or renaming the upstream key.

While in the area, add the same caveat to the `--infisical-recursive` description in `docs/learn/credential-stores.mdx` and `docs/reference/cli.mdx` (around line 198) so the constraint is discoverable from human-facing surfaces too. No security or functional impact; severity nit.

</details>

🔴 🔴 handleVaultSyncNow (handle_vaults.go:113-180) calls s.requireVaultAccess(w, r, vault.ID), which has two compounding problems. (1) requireVaultAccess returns (nil, nil) for scoped sessions whose sess.VaultID matches the requested vault (server.go:454-460), and the success path at lines 174-175 unconditionally dereferences actor.ID and actor.IsOwner() — guaranteed runtime panic on every scoped-session sync that lands the credential commit. (2) requireVaultAccess also admits proxy-role grants and any scoped session with no role check at all, contradicting the handler comment 'Any vault member; broker identity authorizes upstream' and the matching cmd/skill_http.md documentation. One-line fix that closes both: replace s.requireVaultAccess with s.requireVaultMember — it returns a non-nil actor for both instance and scoped sessions and enforces member+, mirroring how handleVaultContext is gated.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

This handler combines two issues that were introduced together by the same auth-gate choice. Both are closed by the same one-line fix (switching to `requireVaultMember`), so they read most naturally as one finding.

### 1. Nil-deref panic on the success path

`handleVaultSyncNow` at `internal/server/handle_vaults.go:122-124`:

```go
actor, err := s.requireVaultAccess(w, r, vault.ID)
if err != nil {
    return
}
```

`requireVaultAccess` at `server.go:446-480` returns `(nil, nil)` for scoped sessions whose `sess.VaultID` matches the requested vault:

```go
if sess.VaultID != "" {
    if sess.VaultID != vaultID { ... return nil, fmt.Errorf("vault mismatch") }
    return nil, nil // scoped session, no actor resolved
}
```

The `if err != nil { return }` guard does not catch the nil actor, so execution continues into the response-building branch at lines 174-175:

```go
vaultRole, _ := s.store.GetVaultRole(ctx, actor.ID, vault.ID)
if vaultRole != "admin" && !actor.IsOwner() {
```

`actor.ID` is a struct-field access on `*Actor`; `Actor.IsOwner` at server.go:319 is `func (a *Actor) IsOwner() bool { return a.Role == "owner" }`. Both dereference the nil pointer and panic.

### 2. Auth gate is broader than the documented intent

`requireVaultAccess` admits any `vault_grants` row including proxy role for instance-level sessions, and any scoped session matching the vault with **no role check at all** (lines 454-460). The handler header at line 112 says `Any vault member; broker identity authorizes upstream`, and the new `cmd/skill_http.md` section describes this endpoint the same way. `requireVaultMember` at server.go:538+ is the helper that actually enforces member+ for both session classes; `requireVaultAccess` does not.

Proxy-role scoped sessions are the default agent session shape per migration 035, and `handle_sessions.go:78` confirms that's the agent hot-path token. The endpoint as written lets those agent tokens force serial upstream refreshes through the operator's machine identity.

## Step-by-step proof of the panic

1. Route registration at server.go:746: `mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync", s.requireInitialized(s.requireAuth(actorAuthed(s.handleVaultSyncNow))))`. `actorAuthed` is rate-limit middleware (server.go:687), not a session-type filter. `requireAuth` accepts scoped sessions.
2. An agent holds a scoped session created against a healthy Infisical-backed vault `demo` (sess.VaultID = demo's ID). It POSTs to `/v1/vaults/demo/sync`.
3. `handleVaultSyncNow` looks up the vault, then calls `requireVaultAccess(w, r, vault.ID)`. sess.VaultID matches vault.ID, so the function returns `(nil, nil)` per server.go:459.
4. `if err != nil { return }` — err is nil, control continues. actor is nil.
5. `s.store.GetVaultCredentialStore(...)` returns the existing row. `s.infisicalSyncer.RefreshOnce(ctx, *cs)` runs and **succeeds** — credentials get committed to the local store via `ReplaceVaultCredentials`. No early return before the response-building branch.
6. `cs, err = s.store.GetVaultCredentialStore(...)` re-reads the row. cs is non-nil.
7. `summary := credentialStoreSummaryOf(cs, true)`.
8. `vaultRole, _ := s.store.GetVaultRole(ctx, actor.ID, vault.ID)` — **panic**: `actor.ID` is a struct-field access on a nil `*Actor`.

Go's net/http recovers from handler panics so the server stays up, but the client gets a connection abort, the credential write side-effect already happened (so retries stack writes), and every scoped-session sync request pollutes the operator's logs with a panic stack.

## Why `handleVaultContext` doesn't hit this

The sibling handler `handleVaultContext` at handle_vaults.go:66-109 uses `requireActor` (always returns a non-nil actor on success), which is why the exact same redaction block at lines 102-108 is safe there. The new endpoint added in this PR copy-pasted the redaction block but picked a different auth helper.

## How to fix

Smallest correct fix is one line. Replace requireVaultAccess with requireVaultMember at handle_vaults.go:123:

```go
actor, err := s.requireVaultMember(w, r, vault.ID)
```

That closes both issues at once:
- `requireVaultMember` returns a non-nil actor for scoped sessions (it resolves `actorFromSession` and then checks roleSatisfies). The redaction block at lines 174-175 stays safe.
- It enforces member+ for both scoped and instance-level sessions via `roleSatisfies(role, "member")`, rejecting proxy-role tokens — aligning the code with the handler comment and the skill docs, and mirroring how proposal/credential mutations are gated for member+ actions elsewhere in this PR.

A unit test seeding a scoped session against an Infisical-backed vault and asserting 200/403 (not panic, not 500-with-recovered-stack) would prevent the regression.

</details>

🟡 On clean shutdown the success branch of `refresh` still emits a misleading `updating health=ok failed err=context canceled` Warn per in-flight vault, because the `!errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows)` guard at sync.go:211 was not extended to also filter `context.Canceled` the way the recordFailure carve-out at sync.go:247-251 does. Pure log noise (credentials were persisted by ReplaceVaultCredentials before this UPDATE; the next post-restart tick relabels health), but the asymmetry was introduced by this PR's own carve-out fix and is closed by one extra `errors.Is` check on the same line.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

Commit a3f9b35 added the `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` early-return at the top of `recordFailure` (sync.go:247-251) so that a refresh whose `FetchSecrets` was parked on the new ctx-aware select returns quietly during shutdown instead of emitting `infisical sync failed err=context canceled` plus a follow-up `updating health=error failed err=context canceled`. That fix lands on the **failure** branch only. The success branch at sync.go:211 — which fires after `ReplaceVaultCredentials` has already committed the snapshot — still reads:

```go
if err := s.Store.UpdateVaultCredentialStoreHealth(ctx, cs.VaultID, StatusOK, "", s.Clock()); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
    s.Logger.Warn("updating health=ok failed", ...)
}
```

Only `sql.ErrNoRows` is filtered. `database/sql` short-circuits an `ExecContext` against a canceled ctx by returning `ctx.Err() = context.Canceled` from its upfront `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() }` (before acquiring a connection), so the UPDATE never reaches sqlite — the Warn fires with `err=context canceled`.

## Why it is reachable

The `ctx` threaded into `refresh` is `pruneCtx`, which `Server.Start` cancels via `stopWorkers()` on shutdown (server.go). A refresh that has just returned from `ReplaceVaultCredentials` (i.e. the credentials have already been committed) but has not yet dispatched the final `UpdateVaultCredentialStoreHealth` observes the cancel between those two calls — a small window (microseconds between two DB calls) but reachable on every shutdown sequence where a refresh was already through the bulk of its work. The same shutdown scenario that motivated the recordFailure carve-out triggers this one, just on the success side.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Infisical-backed vault `demo`, poll interval 60s. The 10s syncer tick fires, becomes due, spawns a refresh goroutine. `FetchSecrets` completes in ~200ms, `EncryptSecrets` is in-memory, `ReplaceVaultCredentials` opens its own `BeginTx` and commits successfully — the new snapshot is on disk.
2. Between `ReplaceVaultCredentials` returning nil and the next `UpdateVaultCredentialStoreHealth` call, the operator sends SIGINT. `Start`’s shutdown path runs `stopWorkers()`, which cancels `pruneCtx`.
3. `refresh` reaches sync.go:211 with the still-canceled ctx. `database/sql.ExecContext` does an upfront ctx-cancellation check, returns `context.Canceled`. `errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows)` is false; the Warn fires: `WARN updating health=ok failed vault_id=demo-vault-id err="context canceled"`.
4. Syncer’s `defer s.wg.Wait()` releases, `Start` proceeds to wipe the DEK, exits cleanly. The Warn line stays in the operator’s log.

## Impact

Pure log noise. The credentials were persisted by `ReplaceVaultCredentials` before this UPDATE attempted to run, so the on-disk state is correct; only the `last_synced_at` / `last_sync_status` row is missed, and the next syncer tick after restart writes them. No security, correctness, or data impact. The harm is that a Warn-level line appears on every clean shutdown of a healthy deployment, eroding the signal value of WARN-level logs and potentially prompting an on-call to chase a phantom failure — exactly the concern that motivated the recordFailure carve-out.

## How to fix

One-line extension to mirror the recordFailure pattern. At sync.go:211:

```go
if err := s.Store.UpdateVaultCredentialStoreHealth(ctx, cs.VaultID, StatusOK, "", s.Clock()); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) && !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
    s.Logger.Warn("updating health=ok failed", ...)
}
```

A short test that calls `refresh` with a canceled ctx (after `ReplaceVaultCredentials` returns ok) and asserts no `updating health=ok failed` Warn fires would lock the symmetric behavior in.

</details>

🟡 After a successful click on Manual sync, the rest of the UI keeps showing stale credential-store metadata: SettingsTab's last-sync timestamp/status and the home-page vault pill both read `credentialStore` from the route loader (router.tsx:279-286, loaded once on navigation), which `handleSyncNow` never invalidates. The server returns the post-refresh `credential_store` summary in the response body (handle_vaults.go:179) but `handleSyncNow` (CredentialsTab.tsx:56-75) discards it and only calls `fetchKeys()`, so the operator gets no confirmation that the sync actually ran on any surface other than the keys list. The failure path is the same shape — SettingsTab's `last_sync_error` ErrorBanner shows the prior value across syncs. Smallest fix: `router.invalidate()` after a 200, or consume `resp.json().credential_store` and propagate through route context.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

`handleSyncNow` at `web/src/pages/vault/CredentialsTab.tsx:56-75` posts to `/v1/vaults/{name}/sync` and on success only calls `fetchKeys()` to refresh the credential keys list. The response body — `handle_vaults.go:179` returns `jsonOK(w, map[string]interface{}{"credential_store": summary})` with the post-refresh `last_synced_at`, `last_sync_status`, and `last_sync_error` — is discarded.

The rest of the UI reads `credentialStore` from the route loader. `useVaultParams()` at `web/src/pages/vault/shared.tsx:14-24` returns `credential_store` from `useRouteContext`, which is loaded once by `vaultLayoutRoute.beforeLoad` at `router.tsx:279-286` (`/v1/vaults/{name}/context`). Three consumers all read this stale value:

- `SettingsTab.tsx` `CredentialStoreSection` renders `timeAgo(credentialStore.last_synced_at)` and `credentialStore.last_sync_error` directly from the prop.
- `web/src/pages/home/VaultsListTab.tsx` derives the `CredentialStorePill` status dot + tooltip from the same field on `GET /v1/vaults`.
- `ProposalsTab.tsx` keys its read-only banner off `credentialStore.kind`.

Nothing in `handleSyncNow` calls `router.invalidate()` or otherwise re-runs the loader, so the route context never sees the post-sync state.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Operator opens a vault's Credentials tab. Vault is Infisical-backed; SettingsTab shows "Last sync: ok" + "5 minutes ago".
2. Operator rotates a secret upstream and clicks Manual sync.
3. POST `/v1/vaults/{name}/sync` succeeds; server runs `RefreshOnce`, commits the refreshed snapshot via `ReplaceVaultCredentials`, updates `vault_credential_stores.last_synced_at` to now via `UpdateVaultCredentialStoreHealth`, returns 200 with the post-refresh `credential_store` summary in the body.
4. `handleSyncNow` ignores `resp.json()`, calls `fetchKeys()`. The keys list refreshes (proxy hot path is now fresh).
5. Operator switches to SettingsTab. `useVaultParams()` returns the unchanged `credentialStore` from the route context loaded in step 1; SettingsTab still renders "Last sync: ok / 5 minutes ago".
6. Same on the home-page vault pill — tooltip still reads "Last synced 5 minutes ago". Only a full route reload (back-and-forth nav, hard refresh) re-runs `beforeLoad` and refreshes the display.

The failure path is worse: if the upstream sync hits `ErrInvalidKey`, the server returns 400 and writes `last_sync_error` via the syncer's failure path. The operator sees the per-request error banner that `setSyncError` renders, but SettingsTab's persistent `ErrorBanner` keeps showing whatever `last_sync_error` was at navigation time — staleness across both success and failure transitions.

## Why this matters specifically for this PR

The manual-sync button was added in this same PR for a single reason: give operators an "I just rotated a secret upstream" affordance with immediate freshness feedback. The Credentials tab itself does not render `last_synced_at` at all — the only place that timestamp shows up is SettingsTab and the home-page pill, both of which are now exactly the surfaces the button doesn't refresh. The feature ships its data path correctly but the user-facing freshness display is one route-context invalidation short of working end-to-end.

## Impact

Pure UX freshness — the sync itself works, credentials are committed before the response returns, and the next proxied request reads the fresh snapshot. No security or correctness impact. Filing as **nit** per verifier consensus.

## How to fix

Smallest correct fix is one line — call `router.invalidate()` after a successful sync so the loader re-runs:

```tsx
import { useRouter } from "@tanstack/react-router";
// ...
const router = useRouter();
// ...
if (!resp.ok) { ... }
await Promise.all([fetchKeys(), router.invalidate()]);
```

Alternative: consume `resp.json().credential_store` and surface a setter from `useVaultParams` that updates the local view. The first option is the smaller change and aligns with how TanStack Router expects loader-backed data to be refreshed.

</details>

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+---
+title: "Credential stores"
+description: "Where a vault's credentials come from: Agent Vault's local DB, or an external system like Infisical."
+---
+
+A **credential store** describes where a vault's [credentials](/learn/credentials) live. Every vault has exactly one credential store, chosen at create time. The kind is immutable; to move a vault between stores, create a new vault and update agents and services to point at it.
+
+There are two kinds:
+
+- **Built-in** (default): Credentials live in Agent Vault's local SQLite database, encrypted at rest with the data encryption key (DEK). Operators add, edit, and delete credentials through the CLI, HTTP API, or browser UI. Agents request new credentials via [proposals](/learn/proposals).
+- **Infisical**: Credentials live in an [Infisical](https://infisical.com) instance. Agent Vault polls Infisical at a per-vault cadence, caches the encrypted snapshot locally, and serves it to proxied requests. The cached values are encrypted with the **same** DEK as built-in credentials, so the at-rest threat model is identical. Local mutations are rejected; Infisical is the source of truth.
+
+## How injection works
+
+Injection is unchanged across kinds. The proxy reads from the local `credentials` table and decrypts with the DEK at request time. For Infisical-backed vaults, the sync worker (not the proxy) is what populates that table from upstream.
+
+## Choosing a kind at create time
+
+```bash
+# Built-in (default)
+agent-vault vault create my-app
+
+# Infisical-backed
+agent-vault vault create my-app \
+  --credential-store=infisical \
+  --infisical-project-id=abc123 \
+  --infisical-environment=dev \
+  --infisical-path=/stripe \
+  --poll-interval-seconds=60
+```
+
+The create handler probes Infisical first. If the project, environment, or path doesn't resolve, or if the machine identity can't read it, the request fails with a clear error and the vault is **not** created. On success, the vault row, the credential-store config, the initial encrypted secret snapshot, and your admin grant are all committed in a single SQL transaction.
+
+To inspect a vault's credential store later:
+
+```bash
+agent-vault vault credential-store show my-app
+```
+
+## Outage behavior
+
+If a sync to Infisical fails (network blip, auth-token rotation, upstream 5xx), Agent Vault keeps serving the last good snapshot. The vault's `last_sync_status` flips to `error` and the short error message surfaces in the CLI and UI, but proxied requests continue to work with stale credentials.
+
+There is no automatic fail-closed window. The poll interval is fixed at create time. If you need stricter freshness on an existing vault, recreate it with a lower `--poll-interval-seconds`; for new vaults, pick the smaller cadence up front.
+
+Unsetting `INFISICAL_URL` and restarting Agent Vault leaves existing Infisical-backed vaults intact: the syncer never starts, but every vault keeps serving its cached snapshot indefinitely. Writes still 409. To force-clear secret residue, delete the vault: `vaults` deletes cascade to credentials, credential-store rows, and request logs through SQLite foreign keys.

🟡 User-facing docs at `docs/learn/credential-stores.mdx` omit three operator surfaces that this PR added: (1) the manual sync endpoint (`POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync`) and the matching CredentialsTab 'Manual sync' button — the Outage behavior section still frames freshness as a create-time-only decision (`recreate it with a lower --poll-interval-seconds`); (2) the UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constraint enforced by `EncryptSecrets` at `internal/infisical/sync.go:235`, which fails sync/create with `external_store_invalid_key` for idiomatic Infisical names like `database-url` or `stripeKey`; (3) the all-or-nothing behavior — one invalid key drops the entire snapshot and the vault keeps serving stale until renamed upstream. The skill files (`cmd/skill_cli.md:194-200`, `cmd/skill_http.md:144-157`) cover the first two for agents; the human-facing reference does not.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What is missing

This PR adds three operator-facing surfaces that `docs/learn/credential-stores.mdx` does not document, even though the file is the canonical reference for the credential-store feature (linked from `docs/learn/credentials.mdx` and indexed in `docs/docs.json`).

### 1. Manual sync endpoint and UI button

`POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync` is registered at `internal/server/server.go:746` and handled by `handleVaultSyncNow` (`internal/server/handle_vaults.go:113`); the CredentialsTab in `web/src/pages/vault/CredentialsTab.tsx` renders a 'Manual sync' button (handleSyncNow at lines 56-74). Both let any vault member force a refresh on demand, outside the poll cadence.

The doc's Outage behavior section (line 44) still reads: *"If you need stricter freshness on an existing vault, recreate it with a lower `--poll-interval-seconds`."* The recreate-the-vault advice is actively misleading now: a rotated upstream secret can be pulled in via manual sync without destroying agents, services, or grants.

### 2. UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constraint on upstream keys

`EncryptSecrets` at `internal/infisical/sync.go:235` enforces `broker.CredentialKeyPattern` (`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`) on every upstream key, returning `ErrInvalidKey` on the first violation. The handler propagates that as `400 external_store_invalid_key` on create (`internal/server/handle_vaults.go:563`) and persists the verbatim message into `last_sync_error` on steady-state sync (sync.go:255-259).

`credential-stores.mdx` walks operators through create at lines 19-32 with an example pointing at `/stripe` — exactly the kind of Infisical path under which lowercase/hyphenated names like `database-url` and `stripeKey` are idiomatic. An operator with such a project hits the error on first sync with no warning in the user-facing reference. The skill docs at `cmd/skill_cli.md:199` already mention it for agents.

### 3. All-or-nothing batch failure

`EncryptSecrets` returns on the first invalid key (sync.go:236), dropping the whole batch — no partial sync. `ReplaceVaultCredentials` is never called, so the vault keeps serving the previous snapshot until the operator renames the upstream secret. The Outage behavior section at lines 40-46 covers network failures and serve-stale, but not this distinct failure mode where a single bad key blocks the entire snapshot.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Operator has an Infisical project with secrets at `/stripe/api-key` (hyphenated) and `/stripe/STRIPE_SECRET`.
2. They run `agent-vault vault create demo --credential-store=infisical --infisical-project-id=p --infisical-environment=prod --infisical-path=/stripe`, following the docs example at lines 19-32.
3. `createExternalVault` calls `FetchSecrets`, which succeeds. `EncryptSecrets` iterates the slice. On `api-key`, `broker.CredentialKeyPattern.MatchString("api-key")` is false; `ErrInvalidKey` is wrapped and returned.
4. The handler at `handle_vaults.go:563` returns `400 external_store_invalid_key` with a message naming the offending key. Nothing is persisted (transaction not even opened).
5. Operator sees a 400 they didn't expect from the doc walkthrough. They search the user-facing reference for 'UPPER_SNAKE_CASE' or 'invalid key' and find nothing. The only places that document the constraint are `cmd/skill_cli.md` and `cmd/skill_http.md` (agent-facing).

For the manual-sync gap: an operator with a healthy external vault rotates a secret upstream and wants to pull it in immediately. They open the docs, see the 'lower --poll-interval-seconds' advice, conclude they must recreate the vault. The Web UI's 'Manual sync' button on the Credentials tab would solve their problem in one click — but the docs don't mention it.

## Impact

Pure documentation completeness — no security, correctness, or functional impact. The system fails closed with clear error codes for the key-shape gap, and the manual-sync path is discoverable via the UI. But:

- The freshness advice at line 44 contradicts a feature introduced in this same PR; following it costs the operator a delete-and-recreate when a Manual sync button exists.
- The UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constraint is a near-certain first-encounter failure for any operator whose Infisical project predates Agent Vault.
- All three gaps were introduced atomically by this PR (the `infisical` package and this mdx file are both new), so the cheapest correction lands here.

## How to fix

Three additions to `docs/learn/credential-stores.mdx`:

- Add a one-paragraph note around line 11 (or in a new 'Naming requirements' subsection) covering UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for upstream secret keys, mirroring the existing `credentials.mdx` line 10 callout that documents the same pattern for built-in credentials. Note that one non-conforming key blocks the entire snapshot.
- Rewrite line 44 to describe `POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync` and the Credentials-tab 'Manual sync' button as the on-demand-freshness option. The recreate-the-vault wording can stay as a fallback for changing `--poll-interval-seconds` itself (which is genuinely create-time only).
- Add a short bullet in the Outage behavior section noting that an invalid upstream key produces `external_store_invalid_key` and the vault keeps serving the previous snapshot until the key is renamed upstream.

</details>

🟡 SettingsTab nests the `last_synced_at` / `last_sync_status` timestamp inside the `isInfisical && store?.config && (...)` block at SettingsTab.tsx:276-288. For non-admin/non-owner vault members on an external-store vault, `handleVaultContext` (handle_vaults.go:99-108) intentionally redacts only `Config` and `LastSyncError` while keeping `kind`, `poll_interval_seconds`, `last_sync_status`, and `last_synced_at` populated — so a non-admin member sees only "Credential store: Infisical" with no sync health, contradicting the server's deliberate field-by-field redaction. CLI `vault credential-store show` renders these fields independently of config, so this asymmetry is web-only; fix is to lift the `store.last_synced_at` row out of the `store?.config` conditional.
Extended reasoning... ## What the bug is `CredentialStoreSection` in `web/src/pages/vault/SettingsTab.tsx:269-298` builds the sync-status row inside a config-gated block: ```tsx {isInfisical && store?.config && ( <> {store.last_synced_at && ( )} )} ``` The `store.last_synced_at` row is nested **inside** the `store?.config` guard. When the server returns a `credential_store` payload without `config`, the whole inner fragment — including the timestamp at lines 281-286 — renders nothing. ## Why this matters with the server's redaction model `handleVaultContext` at `internal/server/handle_vaults.go:99-108` does a deliberate field-by-field redaction: ```go summary := credentialStoreDetailSummary(cs) if vaultRole != "admin" && !actor.IsOwner() { summary.Config = nil summary.LastSyncError = "" } resp["credential_store"] = summary ``` The comment one block up is explicit: *"Config and LastSyncError can both carry upstream topology (paths/keys); gate on the same role check that gates create."* `kind`, `poll_interval_seconds`, `last_sync_status`, and `last_synced_at` are **intentionally** left populated so non-admin vault members can still see whether the vault they rely on is healthy. The UI ignores that intent: by gating everything below the kind label on `store?.config` being truthy, the SettingsTab collapses the full informational payload to a single "Credential store: Infisical" line for any non-admin member. The CLI surface honors the server's intent. `cmd/vaults.go vaultCredentialStoreShowCmd` renders `last_sync_status`, `last_synced_at`, and `poll_interval_seconds` independently of the config map (each field is checked separately), so the asymmetry is web-only. ## Impact No security or correctness impact — the data already on the wire is the same shape; only the rendered output diverges. The cost is operator-confusion on the primary surface non-admin members use to learn whether their vault is healthy: an Infisical-backed vault stuck on `last_sync_status=error` for an hour looks identical to a freshly-synced healthy vault to anyone without admin role. Severity **nit**. ## Step-by-step proof 1. Operator (owner) creates an Infisical-backed vault `demo` and grants user Eve the `member` role on it. 2. The syncer runs successfully a few times; `last_synced_at` is fresh, `last_sync_status=ok`, the config_json is populated. 3. Eve opens the Settings tab. Browser issues `GET /v1/vaults/demo/context`. 4. `handleVaultContext` populates the summary, sees `vaultRole=='member'` && `!actor.IsOwner()`, redacts `summary.Config = nil` and `summary.LastSyncError = ""`. The other fields stay populated. 5. Response: `credential_store: {kind: "infisical", poll_interval_seconds: 60, last_sync_status: "ok", last_synced_at: "2026-05-25T..."}` — no `config`, no `last_sync_error`. 6. `CredentialStoreSection` renders. `store.config` is undefined, so `isInfisical && store?.config` is false, the inner fragment is skipped entirely. Eve sees one row: "Credential store: Infisical". No project, no environment, no path (correct — those are the topology being redacted), but **also** no sync status and no last-synced timestamp. 7. Truth on disk: the vault is healthy and synced a few seconds ago. Eve has no way to learn that from this tab. ## Fix One-line restructuring: lift the `store.last_synced_at` row out of the `store?.config` conditional. Project/Environment/Secret-path stay inside the config gate (they are the redacted topology); sync status and timestamp move alongside the kind label: ```tsx
{isInfisical && store?.config && ( <> )} {isInfisical && store?.last_synced_at && ( )}
``` A poll-interval row keyed off `store?.poll_interval_seconds` could move out alongside it for the same reason. No server, schema, or auth changes needed — the data is already on the response.

🟡 POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync returns the verbatim ErrInvalidKey message — which embeds the upstream secret key name (`infisical: upstream secret key does not match required pattern: "<KEY>" (...)`) — to any vault accessor (member, proxy, scoped session), while the same content is explicitly redacted from `last_sync_error` for non-admin/non-owner callers in handleVaultContext (handle_vaults.go:102-105) and on the matching sync success path (handle_vaults.go:175-178). Fix: mirror the role-based redaction on the ErrInvalidKey error branch — emit `err.Error()` only to admins/owners, return a scrubbed generic (e.g. "Sync failed: upstream key shape invalid (see server logs)") otherwise.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the bug is

`handleVaultSyncNow` at `internal/server/handle_vaults.go:153-154` returns the verbatim `ErrInvalidKey` message via `jsonCodedError`:

```go
case errors.Is(err, infisical.ErrInvalidKey):
    jsonCodedError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "external_store_invalid_key", err.Error())
```

The wrapped message is built at `internal/infisical/sync.go:236`:

```go
return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q (Agent Vault requires UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; rename the secret upstream)", ErrInvalidKey, sec.Key)
```

So the response body carries the offending upstream key name verbatim (`sec.Key` is interpolated through `%q`).

## Why this is asymmetric within the same PR

The same PR establishes that upstream topology (paths, key names) is sensitive to non-admin members and redacts it on every other surface:

- `handleVaultContext` (handle_vaults.go:102-105) clears both `summary.Config` *and* `summary.LastSyncError` for non-admin/non-owner callers.
- `recordFailure` at `internal/infisical/sync.go` has an explicit carve-out for `ErrInvalidKey` that persists the verbatim message into `last_sync_error` — but the persistence path is then redacted on read by `handleVaultContext`, so the leak is plugged on that surface.
- The matching success path of the new sync endpoint (handle_vaults.go:175-178) applies the same role check.

The ErrInvalidKey *error* branch of the same sync endpoint is the one surface that doesn't apply the redaction. So a non-admin vault member who triggers `/sync` reads the offending key name straight through the 400 response body, even though the identical content is masked when read through `/v1/vaults/{name}/context`.

## Who can reach this

`requireVaultAccess` (server.go:446-480, the gate this handler uses) admits any vault accessor: member-role grants, proxy-role grants, and scoped sessions matching the vault. So the leak audience is exactly the non-admin/non-owner cohort the existing redaction was designed to exclude.

## Step-by-step proof

1. Operator (owner) creates an Infisical-backed vault `demo` and adds vault member Eve with `role=member`.
2. Upstream Infisical project gains a secret with a non-conforming key, e.g. `stripe-prod-key` (kebab-case violates `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`).
3. Eve sends `POST /v1/vaults/demo/sync`. `requireVaultAccess` admits her (vault member).
4. `RefreshOnce` calls into the syncer; `FetchSecrets` → `EncryptSecrets` returns `ErrInvalidKey` wrapped with the key name.
5. The error-branch `case errors.Is(err, infisical.ErrInvalidKey)` fires at handle_vaults.go:153-154 with no role check, returning:

   ```json
   {"code":"external_store_invalid_key","error":"infisical: upstream secret key does not match required pattern: \"stripe-prod-key\" (Agent Vault requires UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; rename the secret upstream)"}
   ```

6. Concurrently, `recordFailure` persists the same string into `vault_credential_stores.last_sync_error`. Eve immediately loads the Settings tab; `handleVaultContext` runs, sees `vaultRole != "admin" && !actor.IsOwner()` is true, redacts `LastSyncError` to empty string. The web surface shows nothing — but Eve already has the value from step 5.

## Impact

The leaked datum is an upstream key name (Infisical topology), not the secret value itself. Vault members can already see successfully-synced key names through `/v1/credentials`, so the marginal disclosure is "upstream keys that *fail validation* (and therefore never appear in /v1/credentials)." That's a thin leak — hence **nit** — but the PR's own redaction logic established the standard that such topology is sensitive to non-admin members, and the fix is local and obvious.

## How to fix

Mirror the role check used at lines 175-178. The actor is already in scope at line 123:

```go
case errors.Is(err, infisical.ErrInvalidKey):
    vaultRole, _ := s.store.GetVaultRole(ctx, actor.ID, vault.ID)
    if vaultRole == "admin" || actor.IsOwner() {
        jsonCodedError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "external_store_invalid_key", err.Error())
    } else {
        s.logger.Warn("manual infisical sync rejected invalid upstream key",
            slog.String("vault_id", vault.ID),
            slog.String("err", err.Error()))
        jsonCodedError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "external_store_invalid_key",
            "Sync failed: upstream key shape invalid (see server logs).")
    }
```

A small regression test seeding a member-role session against an external vault with an invalid upstream key, then asserting the response body does not contain the key name, would lock the behavior in.

</details>

🟡 CLI is missing a `vault credential-store sync` subcommand to match the new HTTP endpoint (POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync, handle_vaults.go:113-180) and the Web UI's Manual sync button (CredentialsTab.tsx:56-75) — `vaultCredentialStoreCmd` at cmd/vaults.go:460 registers only `show`. Asymmetric with every other vault operation (create/list/delete/rename/use/current/user add/remove all have CLI subcommands) and with the Web UI; CLI operators have to drop to curl for a feature this PR otherwise wires to three surfaces. Pure UX gap — no security or functional impact, but the asymmetry was introduced atomically by the manual-sync commit (cd1ed4c) and the fix is ~30 lines mirroring `vaultCredentialStoreShowCmd`.

<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

## What the gap is

This PR's manual-sync feature lands three surfaces atomically in commit cd1ed4c:

1. **HTTP endpoint**: `POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync` at `internal/server/handle_vaults.go:113-180`, registered at `server.go:746`.
2. **Web UI**: A `Manual sync` button in `web/src/pages/vault/CredentialsTab.tsx` (`handleSyncNow` at lines 56-75, rendered in the `InfoBanner` action at line 272-282).
3. **HTTP skill docs**: A new bullet in `cmd/skill_http.md:157` enumerating the endpoint, its 409 in-flight error, and the post-refresh response shape.

The matching CLI subcommand is absent. `cmd/vaults.go:460` registers only `vaultCredentialStoreShowCmd` under the parent `vaultCredentialStoreCmd`:

```go
vaultCredentialStoreCmd.AddCommand(vaultCredentialStoreShowCmd)
vaultCmd.AddCommand(vaultCredentialStoreCmd)
```

A grep across `cmd/` for a sync subcommand returns nothing — no `vaultCredentialStoreSyncCmd` exists.

## Why the asymmetry matters

Every other vault operation in this CLI has a subcommand: `create`, `list`, `delete`, `rename`, `use`, `current`, and the entire `user` subtree (`user add`, `user list`, `user remove`, `user set-role`). The parent `credential-store` subcommand was added in this same PR with only one child — `show` — and the natural sibling (`sync`) is missing. The same pattern is visible on the Web UI side: `SettingsTab.tsx` shows read-only credential-store info while `CredentialsTab.tsx` provides the actual sync action button. The CLI has the `show` half but not the action half.

## Addressing the refutation

The refutation correctly notes that the original bug report's central quote — "Refresh on demand with POST {AGENT_VAULT_ADDR}/v1/vaults/{name}/sync" on `cmd/skill_cli.md:200` — is **not in the current file state**. I verified: line 200 of `skill_cli.md` falls after the "Creating an external-store vault" sentence and before "### Creating a Proposal"; there is no manual-sync mention in `skill_cli.md` at all. The PR diff text from the original commit was apparently revised in a later commit.

But this strengthens rather than weakens the case. The CLI-facing skill doc has **zero references** to manual sync (`grep -c 'sync' cmd/skill_cli.md` returns only matches for `create/sync fails with external_store_invalid_key`), so a CLI operator following the skill has no documented path to the manual-refresh endpoint at all — not even the "resort to curl" punt the original bug described. The skill simply doesn't surface the feature on the CLI side.

The refutation's stronger argument is that the omission from BOTH the CLI surface AND the CLI-facing skill doc reads as a deliberate design choice — manual sync is web/HTTP-only, the periodic syncer (60s default) handles the steady state, and rare "I just rotated upstream" cases are interactive. That's a coherent design position, and it's why this is filed as **nit** rather than blocking. But two points push back:

1. The skill_http.md section explicitly documents the endpoint, including its 409 in-flight error and 502/503 paths — so the endpoint is being marketed as part of the operator-facing surface, just not via the CLI. That's the asymmetry.
2. Every other vault management operation in this PR maintains CLI/HTTP/Web parity; manual sync is the lone wire-only operator entry point.

## Step-by-step proof of the gap

1. `cmd/vaults.go:460-461` — only `AddCommand(vaultCredentialStoreShowCmd)` is called under `vaultCredentialStoreCmd`.
2. `grep -rn 'Sync' cmd/vaults.go` returns only references to status text in the `show` subcommand output ("Last sync", "Synced at", "Last attempt") — no `SyncCmd` declaration.
3. `internal/server/handle_vaults.go:113-180` defines `handleVaultSyncNow` and `server.go:746` registers `POST /v1/vaults/{name}/sync` (any vault member).
4. `web/src/pages/vault/CredentialsTab.tsx:56-75` defines `handleSyncNow` that POSTs to that endpoint; the button is rendered at line 272-282.
5. A CLI operator looking to force a refresh has no command. `agent-vault vault credential-store --help` lists only `show`. They must either open the Web UI or run a raw curl against the endpoint with their session token.

## Impact and fix

Severity: **nit**. No security impact (the endpoint exists and works for any authenticated client), no correctness impact, no data impact. Pure UX gap during operator workflows that legitimately need manual sync (post-rotation, post-outage, after creating a new vault and wanting confirmation that the periodic loop is working).

Fix is ~30 lines mirroring `vaultCredentialStoreShowCmd`:

```go
var vaultCredentialStoreSyncCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:   "sync <name>",
    Short: "Force an immediate refresh of an external-store vault",
    Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
    RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
        name := args[0]
        sess, err := ensureSession()
        if err != nil { return err }
        url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/v1/vaults/%s/sync", sess.Address, name)
        respBody, err := doAdminRequestWithBody("POST", url, sess.Token, nil)
        if err != nil { return err }
        // Render the post-refresh credential_store summary, same shape as show.
        ...
    },
}
```

Then `vaultCredentialStoreCmd.AddCommand(vaultCredentialStoreSyncCmd)` alongside the existing `show` registration. A matching entry in `docs/reference/cli.mdx` and a bullet in `cmd/skill_cli.md` close the documentation half. Cheapest to land now while the credential-store CLI surface is still being shaped.

</details>

Guarding with `if services[i].Port == ""` before the split would make the intention explicit and prevent accidental regression.

**Body silently dropped when placeholder is absent or body is multipart** `ApplyBodySubstitutions` always drains `outReq.Body` via `io.ReadAll` whenever `len(bodySubs) > 0`, but the caller only replaces `outReq.Body` when `modified == true`. For any request where body substitutions are declared but the placeholder doesn't appear in the body (or the content-type is `multipart/*`), the original `bytes.NewReader` is left fully consumed, so `RoundTrip` forwards a zero-byte body to the upstream — silently dropping the real payload. Concrete failure: a service configured with `"in": ["body"]` receives a POST whose body happens not to contain the placeholder (e.g., a health-check probe, or a second endpoint on the same host that doesn't do the substitution). The upstream sees an empty body and likely returns a 400 or 500. The same applies to all `multipart/form-data` uploads, which are explicitly skipped by `ApplyBodySubstitutions` (returns `modified=false` with a fresh reader), but then `outReq.Body` is never refreshed. ```suggestion // ApplyBodySubstitutions always drains outReq.Body and returns a // fresh reader. Always update the body so the upstream receives the // original bytes even when no placeholder was found. outReq.Body = newBody if modified { outReq.ContentLength = newLen outReq.Header.Set("Content-Length", fmt.Sprintf("%d", newLen)) } ```

**WebSocket value substitution does not JSON-encode the replacement** `strings.ReplaceAll` replaces the placeholder with the raw credential value. If the value contains JSON special characters — `"`, `\`, or control characters — the resulting frame will be malformed JSON. Discord bot tokens are Base64URL-encoded so they are safe today, but any operator who uses the `websocket` surface for a credential whose value can contain those characters (e.g. a password, an API key with a quote, a JWT) will silently produce invalid JSON that Discord or any other downstream service will reject. The body substitution surface handles this correctly via `jsonEscapeString`; the same encoding should be offered here, or at minimum be documented as a known limitation. Real-world tokens (Discord, API keys) are base64/hex and don't contain JSON-special chars. This is documented in the skill docs.

**Medium: Unbounded substitution expansion**

A proxy-authenticated agent can send a `MaxProxyBodyBytes` request body made mostly of a short placeholder, and each `ReplaceAll` expands it to the credential length with no final size cap. Enforce a maximum substituted body size before allocating/writing the replacement; the WebSocket path has the same input-only cap at `internal/mitm/websocket.go` when building the modified frame.

Not a real concern. The agent is already authenticated with a proxy token — if it wanted to waste server memory it could just send a 64MB body without any placeholders. The substitution doesn't create a new attack surface. Input is already capped at 64MB by `MaxProxyBodyBytes`.

**`check()` inserts a nil map entry for every new key** `recent := l.attempts[key][:0]` re-slices the nil zero-value for keys that have never been seen, and then `l.attempts[key] = recent` writes nil back into the map — adding the key with no timestamp. Every successful CONNECT or forward-proxy request from a new remote IP creates a nil entry in `attempts`, incrementing `len(l.attempts)` and potentially triggering eviction on every call. The nil entries are immediately evictable (`len(v) == 0`), so correctness is preserved, but in a workload with many new IPs making only successful connections, `check()` will insert-then-evict on every call once `maxKeys` is reached. A guard like `if l.attempts[key] != nil { l.attempts[key] = recent }` would avoid the unnecessary write, or a comment clarifying the intentional mutation would help future readers.

**`Check`/`Allow` TOCTOU allows bursts of concurrent auth failures to pass the pre-gate** `Check()` and `recordAuthFailure()` are not atomic. When multiple goroutines arrive concurrently with budget `N` remaining, all can pass `Check()` before any records an event via `Allow()`. The sliding-window mutex serializes the `Allow()` calls and caps how many events are recorded, but all concurrent requests still reach `ParseProxyAuth` and potentially `ResolveForProxy` before the budget is reflected. An attacker with `k >> N` parallel connections can force `k` session lookups in one burst where previously only `N` would have been served. This is an inherent trade-off in the check-then-act pattern and aligns with the PR's goal of not blocking legitimate agents — a comment in `recordAuthFailure` acknowledging this would help future maintainers.

The burst is bounded by concurrent goroutines in the narrow window, and `ResolveForProxy` is a cheap SQLite lookup. Changing the default response cap to `0` lets an authenticated agent keep MITM proxy slots tied up indefinitely by requesting a large or streaming response from an approved upstream. Keep a finite default and allow operators to opt into unlimited responses only when they need it.

@@ -0,0 +1,651 @@
+---
+title: "Run OpenClaw on a VPS"
+description: "Keep real credentials off the agent host by routing every outbound call through Agent Vault on a separate VPS."
+---
+
+Provision two DigitalOcean droplets, install Agent Vault on one and [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) on the other, and broker every outbound call through Agent Vault. Plan for 45–60 minutes and ~$12/month.
+
+By the end, you'll have:
+
+1. **Agent Vault running on one droplet**, holding real Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack credentials encrypted at rest behind a master password.
+2. **An OpenClaw gateway running on a second droplet**, reachable via a Slack bot, with every outbound API call brokered through Agent Vault and revocable from the UI in one click.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A [DigitalOcean](https://cloud.digitalocean.com) account.
+- API keys for the services you want OpenClaw to call. This guide uses Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack.
+- A Slack workspace where you can install a custom app.
+
+<Note>
+This guide installs Agent Vault as a native binary via the install script, the path documented in [Self-hosting locally](/self-hosting/local). For containers, see [Docker self-hosting](/self-hosting/docker).
+</Note>
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
++-----------------------------------------------------------------+
+| Public internet                                                 |
+|                                                                 |
+|   api.anthropic.com   api.github.com                            |
+|   api.notion.com      slack.com                                 |
+|          ^                   ^                                  |
++----------+-------------------+----------------------------------+
+           |                   |
+           +-------------------+
+                               | outbound HTTPS, Agent Vault
+                               | injects real credentials here
++------------------------------+----------------------------------+
+| Private VPC (10.108.0.0/20, region-scoped)                      |
+|                              |                                  |
+|  +---------------------------+----+     +--------------------+  |
+|  | av-broker  10.108.0.3          |     | openclaw-box       |  |
+|  | Agent Vault server             |<----| 10.108.0.2         |  |
+|  | :14321  control UI / API       |     | OpenClaw gateway   |  |
+|  | :14322  MITM proxy             |     | (placeholders)     |  |
+|  | (real credentials, encrypted)  |     |                    |  |
+|  +----------------^---------------+     +--------------------+  |
+|                   |                                             |
++-------------------+---------------------------------------------+
+                    | SSH + tunnel for AV UI from laptop
+                    |
+                Operator
+```
+
+Only `av-broker` holds real credentials, encrypted at rest behind your master password. `openclaw-box` holds placeholder strings (`__anthropic_api_key__`, etc.) and one revocable [agent token](/agents/overview).
+
+## 1. Provision the VPS boxes
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Generate an SSH key on your laptop">
+
+```bash
+ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -C "digital-ocean-1"
+```
+
+Every `ssh` command in this guide uses `-i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1` to pin to this key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Upload the public key to DigitalOcean">
+
+In the DigitalOcean console: **Settings → Security → SSH Keys → Add SSH Key.** Paste the contents of `~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1.pub`, name it (e.g. `digital-ocean-1`), and save.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the VPC">
+
+**Networking → VPC → Create VPC Network.** Pick any region. Both droplets must use the same region. Default IP range is fine.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create av-broker">
+
+**Create → Droplets.** Set:
+
+| Panel | Setting |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Region** | Same region as the VPC |
+| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 (LTS) |
+| **Droplet type** | Basic, Regular ($6/mo, 1GB / 1vCPU is plenty for Agent Vault) |
+| **VPC Network** | The VPC you just created |
+| **Authentication** | SSH Key, tick `digital-ocean-1` |
+| **Hostname** | `av-broker` |
+
+Click **Create Droplet**.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create openclaw-box">
+
+Repeat the previous step with one change:
+
+- **Hostname:** `openclaw-box`
+
+Same region, VPC, and SSH key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Note the private IPs">
+
+Click each droplet, then **Networking**. Note the private IPv4 each got from the VPC range. The rest of this guide assumes:
+
+- `av-broker` is `10.108.0.3`
+- `openclaw-box` is `10.108.0.2`
+
+Substitute yours into every later command.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify private connectivity">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+ping -c 3 10.108.0.2
+```
+
+Three replies confirm the VPC is live. Type `exit` to disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 2. Restrict SSH and broker ports with a cloud firewall
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Find your laptop's public IPv4">
+
+```bash
+curl -4 ifconfig.me; echo
+```
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create and attach the firewall">
+
+**Networking → Firewalls → Create Firewall**, name it `openclaw-lab`. Add three inbound rules:
+
+| Type | Port | Sources |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| TCP | `22` | Your laptop's public IPv4 |
+| TCP | `14321` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+| TCP | `14322` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+
+Leave outbound rules empty (DigitalOcean allows all outbound by default).
+
+Scroll to **Apply to Droplets** and tick both `av-broker` and `openclaw-box`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Warning>
+If your laptop's public IP changes (cafe networks, VPNs), update the firewall rule's source IP for port 22.
+</Warning>
+
+## 3. Install Agent Vault on av-broker
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="SSH into av-broker">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+```
+
+Every command in this section runs on `av-broker` until you exit.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install Agent Vault">
+
+```bash
+curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.agent-vault.dev | sh
+```
+
+The script detects your architecture, verifies the signed release, and drops the binary at `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install tmux">
+
+```bash
+apt update && apt install -y tmux
+```
+
+You'll run Agent Vault inside a `tmux` session so it survives your SSH disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Launch the server inside tmux">
+
+```bash
+tmux new -s av
+agent-vault server --host 10.108.0.3 --port 14321 --mitm-port 14322
+```
+
+`--host 10.108.0.3` binds both listeners to the private NIC, keeping Agent Vault unreachable from the public internet.
+
+First-run prompts: master password, admin email, admin password.
+
+Detach with `Ctrl-B` then `D`. You'll see `[detached from session av]` and drop back to your normal shell. The server keeps running inside the tmux session.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify the server">
+
+```bash
+curl -sI http://10.108.0.3:14321/health
+```
+
+Expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Note>
+On reboot, tmux dies and so does the server. SSH back in, `tmux new -s av`, restart with the same command, re-enter the master password. For zero-touch restart, set [`AGENT_VAULT_MASTER_PASSWORD`](/self-hosting/environment-variables), but note the password then lives in an env file.
+</Note>
+
+## 4. Configure the vault
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Open an SSH tunnel">
+
+In a **new terminal on your laptop** (don't reuse the one you used to install Agent Vault):
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -L 14321:10.108.0.3:14321 root@<av-broker-public-ip> -N
+```
+
+The terminal hangs silently. That's correct. **Leave it running for the rest of the guide.** Closing it stops the tunnel and the AV UI goes dark.
+
+Open `http://localhost:14321` in your laptop's browser and sign in with the admin email and password you set during install.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Understand vaults, credentials, and services">
+
+You'll create one of each. Briefly:
+
+- A [**vault**](/learn/vaults) is a named isolation boundary. We'll create `prod`.
+- A [**credential**](/learn/credentials) is one secret value stored under a name (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-...`). Encrypted at rest.
+- A [**service**](/learn/services) is the wiring for one upstream host: host pattern + auth mode + substitution rules that reference credentials by name.
+
+Credentials store values. Services define wiring. At request time, Agent Vault matches the service by host, looks up the named credential, and rewrites the wire bytes before forwarding.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the prod vault">
+
+**Vaults → New vault → `prod` → Create.**
+
+![Agent Vault UI showing the prod vault](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-create-vault.png)
body: Three image references in this guide still point to the `hermes-on-vps` folder rather than the `openclaw-on-vps` folder. As written, users will see Hermes screenshots — wrong UI context — when following the OpenClaw guide. The same copy-paste issue occurs at line 478 (`hermes-on-vps-agents-add.png`) and line 490 (`hermes-on-vps-agent-modal-2.png`). ```suggestion ![Agent Vault UI showing the prod vault](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-create-vault.png) ```

+---
+title: "Run OpenClaw on a VPS"
+description: "Keep real credentials off the agent host by routing every outbound call through Agent Vault on a separate VPS."

+
+Provision two DigitalOcean droplets, install Agent Vault on one and [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) on the other, and broker every outbound call through Agent Vault. Plan for 45–60 minutes and ~$12/month.

+## Prerequisites

+- A [DigitalOcean](https://cloud.digitalocean.com) account.

+<Note>

+```

+|                                                                 |
+|   api.anthropic.com   api.github.com                            |
+|   api.notion.com      slack.com                                 |
