@@ -0,0 +1,651 @@
+---
+title: "Run OpenClaw on a VPS"
+description: "Keep real credentials off the agent host by routing every outbound call through Agent Vault on a separate VPS."
+---
+
+Provision two DigitalOcean droplets, install Agent Vault on one and [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) on the other, and broker every outbound call through Agent Vault. Plan for 45–60 minutes and ~$12/month.
+
+By the end, you'll have:
+
+1. **Agent Vault running on one droplet**, holding real Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack credentials encrypted at rest behind a master password.
+2. **An OpenClaw gateway running on a second droplet**, reachable via a Slack bot, with every outbound API call brokered through Agent Vault and revocable from the UI in one click.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A [DigitalOcean](https://cloud.digitalocean.com) account.
+- API keys for the services you want OpenClaw to call. This guide uses Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack.
+- A Slack workspace where you can install a custom app.
+
+<Note>
+This guide installs Agent Vault as a native binary via the install script, the path documented in [Self-hosting locally](/self-hosting/local). For containers, see [Docker self-hosting](/self-hosting/docker).
+</Note>
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
++-----------------------------------------------------------------+
+| Public internet                                                 |
+|                                                                 |
+|   api.anthropic.com   api.github.com                            |
+|   api.notion.com      slack.com                                 |
+|          ^                   ^                                  |
++----------+-------------------+----------------------------------+
+           |                   |
+           +-------------------+
+                               | outbound HTTPS, Agent Vault
+                               | injects real credentials here
++------------------------------+----------------------------------+
+| Private VPC (10.108.0.0/20, region-scoped)                      |
+|                              |                                  |
+|  +---------------------------+----+     +--------------------+  |
+|  | av-broker  10.108.0.3          |     | openclaw-box       |  |
+|  | Agent Vault server             |<----| 10.108.0.2         |  |
+|  | :14321  control UI / API       |     | OpenClaw gateway   |  |
+|  | :14322  MITM proxy             |     | (placeholders)     |  |
+|  | (real credentials, encrypted)  |     |                    |  |
+|  +----------------^---------------+     +--------------------+  |
+|                   |                                             |
++-------------------+---------------------------------------------+
+                    | SSH + tunnel for AV UI from laptop
+                    |
+                Operator
+```
+
+Only `av-broker` holds real credentials, encrypted at rest behind your master password. `openclaw-box` holds placeholder strings (`__anthropic_api_key__`, etc.) and one revocable [agent token](/agents/overview).
+
+## 1. Provision the VPS boxes
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Generate an SSH key on your laptop">
+
+```bash
+ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -C "digital-ocean-1"
+```
+
+Every `ssh` command in this guide uses `-i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1` to pin to this key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Upload the public key to DigitalOcean">
+
+In the DigitalOcean console: **Settings → Security → SSH Keys → Add SSH Key.** Paste the contents of `~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1.pub`, name it (e.g. `digital-ocean-1`), and save.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the VPC">
+
+**Networking → VPC → Create VPC Network.** Pick any region. Both droplets must use the same region. Default IP range is fine.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create av-broker">
+
+**Create → Droplets.** Set:
+
+| Panel | Setting |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Region** | Same region as the VPC |
+| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 (LTS) |
+| **Droplet type** | Basic, Regular ($6/mo, 1GB / 1vCPU is plenty for Agent Vault) |
+| **VPC Network** | The VPC you just created |
+| **Authentication** | SSH Key, tick `digital-ocean-1` |
+| **Hostname** | `av-broker` |
+
+Click **Create Droplet**.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create openclaw-box">
+
+Repeat the previous step with one change:
+
+- **Hostname:** `openclaw-box`
+
+Same region, VPC, and SSH key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Note the private IPs">
+
+Click each droplet, then **Networking**. Note the private IPv4 each got from the VPC range. The rest of this guide assumes:
+
+- `av-broker` is `10.108.0.3`
+- `openclaw-box` is `10.108.0.2`
+
+Substitute yours into every later command.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify private connectivity">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+ping -c 3 10.108.0.2
+```
+
+Three replies confirm the VPC is live. Type `exit` to disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 2. Restrict SSH and broker ports with a cloud firewall
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Find your laptop's public IPv4">
+
+```bash
+curl -4 ifconfig.me; echo
+```
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create and attach the firewall">
+
+**Networking → Firewalls → Create Firewall**, name it `openclaw-lab`. Add three inbound rules:
+
+| Type | Port | Sources |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| TCP | `22` | Your laptop's public IPv4 |
+| TCP | `14321` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+| TCP | `14322` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+
+Leave outbound rules empty (DigitalOcean allows all outbound by default).
+
+Scroll to **Apply to Droplets** and tick both `av-broker` and `openclaw-box`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Warning>
+If your laptop's public IP changes (cafe networks, VPNs), update the firewall rule's source IP for port 22.
+</Warning>
+
+## 3. Install Agent Vault on av-broker
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="SSH into av-broker">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+```
+
+Every command in this section runs on `av-broker` until you exit.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install Agent Vault">
+
+```bash
+curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.agent-vault.dev | sh
+```
+
+The script detects your architecture, verifies the signed release, and drops the binary at `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install tmux">
+
+```bash
+apt update && apt install -y tmux
+```
+
+You'll run Agent Vault inside a `tmux` session so it survives your SSH disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Launch the server inside tmux">
+
+```bash
+tmux new -s av
+agent-vault server --host 10.108.0.3 --port 14321 --mitm-port 14322
+```
+
+`--host 10.108.0.3` binds both listeners to the private NIC, keeping Agent Vault unreachable from the public internet.
+
+First-run prompts: master password, admin email, admin password.
+
+Detach with `Ctrl-B` then `D`. You'll see `[detached from session av]` and drop back to your normal shell. The server keeps running inside the tmux session.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify the server">
+
+```bash
+curl -sI http://10.108.0.3:14321/health
+```
+
+Expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Note>
+On reboot, tmux dies and so does the server. SSH back in, `tmux new -s av`, restart with the same command, re-enter the master password. For zero-touch restart, set [`AGENT_VAULT_MASTER_PASSWORD`](/self-hosting/environment-variables), but note the password then lives in an env file.
+</Note>
+
+## 4. Configure the vault
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Open an SSH tunnel">
+
+In a **new terminal on your laptop** (don't reuse the one you used to install Agent Vault):
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -L 14321:10.108.0.3:14321 root@<av-broker-public-ip> -N
+```
+
+The terminal hangs silently. That's correct. **Leave it running for the rest of the guide.** Closing it stops the tunnel and the AV UI goes dark.
+
+Open `http://localhost:14321` in your laptop's browser and sign in with the admin email and password you set during install.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Understand vaults, credentials, and services">
+
+You'll create one of each. Briefly:
+
+- A [**vault**](/learn/vaults) is a named isolation boundary. We'll create `prod`.
+- A [**credential**](/learn/credentials) is one secret value stored under a name (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-...`). Encrypted at rest.
+- A [**service**](/learn/services) is the wiring for one upstream host: host pattern + auth mode + substitution rules that reference credentials by name.
+
+Credentials store values. Services define wiring. At request time, Agent Vault matches the service by host, looks up the named credential, and rewrites the wire bytes before forwarding.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the prod vault">
+
+**Vaults → New vault → `prod` → Create.**
+
+![Agent Vault UI showing the prod vault](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-create-vault.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Add credentials">
+
+In the `prod` vault, **Credentials tab → Add credential.** Add real tokens for Anthropic, GitHub, and Notion now; the two Slack tokens are placeholders you'll fill in the next section.
+
+| Key | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key (`sk-ant-...`) |
+| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub PAT with `repo` scope (`ghp_...`) |
+| `NOTION_TOKEN` | Notion internal integration token (`ntn_...`) |
+| `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Placeholder; you create the Slack app in the next section |
+| `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` | Placeholder; you create the Slack app in the next section |
+
+![Credentials tab in the prod vault with the five credentials added](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-credentials.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Add services">
+
+**Services tab → + Add service.** For each row below: fill **Name** and **Host**, set **Authentication** to the value in the **Auth** column. For Bearer rows, fill the **Token (credential key)** field with the credential name (e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN`) and skip the substitutions section. For Passthrough rows, scroll to **URL Substitutions**, click **+ Add substitution**, paste the placeholder, tick the surface boxes listed, select the credential. Save.
+
+| Name | Host | Auth | Credential / Placeholder | Surface |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `anthropic` | `api.anthropic.com` | Passthrough | `__anthropic_api_key__` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `header` |
+| `github` | `api.github.com` | Bearer | Token key: `GITHUB_TOKEN` | n/a |
+| `notion` | `api.notion.com` | Bearer | Token key: `NOTION_TOKEN` | n/a |
+| `slack` | `slack.com/*` | Passthrough | `__slack_bot_token__` → `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | `header, body` |
+
+![Anthropic service in Agent Vault with the Passthrough auth and URL substitution rule](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-service-anthropic.png)
+
+![GitHub service in Agent Vault with Bearer auth and the GITHUB_TOKEN credential key](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-service-github.png)
+
+The `slack` service carries a second substitution on the same service for the app token. After saving the first rule, click **+ Add substitution** again on the same service:
+
+| Placeholder | Surface | Credential |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `__slack_app_token__` | `header, body` | `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` |
+
+Two auth modes appear above (Bearer for `github`/`notion`, Passthrough + substitution for `anthropic`/`slack`); see [Services](/learn/services) for how each one works and when to pick it.
+
+<Note>
+Slack ticks both `header` and `body` surfaces because `@slack/web-api` puts the bot token in the request body on its method-arg shape (`client.auth.test({token})`). Without `body` ticked, Bolt's `auth.test` validation fails at boot and the bot silently stops responding to mentions.
+</Note>
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Warning>
+**For passthrough+substitution services, placeholder strings are exact-match.** If Anthropic or Slack returns 401, check the failing request's **Credential keys** field in the AV UI's **Logs** tab; an empty value means the substitution didn't fire (typo in the placeholder is the usual cause). Bearer services don't have this concern: Agent Vault rewrites the Authorization header regardless of what the client sent.
+</Warning>
+
+## 5. Install OpenClaw on openclaw-box
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="SSH into openclaw-box and install the Agent Vault CLI">
+
+In a **fresh terminal on your laptop** (leave the SSH tunnel to `av-broker` running):
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<openclaw-box-public-ip>
+curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.agent-vault.dev | sh
+```
+
+On this box the Agent Vault CLI is a client wrapper; no server runs here.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install OpenClaw and walk the setup wizard">
+
+```bash
+curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
+```
+
+The installer drops OpenClaw at `/usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw` and launches its interactive setup wizard. At every token prompt, type the placeholder, not the real value. Exact strings matter; copy from this guide.
+
+1. **Personal data acknowledgement** → **I understand**.
+
+![Personal data acknowledgement prompt](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-personal.png)
+
+2. **Setup mode** → **Quickstart**.
+
+![Quickstart setup mode selection](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-quickstart.png)
+
+3. **Model provider** → **Anthropic**.
+
+![Model provider list with Anthropic selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-provider.png)
+
+4. **Anthropic auth method** → **Anthropic API Key**.
+
+![Anthropic auth method with Anthropic API Key selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-auth-method.png)
+
+5. **Anthropic API key** → `__anthropic_api_key__`.
+
+![Anthropic API key prompt with the placeholder entered](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-anthropic-key.png)
+
+6. **Model** → pick your preferred Claude model.
+
+![Claude model picker](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-model.png)
+
+7. **Messaging platform** → **Slack (Socket Mode)**. The wizard then prints a `Slack manifest JSON` block; copy it for the next section.
+
+![Messaging platform list with Slack (Socket Mode) selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-messaging.png)
+
+![Slack manifest JSON block ready to copy](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-manifest.png)
+
+<Note>
+If you miss the manifest or re-run the wizard, it skips that step. Run `openclaw channels remove slack` then re-run the wizard to see it again.
+</Note>
+
+8. **Slack Bot Token** → `__slack_bot_token__`.
+
+![Slack bot token prompt with the placeholder entered](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-bot-token.png)
+
+9. **Slack App Token** → `__slack_app_token__`.
+
+![Slack app token prompt with the placeholder entered](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-app-token.png)
+
+10. **Configure channel access?** → **Yes**.
+
+![Configure Slack channel access prompt set to Yes](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-channels-configure.png)
+
+11. **Channel access** → **Open**.
+
+![Slack channel access set to Open](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-channels-open.png)
+
+12. **Search provider** → **Skip**.
+
+![Search provider prompt with Skip selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-search.png)
+
+13. **Skills** → **No** (skip).
+
+![Skills configuration prompt with No selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-skills.png)
+
+14. **Hooks** → **Skip for now**.
+
+![Hooks prompt with Skip for now selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-hooks.png)
+
+15. **Hatch agent in terminal?** → **No** (hatch later).
+
+![Hatch agent in terminal prompt with hatch-later selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-hatch.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Sanity-check the placeholders landed">
+
+```bash
+grep -R "__anthropic_api_key__\|__slack_bot_token__\|__slack_app_token__" ~/.openclaw
+```
+
+You should see hits in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (Slack tokens) and `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json` (Anthropic). If any are missing or mistyped, re-run the wizard.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 6. Create the Slack app from OpenClaw's manifest
+
+OpenClaw's manifest pre-configures every scope, event, and feature its Slack plugin needs. Pasting it into Slack's "Create from manifest" flow provisions the app in one shot.
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Create the app in Slack from the manifest">
+
+Go to [api.slack.com/apps](https://api.slack.com/apps), click **Create New App → From a manifest**, pick your workspace, paste the JSON, and click **Create**.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install to your workspace and copy the bot token">
+
+In the new app's sidebar: **OAuth & Permissions → Install to Workspace**. Approve the scopes. Copy the **Bot User OAuth Token** (`xoxb-...`).
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Generate the App-Level Token">
+
+The manifest doesn't cover App-Level Tokens. **Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate Token and Scopes**, name it, add the `connections:write` scope, **Generate**, copy the `xapp-...` token.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Paste the real tokens into Agent Vault">
+
+In the AV UI: `prod` → **Credentials** → `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` → edit → paste the `xoxb-...` token → save. Then `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` → edit → paste the `xapp-...` token → save.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Invite the bot to your channel">
+
+In Slack, open the channel you want OpenClaw to listen in. Type `/invite @<your-bot-name>`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 7. Connect openclaw-box to Agent Vault
+
+`agent-vault run` wraps OpenClaw's gateway so every outbound call goes through `av-broker`.
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Mint an agent token">
+
+Switch to the AV UI tab in your laptop browser. Sidebar: **All Agents → Add agent.**
+
+![All Agents tab with the Add agent button highlighted](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-agents-add.png)
+
+In the modal:
+
+- **Agent name:** `openclaw-box`
+- **Vault access:** click **+ Add vault**, pick `prod`, leave role at `proxy`
+- Click **Add**
+
+![Add Agent modal with openclaw-box name and prod vault assignment](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-agent-modal.png)
+
+The modal flips to the **Connect Your Agent** view with three values you'll need: `AGENT_VAULT_ADDR`, `AGENT_VAULT_TOKEN` (the `av_agt_...` value), and `AGENT_VAULT_VAULT`. Copy all three. The address shown may point at `localhost` or your laptop's tunnel; in the env file below you'll substitute `av-broker`'s private VPC IP (e.g. `http://10.108.0.3:14321`) because `openclaw-box` reaches Agent Vault over the private network, not through your laptop's SSH tunnel.
+
+![Connect Your Agent modal with the three-line export snippet](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-agent-modal-2.png)

+5. **Anthropic API key** → `__anthropic_api_key__`.
+
+![Anthropic API key prompt with the placeholder entered](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-anthropic-key.png)
+
+6. **Model** → pick your preferred Claude model.
+
+![Claude model picker](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-model.png)
+
+7. **Messaging platform** → **Slack (Socket Mode)**. The wizard then prints a `Slack manifest JSON` block; copy it for the next section.
+
+![Messaging platform list with Slack (Socket Mode) selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-messaging.png)
+
+![Slack manifest JSON block ready to copy](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-manifest.png)
+
+<Note>
+If you miss the manifest or re-run the wizard, it skips that step. Run `openclaw channels remove slack` then re-run the wizard to see it again.
+</Note>
+
+8. **Slack Bot Token** → `__slack_bot_token__`.
+
+![Slack bot token prompt with the placeholder entered](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-bot-token.png)
+
+9. **Slack App Token** → `__slack_app_token__`.
+
+![Slack app token prompt with the placeholder entered](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-app-token.png)
+
+10. **Configure channel access?** → **Yes**.
+
+![Configure Slack channel access prompt set to Yes](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-channels-configure.png)
+
+11. **Channel access** → **Open**.
+
+![Slack channel access set to Open](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-channels-open.png)
+
+12. **Search provider** → **Skip**.
+
+![Search provider prompt with Skip selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-search.png)
+
+13. **Skills** → **No** (skip).
+
+![Skills configuration prompt with No selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-skills.png)
+
+14. **Hooks** → **Skip for now**.
+
+![Hooks prompt with Skip for now selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-hooks.png)
+
+15. **Hatch agent in terminal?** → **No** (hatch later).
+
+![Hatch agent in terminal prompt with hatch-later selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-hatch.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Sanity-check the placeholders landed">
+
+```bash
+grep -R "__anthropic_api_key__\|__slack_bot_token__\|__slack_app_token__" ~/.openclaw
+```
+
+You should see hits in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (Slack tokens) and `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json` (Anthropic). If any are missing or mistyped, re-run the wizard.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 6. Create the Slack app from OpenClaw's manifest
+
+OpenClaw's manifest pre-configures every scope, event, and feature its Slack plugin needs. Pasting it into Slack's "Create from manifest" flow provisions the app in one shot.
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Create the app in Slack from the manifest">
+
+Go to [api.slack.com/apps](https://api.slack.com/apps), click **Create New App → From a manifest**, pick your workspace, paste the JSON, and click **Create**.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install to your workspace and copy the bot token">
+
+In the new app's sidebar: **OAuth & Permissions → Install to Workspace**. Approve the scopes. Copy the **Bot User OAuth Token** (`xoxb-...`).
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Generate the App-Level Token">
+
+The manifest doesn't cover App-Level Tokens. **Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate Token and Scopes**, name it, add the `connections:write` scope, **Generate**, copy the `xapp-...` token.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Paste the real tokens into Agent Vault">
+
+In the AV UI: `prod` → **Credentials** → `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` → edit → paste the `xoxb-...` token → save. Then `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` → edit → paste the `xapp-...` token → save.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Invite the bot to your channel">
+
+In Slack, open the channel you want OpenClaw to listen in. Type `/invite @<your-bot-name>`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 7. Connect openclaw-box to Agent Vault
+
+`agent-vault run` wraps OpenClaw's gateway so every outbound call goes through `av-broker`.
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Mint an agent token">
+
+Switch to the AV UI tab in your laptop browser. Sidebar: **All Agents → Add agent.**
+
+![All Agents tab with the Add agent button highlighted](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-agents-add.png)

@@ -0,0 +1,651 @@
+---
+title: "Run OpenClaw on a VPS"
+description: "Keep real credentials off the agent host by routing every outbound call through Agent Vault on a separate VPS."
+---
+
+Provision two DigitalOcean droplets, install Agent Vault on one and [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) on the other, and broker every outbound call through Agent Vault. Plan for 45–60 minutes and ~$12/month.
+
+By the end, you'll have:
+
+1. **Agent Vault running on one droplet**, holding real Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack credentials encrypted at rest behind a master password.
+2. **An OpenClaw gateway running on a second droplet**, reachable via a Slack bot, with every outbound API call brokered through Agent Vault and revocable from the UI in one click.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A [DigitalOcean](https://cloud.digitalocean.com) account.
+- API keys for the services you want OpenClaw to call. This guide uses Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack.
+- A Slack workspace where you can install a custom app.
+
+<Note>
+This guide installs Agent Vault as a native binary via the install script, the path documented in [Self-hosting locally](/self-hosting/local). For containers, see [Docker self-hosting](/self-hosting/docker).
+</Note>
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
++-----------------------------------------------------------------+
+| Public internet                                                 |
+|                                                                 |
+|   api.anthropic.com   api.github.com                            |
+|   api.notion.com      slack.com                                 |
+|          ^                   ^                                  |
++----------+-------------------+----------------------------------+
+           |                   |
+           +-------------------+
+                               | outbound HTTPS, Agent Vault
+                               | injects real credentials here
++------------------------------+----------------------------------+
+| Private VPC (10.108.0.0/20, region-scoped)                      |
+|                              |                                  |
+|  +---------------------------+----+     +--------------------+  |
+|  | av-broker  10.108.0.3          |     | openclaw-box       |  |
+|  | Agent Vault server             |<----| 10.108.0.2         |  |
+|  | :14321  control UI / API       |     | OpenClaw gateway   |  |
+|  | :14322  MITM proxy             |     | (placeholders)     |  |
+|  | (real credentials, encrypted)  |     |                    |  |
+|  +----------------^---------------+     +--------------------+  |
+|                   |                                             |
++-------------------+---------------------------------------------+
+                    | SSH + tunnel for AV UI from laptop
+                    |
+                Operator
+```
+
+Only `av-broker` holds real credentials, encrypted at rest behind your master password. `openclaw-box` holds placeholder strings (`__anthropic_api_key__`, etc.) and one revocable [agent token](/agents/overview).
+
+## 1. Provision the VPS boxes
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Generate an SSH key on your laptop">
+
+```bash
+ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -C "digital-ocean-1"
+```
+
+Every `ssh` command in this guide uses `-i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1` to pin to this key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Upload the public key to DigitalOcean">
+
+In the DigitalOcean console: **Settings → Security → SSH Keys → Add SSH Key.** Paste the contents of `~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1.pub`, name it (e.g. `digital-ocean-1`), and save.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the VPC">
+
+**Networking → VPC → Create VPC Network.** Pick any region. Both droplets must use the same region. Default IP range is fine.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create av-broker">
+
+**Create → Droplets.** Set:
+
+| Panel | Setting |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Region** | Same region as the VPC |
+| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 (LTS) |
+| **Droplet type** | Basic, Regular ($6/mo, 1GB / 1vCPU is plenty for Agent Vault) |
+| **VPC Network** | The VPC you just created |
+| **Authentication** | SSH Key, tick `digital-ocean-1` |
+| **Hostname** | `av-broker` |
+
+Click **Create Droplet**.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create openclaw-box">
+
+Repeat the previous step with one change:
+
+- **Hostname:** `openclaw-box`
+
+Same region, VPC, and SSH key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Note the private IPs">
+
+Click each droplet, then **Networking**. Note the private IPv4 each got from the VPC range. The rest of this guide assumes:
+
+- `av-broker` is `10.108.0.3`
+- `openclaw-box` is `10.108.0.2`
+
+Substitute yours into every later command.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify private connectivity">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+ping -c 3 10.108.0.2
+```
+
+Three replies confirm the VPC is live. Type `exit` to disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 2. Restrict SSH and broker ports with a cloud firewall
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Find your laptop's public IPv4">
+
+```bash
+curl -4 ifconfig.me; echo
+```
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create and attach the firewall">
+
+**Networking → Firewalls → Create Firewall**, name it `openclaw-lab`. Add three inbound rules:
+
+| Type | Port | Sources |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| TCP | `22` | Your laptop's public IPv4 |
+| TCP | `14321` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+| TCP | `14322` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+
+Leave outbound rules empty (DigitalOcean allows all outbound by default).
+
+Scroll to **Apply to Droplets** and tick both `av-broker` and `openclaw-box`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Warning>
+If your laptop's public IP changes (cafe networks, VPNs), update the firewall rule's source IP for port 22.
+</Warning>
+
+## 3. Install Agent Vault on av-broker
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="SSH into av-broker">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+```
+
+Every command in this section runs on `av-broker` until you exit.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install Agent Vault">
+
+```bash
+curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.agent-vault.dev | sh
+```
+
+The script detects your architecture, verifies the signed release, and drops the binary at `/usr/local/bin/agent-vault`.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install tmux">
+
+```bash
+apt update && apt install -y tmux
+```
+
+You'll run Agent Vault inside a `tmux` session so it survives your SSH disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Launch the server inside tmux">
+
+```bash
+tmux new -s av
+agent-vault server --host 10.108.0.3 --port 14321 --mitm-port 14322
+```
+
+`--host 10.108.0.3` binds both listeners to the private NIC, keeping Agent Vault unreachable from the public internet.
+
+First-run prompts: master password, admin email, admin password.
+
+Detach with `Ctrl-B` then `D`. You'll see `[detached from session av]` and drop back to your normal shell. The server keeps running inside the tmux session.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify the server">
+
+```bash
+curl -sI http://10.108.0.3:14321/health
+```
+
+Expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Note>
+On reboot, tmux dies and so does the server. SSH back in, `tmux new -s av`, restart with the same command, re-enter the master password. For zero-touch restart, set [`AGENT_VAULT_MASTER_PASSWORD`](/self-hosting/environment-variables), but note the password then lives in an env file.
+</Note>
+
+## 4. Configure the vault
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Open an SSH tunnel">
+
+In a **new terminal on your laptop** (don't reuse the one you used to install Agent Vault):
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -L 14321:10.108.0.3:14321 root@<av-broker-public-ip> -N
+```
+
+The terminal hangs silently. That's correct. **Leave it running for the rest of the guide.** Closing it stops the tunnel and the AV UI goes dark.
+
+Open `http://localhost:14321` in your laptop's browser and sign in with the admin email and password you set during install.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Understand vaults, credentials, and services">
+
+You'll create one of each. Briefly:
+
+- A [**vault**](/learn/vaults) is a named isolation boundary. We'll create `prod`.
+- A [**credential**](/learn/credentials) is one secret value stored under a name (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-...`). Encrypted at rest.
+- A [**service**](/learn/services) is the wiring for one upstream host: host pattern + auth mode + substitution rules that reference credentials by name.
+
+Credentials store values. Services define wiring. At request time, Agent Vault matches the service by host, looks up the named credential, and rewrites the wire bytes before forwarding.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the prod vault">
+
+**Vaults → New vault → `prod` → Create.**
+
+![Agent Vault UI showing the prod vault](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-create-vault.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Add credentials">
+
+In the `prod` vault, **Credentials tab → Add credential.** Add real tokens for Anthropic, GitHub, and Notion now; the two Slack tokens are placeholders you'll fill in the next section.
+
+| Key | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key (`sk-ant-...`) |
+| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub PAT with `repo` scope (`ghp_...`) |
+| `NOTION_TOKEN` | Notion internal integration token (`ntn_...`) |
+| `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Placeholder; you create the Slack app in the next section |
+| `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` | Placeholder; you create the Slack app in the next section |
+
+![Credentials tab in the prod vault with the five credentials added](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-credentials.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Add services">
+
+**Services tab → + Add service.** For each row below: fill **Name** and **Host**, set **Authentication** to the value in the **Auth** column. For Bearer rows, fill the **Token (credential key)** field with the credential name (e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN`) and skip the substitutions section. For Passthrough rows, scroll to **URL Substitutions**, click **+ Add substitution**, paste the placeholder, tick the surface boxes listed, select the credential. Save.
+
+| Name | Host | Auth | Credential / Placeholder | Surface |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `anthropic` | `api.anthropic.com` | Passthrough | `__anthropic_api_key__` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `header` |
+| `github` | `api.github.com` | Bearer | Token key: `GITHUB_TOKEN` | n/a |
+| `notion` | `api.notion.com` | Bearer | Token key: `NOTION_TOKEN` | n/a |
+| `slack` | `slack.com/*` | Passthrough | `__slack_bot_token__` → `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | `header, body` |
+
+![Anthropic service in Agent Vault with the Passthrough auth and URL substitution rule](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-service-anthropic.png)
+
+![GitHub service in Agent Vault with Bearer auth and the GITHUB_TOKEN credential key](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-service-github.png)
+
+The `slack` service carries a second substitution on the same service for the app token. After saving the first rule, click **+ Add substitution** again on the same service:
+
+| Placeholder | Surface | Credential |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `__slack_app_token__` | `header, body` | `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` |
+
+Two auth modes appear above (Bearer for `github`/`notion`, Passthrough + substitution for `anthropic`/`slack`); see [Services](/learn/services) for how each one works and when to pick it.
+
+<Note>
+Slack ticks both `header` and `body` surfaces because `@slack/web-api` puts the bot token in the request body on its method-arg shape (`client.auth.test({token})`). Without `body` ticked, Bolt's `auth.test` validation fails at boot and the bot silently stops responding to mentions.
+</Note>
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Warning>
+**For passthrough+substitution services, placeholder strings are exact-match.** If Anthropic or Slack returns 401, check the failing request's **Credential keys** field in the AV UI's **Logs** tab; an empty value means the substitution didn't fire (typo in the placeholder is the usual cause). Bearer services don't have this concern: Agent Vault rewrites the Authorization header regardless of what the client sent.
+</Warning>

+
+13. **Skills** → **No** (skip).
+
+![Skills configuration prompt with No selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-skills.png)
+
+14. **Hooks** → **Skip for now**.
+
+![Hooks prompt with Skip for now selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-hooks.png)
+
+15. **Hatch agent in terminal?** → **No** (hatch later).
+
+![Hatch agent in terminal prompt with hatch-later selected](/images/openclaw-on-vps/openclaw-on-vps-wizard-hatch.png)
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Sanity-check the placeholders landed">
+
+```bash
+grep -R "__anthropic_api_key__\|__slack_bot_token__\|__slack_app_token__" ~/.openclaw

+You should see hits in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (Slack tokens) and `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/auth-profiles.json` (Anthropic). If any are missing or mistyped, re-run the wizard.
+
+</Step>

+## 6. Create the Slack app from OpenClaw's manifest

+OpenClaw's manifest pre-configures every scope, event, and feature its Slack plugin needs. Pasting it into Slack's "Create from manifest" flow provisions the app in one shot.

+

+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install to your workspace and copy the bot token">
+
+In the new app's sidebar: **OAuth & Permissions → Install to Workspace**. Approve the scopes. Copy the **Bot User OAuth Token** (`xoxb-...`).
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Generate the App-Level Token">
+
+The manifest doesn't cover App-Level Tokens. **Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → Generate Token and Scopes**, name it, add the `connections:write` scope, **Generate**, copy the `xapp-...` token.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Paste the real tokens into Agent Vault">
+
+In the AV UI: `prod` → **Credentials** → `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` → edit → paste the `xoxb-...` token → save. Then `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` → edit → paste the `xapp-...` token → save.

+In the modal:

+---
+title: "Run OpenClaw on a VPS"
+description: "Keep real credentials off the agent host by routing every outbound call through Agent Vault on a separate VPS."
+---
+
+Provision two DigitalOcean droplets, install Agent Vault on one and [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) on the other, and broker every outbound call through Agent Vault. Plan for 45–60 minutes and ~$12/month.
+
+By the end, you'll have:
+
+1. **Agent Vault running on one droplet**, holding real Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack credentials encrypted at rest behind a master password.
+2. **An OpenClaw gateway running on a second droplet**, reachable via a Slack bot, with every outbound API call brokered through Agent Vault and revocable from the UI in one click.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A [DigitalOcean](https://cloud.digitalocean.com) account.
+- API keys for the services you want OpenClaw to call. This guide uses Anthropic, GitHub, Notion, and Slack.
+- A Slack workspace where you can install a custom app.
+
+<Note>
+This guide installs Agent Vault as a native binary via the install script, the path documented in [Self-hosting locally](/self-hosting/local). For containers, see [Docker self-hosting](/self-hosting/docker).
+</Note>
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
++-----------------------------------------------------------------+
+| Public internet                                                 |
+|                                                                 |
+|   api.anthropic.com   api.github.com                            |
+|   api.notion.com      slack.com                                 |
+|          ^                   ^                                  |
++----------+-------------------+----------------------------------+
+           |                   |
+           +-------------------+
+                               | outbound HTTPS, Agent Vault
+                               | injects real credentials here
++------------------------------+----------------------------------+
+| Private VPC (10.108.0.0/20, region-scoped)                      |
+|                              |                                  |
+|  +---------------------------+----+     +--------------------+  |
+|  | av-broker  10.108.0.3          |     | openclaw-box       |  |
+|  | Agent Vault server             |<----| 10.108.0.2         |  |
+|  | :14321  control UI / API       |     | OpenClaw gateway   |  |
+|  | :14322  MITM proxy             |     | (placeholders)     |  |
+|  | (real credentials, encrypted)  |     |                    |  |
+|  +----------------^---------------+     +--------------------+  |
+|                   |                                             |
++-------------------+---------------------------------------------+
+                    | SSH + tunnel for AV UI from laptop
+                    |
+                Operator
+```
+
+Only `av-broker` holds real credentials, encrypted at rest behind your master password. `openclaw-box` holds placeholder strings (`__anthropic_api_key__`, etc.) and one revocable [agent token](/agents/overview).
+
+## 1. Provision the VPS boxes
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Generate an SSH key on your laptop">
+
+```bash
+ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -C "digital-ocean-1"
+```
+
+Every `ssh` command in this guide uses `-i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1` to pin to this key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Upload the public key to DigitalOcean">
+
+In the DigitalOcean console: **Settings → Security → SSH Keys → Add SSH Key.** Paste the contents of `~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1.pub`, name it (e.g. `digital-ocean-1`), and save.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the VPC">
+
+**Networking → VPC → Create VPC Network.** Pick any region. Both droplets must use the same region. Default IP range is fine.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create av-broker">
+
+**Create → Droplets.** Set:
+
+| Panel | Setting |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Region** | Same region as the VPC |
+| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 (LTS) |
+| **Droplet type** | Basic, Regular ($6/mo, 1GB / 1vCPU is plenty for Agent Vault) |
+| **VPC Network** | The VPC you just created |
+| **Authentication** | SSH Key, tick `digital-ocean-1` |
+| **Hostname** | `av-broker` |
+
+Click **Create Droplet**.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create openclaw-box">
+
+Repeat the previous step with one change:
+
+- **Hostname:** `openclaw-box`
+
+Same region, VPC, and SSH key.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Note the private IPs">
+
+Click each droplet, then **Networking**. Note the private IPv4 each got from the VPC range. The rest of this guide assumes:
+
+- `av-broker` is `10.108.0.3`
+- `openclaw-box` is `10.108.0.2`
+
+Substitute yours into every later command.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify private connectivity">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+ping -c 3 10.108.0.2
+```
+
+Three replies confirm the VPC is live. Type `exit` to disconnect.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+## 2. Restrict SSH and broker ports with a cloud firewall
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Find your laptop's public IPv4">
+
+```bash

+```
+
+</Step>
+

+

+

+| --- | --- | --- |
+| TCP | `22` | Your laptop's public IPv4 |
+| TCP | `14321` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+| TCP | `14322` | `openclaw-box` private IP (`10.108.0.2`) |
+
+Leave outbound rules empty (DigitalOcean allows all outbound by default).
+
+Scroll to **Apply to Droplets** and tick both `av-broker` and `openclaw-box`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+
+<Warning>

+</Warning>
+

+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="SSH into av-broker">
+
+From your laptop:
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 root@<av-broker-public-ip>
+```
+
+Every command in this section runs on `av-broker` until you exit.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install Agent Vault">
+

+curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://get.agent-vault.dev | sh
+```

+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Install tmux">

+apt update && apt install -y tmux
+```

+```

+`--host 10.108.0.3` binds both listeners to the private NIC, keeping Agent Vault unreachable from the public internet.
+
+First-run prompts: master password, admin email, admin password.
+
+Detach with `Ctrl-B` then `D`. You'll see `[detached from session av]` and drop back to your normal shell. The server keeps running inside the tmux session.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Verify the server">
+
+```bash
+curl -sI http://10.108.0.3:14321/health
+```
+
+Expect `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.
+
+</Step>
+
+</Steps>
+

+On reboot, tmux dies and so does the server. SSH back in, `tmux new -s av`, restart with the same command, re-enter the master password. For zero-touch restart, set [`AGENT_VAULT_MASTER_PASSWORD`](/self-hosting/environment-variables), but note the password then lives in an env file.
+</Note>
+
+## 4. Configure the vault
+
+<Steps>
+
+<Step title="Open an SSH tunnel">
+
+In a **new terminal on your laptop** (don't reuse the one you used to install Agent Vault):
+
+```bash
+ssh -i ~/.ssh/digital-ocean-1 -L 14321:10.108.0.3:14321 root@<av-broker-public-ip> -N
+```
+
+The terminal hangs silently. That's correct. **Leave it running for the rest of the guide.** Closing it stops the tunnel and the AV UI goes dark.
+
+Open `http://localhost:14321` in your laptop's browser and sign in with the admin email and password you set during install.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Understand vaults, credentials, and services">
+
+You'll create one of each. Briefly:
+
+- A [**vault**](/learn/vaults) is a named isolation boundary. We'll create `prod`.
+- A [**credential**](/learn/credentials) is one secret value stored under a name (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-...`). Encrypted at rest.
+- A [**service**](/learn/services) is the wiring for one upstream host: host pattern + auth mode + substitution rules that reference credentials by name.
+
+Credentials store values. Services define wiring. At request time, Agent Vault matches the service by host, looks up the named credential, and rewrites the wire bytes before forwarding.
+
+</Step>
+
+<Step title="Create the prod vault">
+
+**Vaults → New vault → `prod` → Create.**
+
+![Agent Vault UI showing the prod vault](/images/hermes-on-vps/hermes-on-vps-create-vault.png)

**Medium: Server-side request to untrusted token URL**

`cfg.TokenURL` is ultimately supplied through OAuth credential configuration, but the token client uses a normal transport with no public-network/HTTPS restriction. A vault member can set `token_url` to an internal URL and trigger `/v1/credentials/oauth/tokens`, the OAuth callback, or automatic refresh to make the server POST to that internal service; validate token URLs and use the same outbound network guard used for proxied upstream dials before sending the request.

The dedicated `tokenClient` explicitly sets `Proxy: nil`, bypassing any proxy-level SSRF protection, so the server will make direct TCP connections to whatever URL an authenticated admin supplies — including `http://169.254.169.254/` or other internal endpoints. The token upload path at lines 291-301 is one example; the same raw value flows to `oauth.Refresh()` in `handleOAuthTokenUpload` and later to `maybeRefreshOAuth` during every hot-path injection. **Medium: Plain HTTP OAuth endpoints accepted**

A proxy-role agent can submit an OAuth proposal with `oauth.token_url` or `authorization_url` set to `http://...`; if a vault member approves and connects or uploads a refresh token, Agent Vault sends the authorization code, refresh token, and client secret over plaintext HTTP. `tokenURL` can come from this request, but an empty `client_secret` falls back to the existing encrypted secret; a vault member can POST a new `token_url` they control with any `refresh_token`, and Agent Vault will send the stored client secret to that endpoint during validation. Only reuse preserved OAuth secrets when the provider configuration is unchanged and the caller explicitly asks to keep them, and clear or require new secrets when `token_url`/`client_id` changes; apply the same rule to preserved refresh tokens in the OAuth config upsert.

When an OAuth proposal updates `token_url` for an existing credential, this upsert leaves the existing refresh token in place and preserves the client secret via the `COALESCE` assignments below. A compromised agent can submit a proposal for an existing OAuth key with an attacker-controlled token endpoint; after approval, automatic refresh sends the stored refresh token and client secret to that endpoint. Clear the stored client secret, refresh token, expiry, and connected state unless the existing provider configuration matches the proposed one.

body:
**High: OAuth refresh token redirection**

A vault member editing an existing OAuth credential can change `token_url` to a server they control while this upsert preserves the old `refresh_token_ct`; the next automatic refresh will POST that stored refresh token to the new endpoint. Clear the refresh token, nonce, expiry, and connection state when `excluded.token_url` differs from the existing `credential_oauth.token_url`, matching the safer proposal-apply logic.

body: fixed, same CASE WHEN guard applied to SetCredentialOAuth. refresh token, expiry, and connection state all clear when token_url changes

**`INSERT OR IGNORE` silently discards static credential on OAuth key collision** `ReplaceVaultCredentials` deletes only `type='static'` rows first, so an existing OAuth credential with the same key survives. The subsequent `INSERT OR IGNORE` then silently no-ops because of the `(vault_id, key)` unique constraint, leaving the OAuth row in place with its original ciphertext — the caller's new static value is lost with no error. The correct fix is to use `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET type = 'static', ciphertext = excluded.ciphertext, nonce = excluded.nonce, updated_at = excluded.updated_at` so the static value actually wins. ```suggestion stmt, err := tx.PrepareContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO credentials (id, vault_id, key, type, ciphertext, nonce, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'static', ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(vault_id, key) DO UPDATE SET type = 'static', ciphertext = excluded.ciphertext, nonce = excluded.nonce, updated_at = excluded.updated_at`) ```

intentional — the syncer manages static credentials from an external source, OAuth credentials are set up manually by an admin. if both have the same key, the admin's OAuth setup should win, not get silently overwritten by the syncer

+func RegisterGORMMigration(version int, name string, fn func(db *gorm.DB) error) {
+	gormMigMu.Lock()
+	defer gormMigMu.Unlock()
+	gormMigrations = append(gormMigrations, GORMMigration{Version: version, Name: name, Fn: fn})
+}
+
+// maxGORMVersion returns the highest registered GORM migration version.
+func maxGORMVersion() int {
+	max := 0

+		if m.Version > max {

+		}
+	}
+	return max

+	if len(gormMigrations) == 0 {
+		return nil
+	}
+

+	// to prevent concurrent migration runs across pods.

+		ctx := context.Background()

+		}

+			return fmt.Errorf("acquiring migration lock: %w", err)
+		}

+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("unknown dialect for GORM: %s", dialectName)
+	}
+
+	gormDB, err := gorm.Open(dialector, &gorm.Config{
+		DisableAutomaticPing: true,
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("initializing gorm for migrations: %w", err)

body:
**Medium: Incomplete destination emptiness check**

An unauthenticated attacker can register the first owner account on an accidentally exposed empty Postgres destination before migration, and this check still passes because it only rejects vaults beyond the seeded default. Check for any existing user data as well (at least users, sessions, vault_grants, credentials, proposals, invites, and CA/master-key rows beyond the expected baseline), ideally under the same migration lock/transaction used for the copy, before proceeding.

**SSRF via HTTP redirect following** `fetch` follows redirects by default (up to 20 hops in Node.js). If the server at `EXAMPLE_API_BASE_URL` returns a `3xx` redirect pointing to an internal host (e.g., cloud metadata at `169.254.169.254`), `fetch` will silently follow it and return that response into the AI context. Because the path is AI-chosen (and Slack users can influence the prompt), a redirecting endpoint combined with certain paths could expose data from otherwise-unreachable internal services. Adding `redirect: "error"` limits every request to the operator-configured host. ```suggestion const response = await fetch(url, { method: "GET", redirect: "error", headers: { Accept: "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT, }, }); ```

**Base URL path is silently discarded when path starts with `/`** `new URL(absolutePath, base)` follows the URL standard: an absolute path (starting with `/`) replaces the entire path of the base URL. So `EXAMPLE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com/v1` with path `/items` resolves to `https://api.example.com/items`, not `https://api.example.com/v1/items`. The test at line 62 actually asserts this discarding behavior. Users who set a base URL with a path prefix (e.g. `/v1`, `/api`) will get silently wrong URLs with no error.

**Thread transcript has no length cap before AI ingestion** The code fetches up to 200 thread messages and joins them into a single string, then passes the full transcript to `runAgent` without any truncation. On long threads this can produce an extremely large prompt, potentially exceeding the model's context window (causing a silent truncation or API error) or generating a disproportionately expensive call. Adding a character or message-count cap on the transcript before appending `userMessage` would bound the worst case.

A user following only this page would see: stop instances → run `master-password change` → ... → restart, and could skip updating the secret store entirely, causing every instance to fail to start with "wrong password." The original `postgres.mdx` text made this explicit: *"update the value in your secret store"* was enumerated as a distinct step between changing the password and restarting instances. Consider adding that step to the note or to the `master-password change` accordion description so the full rotation procedure is self-contained on this page.

**Dismiss endpoints use member access instead of admin** The PR description explicitly states "Both controls are admin-only, matching existing `Add as service` visibility," and the UI correctly gates both dismiss buttons behind `isAdmin`. However, both new DELETE handlers call `requireVaultMember` instead of `requireVaultAdmin`. Any vault member — not just an admin — can call `DELETE /v1/vaults/{name}/discovered-hosts/{host}` or `DELETE /v1/vaults/{name}/discovered-hosts` directly via the API, silently bypassing the intended access control.

**Arbitrary host strings are stored without validation or a size cap** `handleDismissDiscoveredHost` stores any host string from the URL path directly into vault settings without checking that the host actually exists in the discovered-hosts list. A vault member can dismiss thousands of fabricated host strings, causing the `dismissed_discovered_hosts` setting to grow unboundedly. Validating against the live discovered-host set (or capping the list) before persisting would prevent this. ```suggestion const maxDismissed = 1000 dismissed := loadDismissedHosts(ctx, s.store, ns.ID) if !dismissed[host] && len(dismissed) >= maxDismissed { jsonError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "Dismissed hosts limit reached") return } dismissed[host] = true if err := saveDismissedHosts(ctx, s.store, ns.ID, dismissed); err != nil { ```

**`dismissed` count in dismiss-all response includes previously dismissed hosts** `len(dismissed)` reflects the total map size after merging all previously dismissed entries plus the newly dismissed ones, so the response value is misleading for API consumers who expect it to reflect how many hosts were dismissed in this call. ```suggestion jsonOK(w, map[string]any{"dismissed": len(unmatched)}) ```

**Silent error swallowing leaves the user with no feedback on failure** Both `dismissDiscoveredHost` and `dismissAllDiscoveredHosts` catch all errors and discard them. If the server returns a 500 or the network drops, the UI state and the server state will diverge: the host will remain in the server's discovered list but the user sees no indication that anything went wrong.

**Logging omits the requesting user's identity** The warn log for a failed dismiss save records `vault` and `err` but not the actor/user who made the request, making it harder to correlate incidents in cloud log services. The team's logging convention expects something like `"user", actor.Username` or the `[username=…]` format to appear on mutation-path log lines. **Rule Used:** Follow a specific logging pattern for easier query... **Race condition in last-admin guard** The `CountVaultAdmins` read and `RevokeVaultAccess` write are not atomic. If two admin-level users simultaneously call this endpoint, both can observe `adminCount == 2`, both pass the guard, and both have their grants removed — leaving the vault with zero admins and no way to recover without direct database access. The same window exists in `handleVaultMemberDelete`, but this endpoint widens the attack surface because any member can trigger it on themselves (no admin privilege required to call). The fix is to wrap the count-check and revoke in a single database transaction, or expose a `RevokeLastNotAdmin` store primitive that enforces the constraint atomically.

**Swallowed store errors return misleading 4xx responses** Both `GetVaultRole` and `CountVaultAdmins` errors are silently discarded. Both failures are conservative (deny rather than allow), but a transient DB error will look like a permanent logical rejection to the caller, hiding the real problem from both users and operators.

+func EnabledFromEnv() bool {
+	b, err := strconv.ParseBool(os.Getenv("AGENT_VAULT_METRICS_ENABLED"))

+// ProposalCounter is the subset of store.Store that the proposals gauge
+// needs. Declared here instead of importing internal/store to keep this
+// package's dependency surface minimal; store.Store satisfies it structurally.
+type ProposalCounter interface {
+	CountProposalsByStatus(ctx context.Context) (map[string]int, error)

+// Metrics owns a dedicated Prometheus registry (never the global default
+// registry) so that constructing multiple instances — e.g. once per test —
+// never collides on duplicate registration.
+type Metrics struct {
+	registry *prometheus.Registry
+
+	proxyRequestsTotal   *prometheus.CounterVec
+	proxyRequestDuration *prometheus.HistogramVec

+
+// New creates a Metrics instance with the proxy collectors registered. If
+// proposals is non-nil, a live proposals-by-status gauge is also registered,
+// queried directly from the store on every scrape rather than tracked via
+// incremented counters — so it can never drift regardless of which code
+// path transitioned a proposal's status.
+func New(proposals ProposalCounter) *Metrics {
+	reg := prometheus.NewRegistry()
+
+	m := &Metrics{
+		registry: reg,
+		proxyRequestsTotal: prometheus.NewCounterVec(prometheus.CounterOpts{
+			Name: "agent_vault_proxy_requests_total",
+			Help: "Total proxied requests, labeled by matched service name and response status code.",
+		}, []string{"service", "status"}),
+		proxyRequestDuration: prometheus.NewHistogramVec(prometheus.HistogramOpts{

+			Help:    "Latency of proxied requests in seconds, labeled by matched service name.",
+			Buckets: prometheus.DefBuckets,
+		}, []string{"service"}),

+// Handler returns an http.Handler serving this Metrics instance's registry

body:
**Critical: OAuth token exfiltration through header substitution**

An authenticated agent can send `Referer: __GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN__` to `maps.googleapis.com`. Header substitution replaces every occurrence in every outbound header—not only `Authorization`—and Google documents that Maps APIs generally include rejected referrers in error responses, which this proxy returns to the agent. This exposes the raw access token. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/maps/api-security-best-practices?utm_source=openai))

Model this preset as bearer authentication so the broker constructs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or introduce a substitution mechanism constrained to a specific header name.

**Invite state leaks before authorization** When an unrelated authenticated member submits predictable invitation IDs, this handler returns distinct 404 and 409 responses before calling `canManageUserInvite`, exposing which invitations exist and whether they remain pending; the reinvite handler has the same ordering. Move the authorization boundary ahead of these distinguishable state responses. **How this was verified:** Both handlers test ID existence and pending status before invoking the invitation-management authorization check.

**First attempt exhausts fallback timeout** When the first resolved address remains pending until the dialer's 10-second timeout, it consumes the entire shared 10-second context, causing the function to return `context.DeadlineExceeded` without trying a later reachable address.

The shared 10-second deadline allows a hanging first address to consume the complete fallback budget. I’ll allocate each attempt a share of the remaining total deadline, while preserving the caller’s earlier deadline and the overall 10-second cap. I’ll also add a deterministic regression test where the first address blocks until its per-attempt deadline and the second address succeeds. I will fix it.

Fixed in `c0d5b84`. Each address attempt now receives `remaining total time / remaining addresses`, recomputed before every dial. Prompt failures leave unused time for later addresses, a per-attempt deadline continues fallback while the parent context is still live, and caller cancellation or the overall deadline still stops immediately.

Added deterministic coverage where the first address blocks until its per-attempt deadline and the second succeeds, plus earlier-caller-deadline coverage. Verification passed:

- timeout regression tests: 50 consecutive runs
- `go test -race ./internal/netguard`
- full `make test` in a clean, read-only Go 1.25 container

Thanks for catching this.

+package server
+
+import (
+	"database/sql"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+	"unicode/utf8"
+
+	"github.com/Infisical/agent-vault/internal/broker"
+	"github.com/Infisical/agent-vault/internal/store"
+)
+
+// A skill is a named markdown instruction document scoped to one vault.
+// Reads are open to any vault grant (including `proxy`, so an agent's own
+// token can pull the skills it should be following); mutations are vault
+// admin only. Skills are deliberately outside the proposal system: agents
+// cannot propose skill changes, so nothing here touches internal/proposal.
+//
+// Bodies are stored in plaintext, unlike credentials.
+
+const (
+	// maxSkillDescriptionChars matches the Agent Skills frontmatter limit for
+	// a skill's `description` field, so a skill authored here stays valid when
+	// `vault run` writes it out as SKILL.md. Mirrored as
+	// MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS in web/src/pages/vault/SkillsTab.tsx.
+	//
+	// The companion `name` limit from that spec (64 characters) is already
+	// enforced by broker.ValidateSlug, which is also stricter about the
+	// charset because the name becomes a directory name on disk.
+	maxSkillDescriptionChars = 1024
+	// maxSkillContentChars caps the markdown body, counted in characters
+	// (runes) rather than bytes so the limit means the same thing to the
+	// author as it does here — the dashboard shows this exact number. Also
+	// bounds the payload: at UTF-8's worst case of 4 bytes per rune this is
+	// 400 KB, comfortably under limitBody's 1 MB ceiling, so an oversized
+	// paste gets a precise error instead of a generic decode failure.
+	// Mirrored as MAX_CONTENT_CHARS in web/src/pages/vault/SkillsTab.tsx —
+	// update both together.
+	maxSkillContentChars = 100_000
+)
+
+// skillResponse is the wire shape for a single skill. Content is omitted
+// from list responses so the payload stays small regardless of body size.
+type skillResponse struct {
+	Name        string    `json:"name"`
+	Description string    `json:"description"`
+	Content     string    `json:"content,omitempty"`
+	CreatedAt   time.Time `json:"created_at"`
+	UpdatedAt   time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
+}
+
+func skillToResponse(sk *store.Skill) skillResponse {
+	return skillResponse{
+		Name:        sk.Name,
+		Description: sk.Description,
+		Content:     sk.Content,
+		CreatedAt:   sk.CreatedAt,
+		UpdatedAt:   sk.UpdatedAt,
+	}
+}
+
+// normalizeSkillContent makes bodies stable across platforms: skills are
+// written to disk verbatim by `vault run`, so CRLF would leak into files.
+func normalizeSkillContent(content string) string {
+	return strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n")
+}
+
+// validateSkillPayload enforces the skill field rules. Names reuse
+// broker.ValidateSlug because a skill name becomes a directory name when
+// `vault run` writes the skill to an agent's filesystem.
+func validateSkillPayload(name, description, content string) error {
+	if err := broker.ValidateSlug(name); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if !utf8.ValidString(description) || !utf8.ValidString(content) {
+		return errors.New("description and content must be valid UTF-8")
+	}
+	// NUL bytes are a genuine dialect divergence: SQLite stores them in
+	// TEXT while Postgres rejects them outright, so without this check the
+	// same request succeeds on SQLite and 500s on Postgres. Name needs no
+	// check — ValidateSlug already restricts it to [a-z0-9-].
+	if strings.ContainsRune(description, 0) || strings.ContainsRune(content, 0) {
+		return errors.New("description and content must not contain NUL bytes")
+	}
+	// Counted in runes, not bytes, so a limit stated to the author in
+	// characters is the limit actually enforced regardless of script.
+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(description) > maxSkillDescriptionChars {
+		return fmt.Errorf("description must be at most %d characters", maxSkillDescriptionChars)
+	}
+	if strings.TrimSpace(content) == "" {
+		return errors.New("content is required")
+	}
+	if n := utf8.RuneCountInString(content); n > maxSkillContentChars {
+		return fmt.Errorf("content must be at most %d characters (got %d)", maxSkillContentChars, n)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// handleSkillsList returns the vault's skills without their markdown bodies.
+func (s *Server) handleSkillsList(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	ns := s.resolveVaultByPath(w, r)
+	if ns == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	name := ns.Name
+	if _, err := s.requireVaultAccess(w, r, ns.ID); err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+
+	metas, err := s.store.ListSkills(r.Context(), ns.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to list skills")
+		return
+	}
+
+	out := make([]skillResponse, 0, len(metas))
+	for _, m := range metas {
+		out = append(out, skillResponse{
+			Name:        m.Name,
+			Description: m.Description,
+			CreatedAt:   m.CreatedAt,
+			UpdatedAt:   m.UpdatedAt,
+		})
+	}
+	jsonOK(w, map[string]interface{}{"vault": name, "skills": out})
+}
+
+// handleSkillGet returns one skill including its markdown body.
+func (s *Server) handleSkillGet(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	ns := s.resolveVaultByPath(w, r)
+	if ns == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	name := ns.Name
+	if _, err := s.requireVaultAccess(w, r, ns.ID); err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+
+	skillName := r.PathValue("skill")
+	sk, err := s.store.GetSkill(r.Context(), ns.ID, skillName)
+	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusNotFound, fmt.Sprintf("Skill %q not found", skillName))
+		return
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to load skill")
+		return
+	}
+	jsonOK(w, map[string]interface{}{"vault": name, "skill": skillToResponse(sk)})
+}
+
+// handleSkillCreate adds a skill to the vault. Vault admin only.
+func (s *Server) handleSkillCreate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	ctx := r.Context()
+	ns := s.resolveVaultByPath(w, r)
+	if ns == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	name := ns.Name
+	actor, err := s.requireVaultAdmin(w, r, ns.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+
+	var req struct {
+		Name        string `json:"name"`
+		Description string `json:"description"`
+		Content     string `json:"content"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Invalid request body")
+		return
+	}
+
+	req.Name = strings.TrimSpace(req.Name)
+	req.Description = strings.TrimSpace(req.Description)
+	req.Content = normalizeSkillContent(req.Content)
+	if err := validateSkillPayload(req.Name, req.Description, req.Content); err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
+		return
+	}
+
+	// No vault lock needed: InsertSkill is a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
+	// DO NOTHING, and the (vault_id, name) primary key is the uniqueness
+	// guard. Only handleSkillPatch does a read-modify-write.
+	sk, err := s.store.InsertSkill(ctx, store.Skill{
+		VaultID:     ns.ID,
+		Name:        req.Name,
+		Description: req.Description,
+		Content:     req.Content,
+	})
+	if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSkillExists) {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusConflict, fmt.Sprintf("A skill named %q already exists", req.Name))
+		return
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "Failed to create skill")
+		return
+	}
+
+	s.captureEvent(r, "av.skill-add", actor, map[string]string{"vault": name})
+	jsonCreated(w, map[string]interface{}{"vault": name, "skill": skillToResponse(sk)})
+}
+
+// handleSkillPatch updates a skill's name, description, and/or body.
+// Vault admin only. Omitted fields are left as-is.
+func (s *Server) handleSkillPatch(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	ctx := r.Context()
+	ns := s.resolveVaultByPath(w, r)
+	if ns == nil {
+		return
+	}
+	name := ns.Name
+	actor, err := s.requireVaultAdmin(w, r, ns.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+
+	skillName := r.PathValue("skill")
+	var req struct {
+		Name        *string `json:"name"`
+		Description *string `json:"description"`
+		Content     *string `json:"content"`
+	}
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Invalid request body")
+		return
+	}
+	if req.Name == nil && req.Description == nil && req.Content == nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "At least one field is required (name, description, content)")
+		return
+	}
+
+	unlock, err := s.lockVault(ctx, ns.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "lock failed")
+		return
+	}
+	defer unlock()
body: **Advisory lock exhausts pool** If concurrent skill updates exhaust the bounded PostgreSQL pool, each request retains a pinned advisory-lock connection while `GetSkill` and `UpdateSkill` require another pooled connection, causing the lock holder and waiting updates to hang until their request contexts are cancelled. **Knowledge Base Used:** [Database storage and migrations](https://app.greptile.com/infisical/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/infisical/agent-vault/-/docs/database-storage-and-migrations.md)

**Flood Gate Is Bypassable** Any nonempty `Proxy-Authorization` value now selects its own rate-limit bucket before authentication. An unauthenticated client can vary a well-formed but invalid token on every CONNECT or forward request, preventing any bucket from reaching its limit. Each attempt can still perform a session-store lookup, while the peer-IP fallback applies only when the header is absent. This defeats the authentication-failure flood gate and permits resource-exhaustion attacks. > **How this was verified:** Distinct attacker-controlled header values produce distinct hashes, and both pre-authentication checks and failure accounting use those hashes before any global or per-peer limit applies. **Knowledge Base Used:** - [Secure traffic mediation](https://app.greptile.com/infisical/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/infisical/agent-vault/-/docs/secure-traffic-mediation.md) - [Broker and proxy data plane](https://app.greptile.com/infisical/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/infisical/agent-vault/-/docs/broker-and-proxy-data-plane.md)
